66	
67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
76	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
77	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
78	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
79	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
80	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
81	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
82	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
83	
84	Active series in this repo:
85	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
86	
87	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
88	
89	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
90	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
91	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
92	
93	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
94	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
95	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
96	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
97	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
98	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
99	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
100	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
101	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
102	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
103	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
104	
105	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
106	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
107	
108	## Marketplace Catalog
109	
110	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
111	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
112	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
113	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
114	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
115	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
116	for the full mechanism.
117	
118	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
119	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
120	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
121	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
122	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
123	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
124	
125	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
126	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
127	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
128	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
129	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
130	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
131	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
132	within-group caveat in
133	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
134	
135	## SKILL.md Format
136	
137	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
138	
139	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
140	
141	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
142	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
143	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
144	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
145	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
146	
147	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
148	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
149	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
150	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
151	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
152	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
153	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
154	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
155	
156	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
157	
158	```bash
159	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
160	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
161	
162	# …or remove them afterward
163	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
164	```
165	
166	## Project Memory Workflow
167	
168	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
169	
170	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
171	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
172	
173	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
174	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
175	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
176	
177	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
178	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
179	
180	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
181	
182	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
183	
184	   ```bash
185	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
186	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
187	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
188	   ```
189	
190	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
191	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
192	
193	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
194	
195	   ```bash
196	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
197	   ```
198	
199	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
200	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
201	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
202	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
203	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
204	
205	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
206	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
207	   afterwards to catch drift.
208	
209	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
210	
211	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
212	
213	```bash
214	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
215	```
216	
217	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
218	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
219	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
220	
221	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
222	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
223	
224	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
225	
226	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
227	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
228	own conventions). It has four subareas:
229	
230	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
231	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
232	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
233	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
234	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
235	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
236	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
237	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
238	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
239	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
240	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
241	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
242	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
243	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
244	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
245	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
246	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
247	  status / license / last_verified`).
248	
249	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
250	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
251	
252	| Status | Meaning |
253	|---|---|
254	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
255	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
256	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
257	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
258	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
259	
260	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
261	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
262	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
263	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
264	
265	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
266	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
267	
268	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
269	
270	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
271	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
272	
273	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
274	2. The root cause
275	3. The workaround
276	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
277	
278	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
279	the explanation they do not know yet.

206	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
207	
208	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
209	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
210	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
211	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
212	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
213	canonical).
214	
215	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
216	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
217	
218	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
219	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
220	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
221	> invent translations)."
222	
223	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
224	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
225	
226	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
227	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
228	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
229	user may want one without the other.
230	
231	## Available scripts
232	
233	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
234	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
235	  - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
236	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
237	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
238	  - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,
239	    `--no-workflow`, `--no-skeleton`, `--social`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
240	  - Always appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to `.gitignore`,
241	    idempotently.
242	  - `--social` opts into OG/Twitter cards: expands the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers in
243	    the templates with the blocks in `assets/social/`, and adds `/.cache/` to
244	    `.gitignore`. Off by default (keeps the scaffold Cairo/Pango-free).
245	- **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via
246	  `gh api`. Requires `gh auth status` to pass first.
247	  - Flags: `--repo OWNER/REPO`, `--no-trigger`, `--dry-run`.
248	- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page and insert it into
249	  `mkdocs.yml`'s nav. If multiple languages are configured, also writes
250	  `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.
251	  - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--lang LANG`
252	    (single-language stub only), `--dry-run`, `--force`.
253	- **`scripts/add-language.sh`** — Retrofit a non-default language into an
254	  existing site. Inserts `plugins.i18n`, creates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs with
255	  the terminology admonition, updates preferences, uncomments the static-i18n
256	  dep. Keeps `mkdocs-llmstxt` by default; auto-patches CI to drop `--strict`
257	  with `--drop-strict`. Idempotent.
258	  - Flags: `--lang LANG` (required), `--name NAME`, `--default-lang LANG`,
259	    `--target-dir DIR`, `--no-stubs`, `--remove-llmstxt`, `--drop-strict`,
260	    `--dry-run`, `--force`.

309	
310	## Gotchas
311	
312	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
313	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
314	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
315	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
316	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
317	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
318	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
319	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
320	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
321	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
322	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
323	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
324	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
325	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
326	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
327	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
328	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
329	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
330	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
331	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
332	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
333	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
334	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
335	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
336	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
337	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
338	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
339	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
340	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
341	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
342	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
343	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
344	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
345	  `select()` form.
346	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
347	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
348	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
349	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
350	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
351	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
352	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
353	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
354	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
355	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
356	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
357	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
358	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
359	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
360	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
361	  Counter-intuitive name.
362	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
363	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
364	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
365	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
366	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
367	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
368	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
369	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
370	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
371	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
372	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
373	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
374	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
375	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
376	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
377	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
378	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
379	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
380	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
381	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
382	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
383	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
384	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
385	  is just acting on it.
386	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
387	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
388	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
389	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
390	
391	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
392	
393	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
394	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
395	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
396	have customizations the templates don't know about.
397
```

8	
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	usage() {
12	  cat <<'EOF'
13	Usage: check-preferences.sh [OPTIONS]
14	
15	Read, write, or reset entries in .skills/preferences.yaml (per-repo).
16	
17	Options:
18	  --get KEY                  Print the value at KEY (e.g., mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled).
19	                             Prints empty string + exits 0 if absent.
20	  --set KEY=VALUE            Set a key. Repeatable. VALUE is parsed as YAML
21	                             (so 'true', '42', '2026-04-23', and bare strings
22	                             all work). Quote complex values.
23	  --reset NAMESPACE          Delete the entire top-level NAMESPACE key (returns
24	                             that skill to "never asked" state).
25	  --list                     Print the entire file (or "(empty)" if missing).
26	  --file PATH                Override file location (default: .skills/preferences.yaml
27	                             in the current dir or the first ancestor that has
28	                             a .git directory).
29	  --json                     Format --get / --list output as JSON.
30	  --dry-run                  Print actions but don't write.
31	  --help, -h                 Show this help and exit.
32	
33	Examples:
34	  check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
35	  check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
36	                       --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
37	  check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
38	  check-preferences.sh --list --json
39	
40	Exit codes:
41	  0  success (key absent on --get is also success — empty stdout)
42	  1  invalid arguments
43	  2  file/dir not accessible
44	  3  yq missing or yq error
45	EOF
46	}
47	
48	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
49	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
50	
51	# --- arg parsing ---
52	ACTION=""
53	KEY=""
54	NAMESPACE=""
55	FILE=""
56	JSON=0
57	DRY_RUN=0
58	SET_PAIRS=()

63	    --set)        ACTION="set"; SET_PAIRS+=("${2:-}"); shift 2 ;;
64	    --reset)      ACTION="reset"; NAMESPACE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
65	    --list)       ACTION="list"; shift ;;
66	    --file)       FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
67	    --json)       JSON=1; shift ;;
68	    --dry-run)    DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
69	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
70	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
71	    *)            die "unexpected positional argument: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
72	  esac
73	done
74	
75	[ -n "$ACTION" ] || die "must specify one of --get/--set/--reset/--list (try --help)" 1
76	
77	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "yq not found in PATH (install: brew install yq)" 3
78	
79	# --- file resolution ---
80	if [ -z "$FILE" ]; then
81	  cur="$(pwd)"
82	  ROOT=""
83	  while [ "$cur" != "/" ]; do
84	    if [ -d "$cur/.git" ]; then ROOT="$cur"; break; fi
85	    cur="$(dirname "$cur")"
86	  done
87	  if [ -z "$ROOT" ]; then ROOT="$(pwd)"; fi
88	  FILE="$ROOT/.skills/preferences.yaml"
89	fi
90

92	  local dir
93	  dir="$(dirname "$FILE")"
94	  if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
95	    [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ] && { log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $dir"; return 0; }
96	    mkdir -p "$dir"

100	    cat >"$FILE" <<'EOF'

103	# namespace. See:
104	#   skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/preferences-schema.md
105	EOF
106	  fi
107	}
108

110	case "$ACTION" in
111	
112	get)
113	  [ -n "$KEY" ] || die "--get requires KEY" 1
114	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
115	    if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then printf 'null\n'; fi
116	    exit 0
117	  fi
118	  # yq prints "null" for missing; convert to empty string for shell-friendliness.
119	  VALUE=$(yq -r ".${KEY}" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "null")
120	  if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then
121	    yq -o=json ".${KEY}" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null || printf 'null\n'
122	  else
123	    if [ "$VALUE" = "null" ]; then
124	      printf ''
125	    else
126	      printf '%s\n' "$VALUE"
127	    fi
128	  fi

130	
131	set)
132	  [ "${#SET_PAIRS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || die "--set requires at least one KEY=VALUE" 1
133	  ensure_file

135	  # Build a single yq expression so we make one atomic write.
136	  EXPR=""

138	    case "$pair" in
139	      *=*) ;;
140	      *) die "--set value must be KEY=VALUE (got '$pair')" 1 ;;
141	    esac

145	    # Dates and everything else go through as strings (quoted) — yq treats
146	    # ISO-8601 unquoted as arithmetic / invalid expression.
147	    case "$v" in

149	      \[*\]|\{*\}) yv="$v" ;;  # YAML flow sequence/mapping pass-through
150	      ''|*[!0-9]*) yv="\"${v//\"/\\\"}\"" ;;
151	      *) yv="$v" ;;
152	    esac
153	    if [ -z "$EXPR" ]; then
154	      EXPR=".${k} = ${yv}"
155	    else
156	      EXPR="${EXPR} | .${k} = ${yv}"
157	    fi
158	  done
159	
160	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
161	    log "[dry-run] yq -i '$EXPR' $FILE"
162	    exit 0
163	  fi
164	
165	  TMP="${FILE}.tmp.$$"
166	  yq "$EXPR" "$FILE" > "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; die "yq failed applying: $EXPR" 3; }
167	  mv "$TMP" "$FILE"
168	  log "Updated $FILE"
169	  ;;
170	
171	reset)
172	  [ -n "$NAMESPACE" ] || die "--reset requires NAMESPACE" 1
173	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
174	    log "Nothing to reset (file does not exist): $FILE"
175	    exit 0
176	  fi
177	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
178	    log "[dry-run] yq -i 'del(.${NAMESPACE})' $FILE"
179	    exit 0
180	  fi
181	  TMP="${FILE}.tmp.$$"
182	  yq "del(.${NAMESPACE})" "$FILE" > "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; die "yq failed deleting .${NAMESPACE}" 3; }
183	  mv "$TMP" "$FILE"
184	  log "Reset namespace .${NAMESPACE} in $FILE"
185	  ;;
186	
187	list)
188	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then

190	    exit 0
191	  fi
192	  if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then
193	    yq -o=json '.' "$FILE"

196	  fi

199	esac

```text
1	# Agent Skills
2	
3	A personal collection of [agent skills](https://agentskills.io/home) — both custom-authored and cherry-picked from upstream repos — installable as a single package.
4	
5	📚 **[Read the docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/)** for the full guide, conventions, and skill index.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	<!-- snippet:install (keep in sync with docs/_snippets/install.md) -->
10	```bash
11	# Install all skills bundled in this repo into your project's
12	# .agents/skills/ directory.
13	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
14	```
15	
16	> **Note**
17	> The trailing `/skills` matters. Without it, `npx skills` will look in
18	> `.agents/skills/` of the upstream repo, which contains a different
19	> layout. The `skills/` suffix points the installer at the
20	> `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/` trees.
21	
22	This is the recommended cross-agent install path. Project installs place the
23	canonical skill content under `.agents/skills/`, which Codex reads directly;
24	Claude Code receives its corresponding `.claude/skills/` links.
25	
26	> **Heads-up — upstream picker bug.**
27	> `npx skills`' interactive multiselect glitches once the skill list is long
28	> enough to scroll: options render duplicated and the selection state gets
29	> corrupted ([vercel-labs/skills#969](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/969)).
30	> This repo ships enough skills to trigger it. Until it's fixed upstream, skip
31	> the picker:
32	>
33	> ```bash
34	> # Install everything, non-interactively (no picker)
35	> npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills --yes
36	>
37	> # List names from a disposable directory. In an existing agent-managed
38	> # project, skills@1.5.23 may reconcile .agents/skills even with --list.
39	> scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
40	> (cd "$scratch" && npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills --list)
41	> rm -rf "$scratch"
42	>
43	> # Install one skill by name.
44	> npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills --skill clash-proxy-api
45	> ```
46	
47	### Optional: native Claude Code and Codex marketplaces
48	
49	A local checkout can expose the same category catalog through either native
50	plugin CLI:
51	
52	```bash
53	git clone https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills.git
54	
55	# Claude Code
56	claude plugin marketplace add ./agent-skills/skills
57	claude plugin install version-control@daviddwlee84-skills
58	
59	# Codex (verified with 0.147.0)
60	codex plugin marketplace add ./agent-skills/skills
61	codex plugin add version-control@daviddwlee84-skills
62	```
63	
64	Both native routes install a whole category plugin (`version-control` in this
65	example), not an arbitrary single skill. Codex reads the existing Claude-format
66	marketplace and generates its `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` adapter inside the
67	plugin cache; this repository does not need to maintain that second manifest.
68	Keep using `npx skills` when you want one skill or a cross-agent installation.
69	
70	Pass the checkout's `skills/` directory, not the repository root: the catalog
71	intentionally lives under `skills/.claude-plugin/` for the `npx` subpath above,
72	and both native CLIs require a supported manifest at the marketplace source
73	root.
74	<!-- /snippet:install -->
75	
76	## What's in here
77	
78	- **`skills/local/`** — custom-authored skills.
79	  - [`project-knowledge-harness`](skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/) — TODO + backlog + pitfalls structure with init / kanban / promote / add-todo / sweep-inbox toolkit. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/project-knowledge-harness/))
80	  - [`quantatitive-factor-researcher`](skills/local/quantatitive-factor-researcher/) — Python quant-research persona. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/quantatitive-factor-researcher/))
81	  - [`skill-author`](skills/local/skill-author/) — Author new skills following [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices) best practices; ships `new-skill.sh` scaffolder and `lint-skill.sh` linter. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/skill-author/))
82	  - [`verifiable-surfaces`](skills/local/verifiable-surfaces/) — Design CLIs/tools/services with `--help`/`--dry-run`/`--print-config`/isolated-state smoke, and verify config/CLI/dotfile/IaC changes via app-native loaders before claiming done. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/verifiable-surfaces/))

([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/12-factor-agent-design-review/))

Lifecycle: `new-bundle.sh` → `capture.sh <web|term|http|screen>` → `finalize.sh`. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/demo-evidence/))

102	    - [`skill-creator`](skills/vendor/skill-creator/) — from [anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills); evaluate, benchmark, and optimize skill trigger descriptions. Complements local [`skill-author`](skills/local/skill-author/). ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/skill-creator/))

115	## Categories in the install UI
116	
117	The grouped picker UI of `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`
118	is driven by [`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`](skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json).
119	Each plugin entry defines one category and explicitly lists its member skills;
120	anything not listed there falls under **Other** automatically. The manifest is
121	the source of truth for the current category set rather than a duplicated list
122	in this README.
123	
124	```bash
125	# Validate the manifest (paths exist, no duplicates, name not reserved,
126	# on-disk skills covered).
127	make marketplace
128	
129	# Exercise Claude Code + Codex native add/list/install in isolated state.
130	make native-marketplace-smoke
131	```
132	
133	The manifest lives under `skills/`, **not** at the repo root, because the
134	install command's `/skills` subpath makes the CLI read
135	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. See
136	[npx skills metadata model](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/reference/npx-skills-metadata/)
137	for the full mechanism, the `kebabToTitle` group naming rule, reserved
138	marketplace names, and the `marketplace.json` vs `plugin.json` distinction.
139	
140	## Repo memory
141	
142	This repo dogfoods `project-knowledge-harness` on itself:
143	
144	- [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) — priority/effort-tagged backlog.
145	- [`backlog/`](backlog/) — research notes for `P?` items (when populated).
146	- [`backlog/inbox.md`](backlog/) — quick-capture inbox; sweep into `TODO.md` later.
147	- [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — symptom-grep-able knowledge base of past traps (when populated).
148	
149	```bash
150	# Validate TODO.md and render kanban-style board
151	make kanban
152	
153	# Quick add structured TODO entry
154	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M --title "..." --description "..."
155	
156	# Move an active TODO to ## Done in same commit as the implementation
157	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
158	
159	# Triage backlog/inbox.md interactively
160	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh
161	```
162	
163	Full workflow: [Project memory](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/project-memory/).
164	
165	## Vendor system
166	
167	```bash
168	# Add a vendored skill (auto-syncs)
169	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
170	# or via Makefile
171	make add-vendor SOURCE=owner/repo/path/to/skill
172	
173	# Group into a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
174	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
175	
176	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
177	make sync
178	
179	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
180	make sync-check
181	```
182	
183	Full workflow: [Adding vendor skills](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/adding-vendor-skills/).
184	
185	**Dependencies:** `gh` (GitHub CLI, authenticated) and `yq` (YAML processor).
186	
187	## Docs site
188	
189	The docs site is built with MkDocs Material + `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`.
190	
191	```bash
192	uv sync --extra docs
193	make docs-serve         # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
194	make docs-build         # produces ./site/
195	```
196	
197	Deployed automatically to GitHub Pages on push to `main` via [`.github/workflows/docs.yml`](.github/workflows/docs.yml).
198	
199	If you want to apply the same docs stack to your own project, see [Downstream docs stack recipe](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/reference/docs-stack-recipe/).
200	
201	## Adding a new local skill
202	
203	Use the bundled scaffolder (recommended — seeds the agentskills.io best-practice
204	template **and** fans out discovery symlinks for non-universal agents):
205	
206	```bash
207	# Auto-detects scope: LOCAL (this repo) / PROJECT (another git repo) / GLOBAL (~/).
208	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
209	
210	# Override scope explicitly when intent isn't obvious:
211	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --project <skill-name>
212	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --global  <skill-name>
213	
214	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
215	```
216	
217	The scaffolder mirrors `npx skills add`'s placement contract — canonical
218	content goes under `.agents/skills/<name>/` (read directly by Cursor /
219	Codex / OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot), with relative symlinks
220	fanned out to `.claude/skills/` and any other already-present
221	non-universal agent dir. In this repo (LOCAL mode) the canonical lives
222	in `skills/local/<name>/` and the symlinks point back at it. See
223	[Creating local skills](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/creating-local-skills/)
224	for the full scope table.
225	
226	Or, just the SKILL.md skeleton via the upstream init (no symlinks, no
227	`references/` / `scripts/` / `assets/`):
228	
229	```bash
230	cd skills/local
231	npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
232	```
233

240	external skill collections, per-domain hubs (Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML
241	Research, Web & Fullstack, Knowledge Work, Agent Harness), a docs-only
242	curiosity shelf, and an MCP wiki.

244	Highlights:
245	
246	- [Skill collections index](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/catalog/skill-collections/) — every upstream we track, with `vendored / deferred / skipped / evaluated / wishlist` status per entry.
247	- [Skill curiosity shelf](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/catalog/curiosities/) — unusual or playful skills worth remembering without adding them to normal discovery or workflows.
248	- [Finance hub](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/catalog/domains/finance/) — covers `anthropics/financial-services`, `RKiding/Awesome-finance-skills`, the [Financial Datasets MCP](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/catalog/mcp/financialdatasets-ai/), and more.
249	- [Adding catalog entries workflow](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/adding-catalog-entries/) — how to record an external skill / MCP / domain decision.

86a8f7d42750f9c70dbb05308ca0d7409504ca4f refs/tags/ahh-v1.1.0
e050df5a9041d43281d2f3e3361c19b99ee75a45 refs/tags/ahh-v1.1.0^{}
# Pre-commit hook manifest for the agent-history-hygiene skill.
# https://pre-commit.com/#creating-new-hooks
#
# Consume from any repo's .pre-commit-config.yaml:
#
#   - repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
#     rev: ahh-v1.1.0            # bump with `pre-commit autoupdate`
#     hooks:
#       - id: redact-agent-secrets
#
# `pre-commit autoupdate` tracks the newest tag on this repo. Because this is a
# multi-skill monorepo, keep this hook's releases on the `ahh-v*` tag series
# (or pin a commit SHA in `rev:`) so an unrelated skill's tag can't silently
# bump this hook.
#
# language: script -> pre-commit runs the file directly (its `#!/usr/bin/env
# python3` shebang picks the interpreter); the redactor is stdlib-only, so no
# env is built and no uv/pip install is needed. It scans staged files itself
# (pass_filenames: false) and rewrites any leak in place, so pre-commit reports
# "files were modified by this hook" and you re-stage + recommit.
- id: redact-agent-secrets
  name: Auto-redact secrets in agent artifacts
  description: >-
    Redact leaked secrets in agent transcript/plan artifacts (SpecStory,
    Claude/Cursor/OpenCode plans, spec-kit, Codex) before they are committed.
  entry: skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/assets/redact_secrets.py --fix
  language: script
  pass_filenames: false
  # Default artifact-dir scope (mirror of assets/artifact-dirs.txt). A consuming
  # repo may override `files:` in its own .pre-commit-config.yaml to widen it.
  files: ^(\.specstory/history|\.claude/plans|\.cursor/plans|\.cursor/rules|\.opencode/plans|\.specify|\.codex)/.*\.md$
commit e050df5a9041d43281d2f3e3361c19b99ee75a45
Author:     Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
AuthorDate: Fri Jul 10 16:54:14 2026 +0800
Commit:     Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
CommitDate: Fri Jul 10 16:54:14 2026 +0800

    feat(agent-history-hygiene): publish redactor as a pinned pre-commit hook
    
    Vendoring scripts/redact_secrets.py into each project froze a copy that never
    saw upstream fixes (the header-scoping fix had to be applied per-repo). Publish
    the redactor as a pinned REMOTE pre-commit hook so fixes propagate via
    `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of manual re-copying.
    
    - .pre-commit-hooks.yaml (repo root): defines `redact-agent-secrets` as a
      language:script hook -> skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/assets/redact_secrets.py
    - redact_secrets.py: swap the uv/PEP723 shebang for `#!/usr/bin/env python3`
      + `from __future__ import annotations` so it runs stdlib-only on any python3
      (incl. macOS system 3.9) with no uv/pip; keep PEP723 block for standalone use
    - pre-commit-config.yaml.template: reference repo:…/agent-skills rev:ahh-v1.1.0
      instead of a `- repo: local` block + vendored script
    - bootstrap-project.sh: stop vendoring the script; add `--migrate` to convert
      old vendored repos (removes scripts/redact_secrets.py, rewrites the local
      hook -> pinned remote hook; idempotent, preserves other hooks)
    - SKILL.md + references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md: document the pinned-hook
      model, `--migrate`, release/autoupdate flow, and the monorepo-tag caveat
    
    Consumed as:
      - repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
        rev: ahh-v1.1.0
        hooks: [{id: redact-agent-secrets}]
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

```text
1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` will have `docs_dir: docs` pointing at their
36	  files and an **empty** `nav:` so MkDocs auto-generates the nav from the
37	  filesystem.
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing markdown files into an
46	  explicit `nav:` block** so the user can see/reorder them later.
47	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to
48	  pick a reasonable initial order (alphabetical by default).
49	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
50	  content is already there.
51	
52	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
53	
54	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
55	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
56	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
57	  has been asked once.
58	
59	## What "non-hidden files" means
60	
61	For the purposes of this check:
62	
63	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
64	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
65	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
66	  "no existing content".
67	
68	Implementation hint:
69	
70	```bash
71	find docs -type f \
72	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
73	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
74	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
75	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
76	  | head -50
77	```
78	
79	## Things this skill must NOT do
80	
81	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
82	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
83	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
84	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
85	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
86	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
87	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
88	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
89	  breaks rendering.
90	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
91	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
92	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
93	
94	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
95	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
96	
97	## After bootstrap
98	
99	Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
100	for option a) and report:
101	
102	- Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
103	- Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
104	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
105	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
106	
107	## Recording the decision
108	
109	```bash
110	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
111	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
112	```
113	
114	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
115	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).
116
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# `.skills/preferences.yaml` schema
2	
3	Per-repo preferences file used by `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` and any future
4	skill that needs to remember a user decision across sessions.
5	
6	## Location
7	
8	Always at `<repo-root>/.skills/preferences.yaml`. **Per-repo, not global.**
9	Each repository carries its own decisions; never write to `~/.skills/` or
10	`~/.config/`.
11	
12	The directory is created on first write. Add `.skills/preferences.yaml` to
13	`.gitignore` if the user prefers it private, but the default assumption is
14	that it's committed (decisions about *this repo's tooling* belong in the
15	repo).
16	
17	## Top-level structure
18	
19	```yaml
20	# .skills/preferences.yaml
21	# Decisions recorded by skills. Each top-level key is a skill namespace.
22	
23	mkdocs_site_bootstrap:
24	  enabled: true                  # null = never asked, true = opted in, false = opted out
25	  decided_at: 2026-04-23
26	  stack: mkdocs-material         # which docs stack variant
27	  auto_deploy: true              # deploy via GitHub Actions on push
28	  pages_deployed: true           # has the first deploy succeeded
29	  pages_enabled_at: 2026-04-23
30	  existing_docs_decision: skipped  # skipped | wrapped | none
31	  site_url: https://owner.github.io/repo/
32	  repo_slug: owner/repo
33	  # i18n keys — written by add-language.sh, read by add-docs-page.sh.
34	  languages: ["en", "zh-TW"]      # ordered list; first is default
35	  keep_english_terms: true         # injects terminology admonition into non-default stubs
36	  i18n_structure: suffix           # suffix | folder (folder reserved, not yet implemented)
37	
38	# Future skills add their own top-level keys with the same shape.
39	# example_other_skill:
40	#   enabled: true
41	#   decided_at: 2026-05-01
42	```
43	
44	## Conventions for skill namespaces
45	
46	- **Namespace key matches the skill's directory name** with `-` → `_`
47	  (YAML-friendly): `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` → `mkdocs_site_bootstrap`.
48	- **Always include `enabled` and `decided_at`.** These are the universal
49	  fields. `enabled` is the consent state; `decided_at` lets the agent see
50	  how stale the decision is.
51	- **Don't store secrets.** This file is meant to be safely committable.
52	  API tokens, passwords, etc. go in `.env` (gitignored) or in CI secrets.
53	- **Don't store derived state.** Anything reproducible from other files
54	  (e.g., "is mkdocs.yml present") should be re-checked, not cached. Only
55	  store decisions and timestamps.
56	
57	## Three-state semantics for `enabled`
58	
59	| Value | Meaning | Agent behavior |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| key absent or `null` | Never asked | Run the interview |
62	| `true` | User opted in | Proceed without re-asking |
63	| `false` | User opted out | Don't pester. If the user is now asking for it, confirm they want to reverse the decision, then `--reset` and re-interview |
64	
65	This three-state model is why we don't use a marker file (presence-only)
66	or a boolean (only two states). The "never asked" state matters.
67	
68	## Reading and writing
69	
70	Always go through `scripts/check-preferences.sh` rather than parsing the YAML
71	yourself. It handles:
72	
73	- Creating the file and `.skills/` dir if missing
74	- Preserving the comment header
75	- Atomic writes (write to `.tmp`, then `mv`)
76	- Friendly errors for malformed input
77	
78	```bash
79	# Read one key
80	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
81	
82	# Set one or more keys
83	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
84	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
85	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
86	
87	# Reset an entire skill namespace (returns to "never asked" state)
88	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
89	
90	# Dump everything
91	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --list
92	```
93	
94	The script supports `--json` for structured output that an agent can parse
95	reliably.
96	
97	## When to reset
98	
99	The user explicitly says one of:
100	
101	- "I changed my mind about <skill>" → `--reset <namespace>`
102	- "Stop nagging me about docs" → `--set <namespace>.enabled=false`
103	- "Re-ask me next time" → `--reset <namespace>`
104	
105	Don't reset proactively. The whole point is to *avoid* re-asking.
106	
107	## Cross-skill coordination
108	
109	Two skills shouldn't share namespace keys. If `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` and
110	some hypothetical `docs-publisher` skill both care about whether a docs site
111	exists, the answer is to **detect from the filesystem** (does `mkdocs.yml`
112	exist?), not to share a preference key. Preferences record *intent*; the
113	filesystem records *state*.
114	
115	## i18n keys (added when `add-language.sh` runs)
116	
117	| Key | Type | Meaning |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| `languages` | ordered list of locale codes | First entry is the default language. Empty / missing means monolingual (default). |
120	| `keep_english_terms` | bool | Whether to inject the "Terminology rule" admonition into non-default-language stubs. Defaults to `true`; the user can flip this if they don't want the admonition. |
121	| `i18n_structure` | `suffix` \| `folder` | How translated files are laid out. **Currently only `suffix` is implemented.** `folder` is reserved for future work; setting it now will not change script behavior. |
122	
123	`add-docs-page.sh` reads `languages` to decide whether to generate
124	`*.<LANG>.md` siblings alongside the default-language page. If the key is
125	missing or has only one entry, it stays mono-lingual (existing behavior).
126	
127	## Array values via `--set`
128	
129	`check-preferences.sh --set` recognises YAML flow sequences (`[…]`) and
130	mappings (`{…}`) and passes them through to `yq` unquoted. Use this for the
131	`languages` key:
132	
133	```bash
134	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
135	  --set 'mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=["en", "zh-TW"]'
136	```
137	
138	Bare strings, booleans, and numbers still work as before.
139	
140	## Schema versioning
141	
142	If we ever need to change the shape, add a top-level `schema_version: 1`
143	key and bump it. Until then, treat the schema as version 0 / implicit.
144	
145	## Validation
146	
147	`check-preferences.sh --validate` is a future addition (not yet implemented).
148	For now, trust the script's writes and don't hand-edit the file unless you
149	re-read it after to verify.
150
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# How `npx skills` reads catalog metadata
2	
3	This page captures the verified mechanism behind the grouped install UI
4	of `npx skills@latest add ...`. Everything below was confirmed by reading
5	the actual source of the npm package (`vercel-labs/skills`,
6	[`src/plugin-manifest.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/plugin-manifest.ts)
7	and [`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts))
8	and the official [Claude Code plugin-marketplaces docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces).
9	
10	## TL;DR for this repo
11	
12	- The grouped picker UI you see when running
13	  `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` is driven by
14	  `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — **inside** the `skills/`
15	  directory, not at the repo root.
16	- Every group header is `kebabToTitle(plugins[].name)`. Skills not listed
17	  under any plugin fall through to the **Other** group.
18	- Edit the manifest by hand; run `make marketplace` (= `bash
19	  scripts/validate-marketplace.sh`) to catch broken paths, duplicates, or
20	  on-disk skills that would silently fall under "Other".
21	- We do **not** ship per-plugin `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` files: each
22	  marketplace entry is already a complete inline `strict: false` skill bundle.
23	
24	## How the CLI resolves the manifest path
25	
26	The user's argument to `npx skills add` is parsed into `repo` + optional
27	`subpath`. For this repo:
28	
29	```
30	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
31	                       └────────── repo ──────────┘ └sub┘
32	```
33	
34	Inside the CLI ([`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts)):
35	
36	```ts
37	const searchPath = subpath ? join(basePath, subpath) : basePath;
38	// ...
39	const pluginGroupings = await getPluginGroupings(searchPath);
40	```
41	
42	So when the install command **includes** a subpath, the CLI reads the
43	catalog from `<repo>/<subpath>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
44	
45	| Invocation | Where the CLI looks for the manifest |
46	|---|---|
47	| `npx skills add anthropics/skills` | `<repo>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
48	| `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` | `<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
49	| `npx skills add foo/bar/some/dir` | `<repo>/some/dir/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
50	
51	This repo uses the second form because the `skills/local/` and
52	`skills/vendor/` trees live under `skills/`, not at the repo root.
53	
54	!!! warning "Common pitfall"
55	    Putting `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root and then
56	    invoking the CLI with a subpath silently disables grouping — the
57	    file at the root is never read, and every skill ends up in **Other**.
58	    Match the manifest's location to the install command's subpath.
59	
60	## Reusing the nested manifest with Claude Code and Codex
61	
62	The same file is consumed by three installers, but each chooses its marketplace
63	root independently:
64	
65	| Consumer | Marketplace root |
66	|---|---|
67	| `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` | the requested `skills/` subpath |
68	| `claude plugin marketplace add owner/repo` | the cloned repository root |
69	| `claude plugin marketplace add ./local/path` | the local path passed to the command |
70	| `codex plugin marketplace add ./local/path` | the local path passed to the command |
71	
72	A local checkout therefore provides zero-duplication native routes for both
73	plugin CLIs:
74	
75	```bash
76	git clone https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills.git
77	
78	claude plugin marketplace add ./agent-skills/skills
79	claude plugin install version-control@daviddwlee84-skills
80	
81	codex plugin marketplace add ./agent-skills/skills
82	codex plugin add version-control@daviddwlee84-skills
83	```
84	
85	Verified with Claude Code 2.1.235 and Codex 0.147.0. Codex reads the inline
86	Claude-format marketplace entry and generates a `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`
87	adapter in its install cache with only that category's explicit `skills[]`.
88	There is no second source manifest to maintain.
89	
90	The bare repository root does not contain a supported marketplace manifest, so
91	pass its `skills/` directory. The Claude GitHub shorthand `claude plugin
92	marketplace add daviddwlee84/agent-skills` consequently fails. A direct URL to
93	the nested JSON is not an equivalent Claude workaround: URL marketplaces fetch
94	the catalog file without the adjacent repository tree, so relative `source:
95	"./"` and skill paths have no installable source beside them.
96	
97	Both native routes install a category plugin, while `npx skills` can install one
98	selected skill across agents. `make native-marketplace-smoke` exercises both
99	local native paths in temporary configuration state and verifies that the
100	runtime adapter preserves category boundaries.
101	
102	## Manifest shape
103	
104	Reference: official [marketplace manifest schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces).
105	
106	```json
107	{
108	  "name": "<unique-marketplace-id>",
109	  "owner": { "name": "...", "email": "..." },
110	  "metadata": {
111	    "description": "...",
112	    "version": "1.0.0"
113	  },
114	  "plugins": [
115	    {
116	      "name": "<group-name-kebab-case>",
117	      "description": "Short description of the plugin / category",
118	      "category": "<for Claude Code /plugin UI>",
119	      "tags": ["...", "..."],
120	      "source": "./",
121	      "strict": false,
122	      "skills": [
123	        "./relative/path/to/skill-dir",
124	        "./another/skill-dir"
125	      ]
126	    }
127	  ]
128	}
129	```
130	
131	What the `npx skills` picker actually consumes:
132	
133	| Field | Used by `npx skills`? | Used by Claude Code `/plugin` UI? |
134	|---|---|---|
135	| `metadata.pluginRoot` | yes (resolves `source`) | yes |
136	| `plugins[].name` | **yes — drives the group header label** | yes |
137	| `plugins[].source` | yes (must be a string starting with `./`; object/remote sources are skipped) | yes |
138	| `plugins[].skills[]` | yes (must start with `./`) | yes |
139	| `plugins[].description` / `category` / `tags` / `version` / `strict` | **no — pass through** | yes |
140	
141	So `category` and `tags` are essentially free metadata for now: they cost
142	nothing to include in the manifest, and any future native consumer
143	(Claude Code's `/plugin` browser, downstream catalog tooling) can use
144	them without us migrating the file.
145	
146	### What the picker actually shows for a skill row
147	
148	Per [`src/add.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/add.ts)
149	(the `groupMultiselect` call), each skill row is constructed as:
150	
151	```ts
152	{
153	  value: s,
154	  label: getSkillDisplayName(s),        // = s.name (SKILL.md frontmatter)
155	  hint:  s.description.slice(0, 57)+'…' // = SKILL.md description, truncated to 60 chars
156	}
157	```
158	
159	So the **only** thing the user sees per skill is `name` + truncated
160	`description` from that skill's SKILL.md. **Nothing in `marketplace.json`
161	is shown per-skill** — not `plugins[].description`, not `category`, not
162	`tags`, not anything. The plugin's `name` only ever appears as the group
163	header above the skill rows.
164	
165	This means: if you want to annotate / re-label / "tag as deprecated" /
166	override the description for a single skill in the picker, the SKILL.md
167	itself is the only knob. There is no "external annotation" mechanism in
168	the catalog manifest.
169	
170	## Group header rendering — `kebabToTitle`
171	
172	The picker turns each plugin `name` into a header label by splitting on
173	hyphens and titlecasing each token. So:
174	
175	| `plugins[].name` | UI header |
176	|---|---|
177	| `document-skills` | Document Skills |
178	| `claude-api` | Claude Api |
179	| `ml-workflow` | Ml Workflow |
180	| `fullstack-nextjs` | Fullstack Nextjs |
181	| `notebooks` | Notebooks |
182	
183	Pick names that titlecase legibly. `claude-api` → "Claude Api" is the
184	official upstream choice and ships in the user-facing UI of
185	`anthropics/skills`, so awkward casing is a known quirk; do not work
186	around it with weird name fields.
187	
188	## Ordering in the picker (alphabetical-only)
189	
190	The picker sorts **purely alphabetically** — the order of the `plugins[]`
191	array in `marketplace.json`, and of each group's `skills[]` array, is
192	**ignored**. Confirmed in
193	[`src/add.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/add.ts)
194	(the interactive `groupMultiselect` path, ~L1298):
195	
196	```ts
197	const sortedSkills = [...skills].sort((a, b) => {
198	  if (a.pluginName && b.pluginName && a.pluginName !== b.pluginName)
199	    return a.pluginName.localeCompare(b.pluginName);          // ① group name, A→Z
200	  return getSkillDisplayName(a).localeCompare(getSkillDisplayName(b)); // ② skill name, A→Z
201	});
202	```
203	
204	The non-interactive list / summary / results paths sort the same way via
205	`Object.keys(grouped).sort()`. So there are two sort keys, both
206	alphabetical and neither array-driven:
207	
208	1. **Group order** — `plugins[].name` (kebab), A→Z.
209	2. **Within a group** — each skill's `SKILL.md` `name`, A→Z.
210	
211	### The only lever: rename the group so it sorts earlier
212	
213	Because the sort key is the group `name` string itself, the sole way to
214	move a group up is to make its name sort earlier. `localeCompare` orders
215	digits before letters, so a two-digit `NN-` prefix pins a group to the
216	top in an explicit order (the prefix shows in the header via
217	`kebabToTitle` — the accepted trade-off):
218	
219	| `plugins[].name` | picker header | position |
220	|---|---|---|
221	| `01-project-memory` | `01 Project Memory` | 1st |
222	| `02-skill-authoring` | `02 Skill Authoring` | 2nd |
223	| `03-infra-and-docs` | `03 Infra And Docs` | 3rd |
224	| `04-ml-workflow` | `04 Ml Workflow` | 4th |
225	| `05-notebooks` | `05 Notebooks` | 5th |
226	| *(everything else)* | *(kebabToTitle)* | A→Z, after all `NN-` groups |
227	
228	!!! warning "The `NN-` prefixes are intentional, not typos"
229	    Stripping a prefix drops that group back to its A→Z position. This
230	    repo pins its frequently-used groups this way; the rest stay
231	    alphabetical. Re-run `make marketplace` after any rename.
232	
233	**Within-group order is not controllable** without renaming the skills
234	themselves — and the `SKILL.md` `name` is load-bearing (it's the install
235	id), so don't. Example: under `02 Skill Authoring` the rows render
236	`mcp-builder → skill-author → skill-creator` regardless of the `skills[]`
237	array order.
238	
239	## "Other" — the auto-fallback group
240	
241	Any SKILL.md the CLI discovers under the search root that is **not**
242	listed in any `plugins[].skills[]` entry shows up under the **Other**
243	group header. This is how `anthropics/skills`'s `template-skill` ends up
244	under "Other" — it's not listed in their manifest's `plugins[]`.
245	
246	Use this to your advantage: a skill that doesn't fit any category yet
247	can simply be omitted from `marketplace.json` and it will still install,
248	just under "Other". Our `make marketplace` validator emits a warning (not
249	an error) for unlisted on-disk skills so they're easy to notice.
250	
251	## Path resolution rules (gotchas)
252	
253	- `source: "./..."` and `skills[]: "./..."` are **relative to the
254	  marketplace root** (the directory containing `.claude-plugin/`), not
255	  relative to the JSON file itself or the `.claude-plugin/` dir.
256	- The CLI rejects any path that does not start with `./` — `../` and
257	  absolute paths are not allowed (path-traversal protection in
258	  [`isContainedIn`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/plugin-manifest.ts)).
259	- `metadata.pluginRoot` (optional) is prepended to every plugin's
260	  `source`. We don't use it; we set `source: "./"` per plugin so each
261	  plugin path resolves directly under the manifest root (`skills/`).
262	
263	## Reserved marketplace `name`s
264	
265	These cannot be used as the `name` field, per official docs:
266	
267	- `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-code-plugins`,
268	  `claude-plugins-official`
269	- `anthropic-marketplace`, `anthropic-plugins`
270	- `agent-skills`
271	- `knowledge-work-plugins`, `life-sciences`
272	- Any name that impersonates an official marketplace
273	  (e.g. `official-claude-plugins`, `anthropic-tools-v2`)
274	
275	This repo's manifest uses **`daviddwlee84-skills`** — the GitHub repo
276	folder is still allowed to be `agent-skills`; only the `name` field
277	inside the manifest is restricted. The validator script enforces this.
278	
279	## Versioning
280	
281	Top-level `metadata.version` describes the marketplace catalog; it does not pin
282	these inline plugins. Claude Code 2.1.235 resolves plugin version identity from
283	`plugin.json`, then an individual `plugins[].version`, then the git source SHA.
284	These entries define neither of the first two, so an isolated update test advanced the installed SHA
285	and content after a new commit even while `metadata.version` stayed at
286	`"1.0.0"`; omitting the field behaved the same.
287	
288	This repository therefore keeps `metadata.version: "1.0.0"` as catalog
289	metadata, not as a release gate. A git-backed install still needs its normal
290	refresh sequence: fetch the new source (for the documented local checkout,
291	`git pull`), run `claude plugin marketplace update daviddwlee84-skills`, then
292	`claude plugin update <plugin>@daviddwlee84-skills`. The `npx skills` grouping
293	path ignores this field.
294	
295	## `marketplace.json` vs `plugin.json`
296	
297	| File | Purpose | When to use |
298	|---|---|---|
299	| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | Catalog of one or more plugins / categories | A repository that users register as a marketplace |
300	| `<plugin>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Manifest for one plugin | Conventional strict marketplace plugins that own their component tree |
301	
302	The two files are not redundant, but a marketplace entry may define a
303	manifest-less bundle inline. This repository does exactly that: every entry sets
304	`strict: false`, points `source` at the shared `skills/` root, and explicitly
305	lists its skill directories. Adding a set of near-empty `plugin.json` files
306	would not make discovery more correct; it would only create another identity/version
307	surface to keep synchronized.
308	
309	## Cross-agent portability
310	
311	`npx skills` is a one-way installer: it reads the manifest, then copies
312	SKILL.md files into each target agent's native skills directory
313	(supported targets enumerated in
314	[`src/types.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/types.ts)).
315	Most other agents (OpenCode, Cursor, Aider, …) do **not** read
316	`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` natively; they have their own conventions
317	(`.opencode/`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules/`, etc.). Codex 0.147.0 is a verified
318	exception: its plugin marketplace CLI accepts this manifest directly.
319	
320	The resulting distribution paths are:
321	
322	- One `marketplace.json` is enough for cross-agent **install** via
323	  `npx skills add`.
324	- The same file provides category-plugin installation through both Claude Code
325	  and Codex when `skills/` is passed as the local marketplace root.
326	- Standalone Codex skills installed under `.agents/skills/` continue to use its
327	  canonical shared discovery path; they do not require plugin packaging.
328	
329	On `codex plugin add`, Codex copies the shared source and generates a cache-local
330	`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` whose `skills[]` contains only the selected category.
331	Do not commit a second manifest merely to reproduce that adapter. A source
332	`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` remains relevant only if this repository later
333	chooses to publish a standalone Codex-specific package with its richer interface
334	metadata. Codex's public CLI does not install arbitrary `.plugin` or ZIP
335	archives, so a packaging script would still need a named release/upload consumer.
336	
337	## Hiding / deprecating a skill without deleting it
338	
339	The CLI has a built-in hide mechanism via SKILL.md frontmatter — set
340	`metadata.internal: true` and the skill becomes invisible in the picker
341	while staying in the repo.
342	
343	Per [`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts):
344	
345	```ts
346	const isInternal = data.metadata?.internal === true;
347	if (isInternal && !shouldInstallInternalSkills() && !options?.includeInternal) {
348	  return null;
349	}
350	```
351	
352	```yaml
353	---
354	name: my-deprecated-skill
355	description: ...
356	metadata:
357	  internal: true   # <- hides this skill from `npx skills add` picker UI
358	---
359	```
360	
361	What this does:
362	
363	- ✅ Skill stays in the repo, files unchanged.
364	- ✅ Hidden from the interactive picker by default.
365	- ✅ Still installable on direct request: `npx skills add <repo> my-deprecated-skill`
366	  passes `includeInternal: true` so the by-name lookup finds it.
367	- ✅ Power-user override: `INSTALL_INTERNAL_SKILLS=1 npx skills add ...`
368	  shows internal skills in the picker as well.
369	- ✅ Compatible with discovery elsewhere (Claude Code's auto-discovery,
370	  this repo's docs site) — `metadata.internal` is a `npx skills` convention
371	  only.
372	
373	When marking a skill as internal, also **remove its path from
374	`plugins[].skills[]`** in `marketplace.json` — otherwise you have a dead
375	catalog entry pointing at a hidden skill. The two settings should not
376	coexist for the same skill.
377	
378	### Why not just delete it?
379	
380	Reasons to use `metadata.internal` over deletion:
381	
382	- Keep the docs page reachable (the skill still renders on the docs site).
383	- Preserve `vendor.yaml` history and `last_sync` dates for vendored skills.
384	- Allow opt-in installs by name during a deprecation grace period.
385	- Keep `git log` / `git blame` continuity for future debugging.
386	
387	If you want it gone for good, delete the directory and remove the entry
388	from `marketplace.json` and (for vendored skills) `vendor.yaml`.
389	
390	### Validator coverage (today)
391	
392	`scripts/validate-marketplace.sh` does **not** currently parse SKILL.md
393	frontmatter, so it won't flag the "internal skill listed in
394	`marketplace.json`" mistake. If we hit this in practice, the validator
395	can be extended to:
396	
397	1. Parse each SKILL.md's frontmatter (e.g. via `yq` or python-frontmatter).
398	2. Error if any path listed in `plugins[].skills[]` resolves to a skill with
399	   `metadata.internal: true`.
400	3. Skip the "falls under Other" warning for internal skills (they
401	   wouldn't show up in the picker at all, so the warning is misleading).
402	
403	This is a deferred enhancement — see TODO if/when it becomes worth it.
404	
405	## Working with the manifest in this repo
406	
407	```bash
408	# Validate the manifest (parses, name not reserved, all paths exist,
409	# no duplicates, on-disk skills covered).
410	make marketplace
411	
412	# Or run the script directly with verbose output.
413	bash scripts/validate-marketplace.sh
414	
415	# Exercise native Claude + Codex add/list/install in temporary config state.
416	make native-marketplace-smoke
417	```
418	
419	After adding a new local or vendored skill:
420	
421	1. Place the SKILL.md as usual under `skills/local/<name>/` or
422	   `skills/vendor/<name>/`.
423	2. Open `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and add the new path
424	   (relative to `skills/`) to the appropriate plugin's `skills[]` array,
425	   **or** intentionally leave it out so it falls under "Other".
426	3. Run `make marketplace`. It will warn for unlisted skills and error
427	   for broken paths.
428
