```text
1	# Pre-commit redaction stack
2	
3	The three-layer defense agents can rely on when committing agent
4	transcripts + plan files.
5	
6	```
7	  Layer 0: SpecStory native        (specstory >= 2.4.0, ON BY DEFAULT)
8	            │  redacts as it WRITES .specstory/history/*.md (and cloud sync)
9	            │  emits [REDACTED:<betterleaks-rule-id>]
10	            ▼
11	  staged .md (transcript / plan)
12	            │
13	            ▼
14	  Layer 1: redact-agent-secrets   (pre-commit, pinned remote hook)
15	            │  rewrites file in place, re-stages via pre-commit
16	            ▼
17	  Layer 2: gitleaks-system         (pre-commit, github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks)
18	            │  blocks commit if a rule still matches
19	            ▼
20	  Layer 3: scan-staged.sh          (agent-invoked, belt-and-suspenders)
21	            │  run by the agent before `git commit` to branch on exit codes
22	            ▼
23	         git commit
24	```
25	
26	Layers 1 and 2 are installed by `bootstrap-project.sh`. Layer 3 is the
27	wrapper agents are expected to call before committing so they can react
28	to structured exit codes without parsing pre-commit output.
29	
30	Layer 0 is not ours — it is SpecStory doing the same job first, and only for
31	`.specstory/history/`. It is the reason Layer 1 usually has nothing to do.
32	
33	## Layer 0: SpecStory native redaction
34	
35	Since v2.4.0 the SpecStory CLI redacts secrets before writing markdown or
36	syncing to cloud, using the Betterleaks ruleset, on by default. Measured
37	coverage, the config knobs, and the classes it misses are in
38	[`specstory-native-redaction.md`](./specstory-native-redaction.md).
39	
40	Two consequences for the layers below:
41	
42	- **Layer 1 must not re-redact what Layer 0 cleaned.** Both write
43	  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists that shape (at
44	  `regexTarget = "match"`, so a line holding both a placeholder and a live key
45	  still fires). A transcript SpecStory already cleaned passes through
46	  untouched — which is what stops the `git add` -> commit -> "files were
47	  modified by this hook" -> `git add` -> commit loop.
48	- **Layer 1 is still load-bearing.** Layer 0 covers none of the other artifact
49	  dirs (`.claude/plans/`, `.cursor/rules/`, …), none of our custom rules, and
50	  misses many classes when the token appears in prose rather than `KEY=value`.
51	
52	Below SpecStory 2.4.0, or with `[redaction] enabled = false`, Layer 0 does not
53	exist and Layer 1 should run with `--legacy`.
54	
55	## Layer 1: redact-agent-secrets
56	
57	Implemented by `assets/redact_secrets.py` and published as a **pinned
58	remote pre-commit hook** via this repo's root `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`.
59	Consuming repos reference it in their `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
60	
61	```yaml
62	- repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
63	  rev: ahh-v1.1.0
64	  hooks:
65	    - id: redact-agent-secrets
66	```
67	
68	There is no vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py`, so a fix here reaches
69	every repo via `pre-commit autoupdate` (bumps `rev:`). On each commit:
70	
71	1. Pre-commit matches staged files against the hook's `files:` default
72	   (declared in `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`, mirroring
73	   `assets/artifact-dirs.txt`). `language: script` runs the file
74	   directly via its `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang — stdlib-only, no
75	   env build, no uv/pip.
76	2. `redact_secrets.py --fix` runs gitleaks against those files in staged
77	   mode, gathers findings, and replaces each literal secret with
78	   `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` — the same sentinel SpecStory >= 2.4.0 writes
79	   natively, so neither layer re-redacts the other's output. (`first3...last3`
80	   still appears in the *console report*, where a fingerprint helps identify
81	   which credential to rotate; `--legacy` writes it to the file instead.)
82	3. Private-key PEM blocks (`[REDACTED PEM PRIVKEY BLOCK]`) are replaced wholesale with
84	   `[REDACTED:private-key]` — SpecStory's own label for this class — and any
85	   stray key **header** token (a truncated key, or a header quoted in prose)
86	   with `[REDACTED:private-key-header]`. These
87	   headers — *not* the bare phrase `PRIVATE KEY` — are exactly what the
88	   downstream `detect-private-key` hook greps for (its `BLACKLIST`:
89	   `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY`, `PuTTY-User-Key-File-N`, `BEGIN OpenVPN Static
90	   key V1`), so the redactor scopes to them. Bare `PRIVATE KEY` prose is
91	   left intact on purpose: redacting it mangled legitimate text and,
92	   against a live transcript writer that re-appends the words on every
93	   diagnostic command, never converged (see the redact-loop pitfall in
94	   `SKILL.md`). The two placeholders contain neither a header token nor
95	   the bare phrase (they are lowercase; the header regex matches uppercase
96	   only), so a second pass is a no-op.
97	4. Any modified file is rewritten on disk. Pre-commit notices and exits
98	   non-zero with "files were modified by this hook" — the user then
99	   `git add`s the redacted files and recommits. Same UX as
100	   trailing-whitespace or end-of-file-fixer.
101	
102	### Why redact (Layer 1) instead of block (Layer 2) for agent artifacts?
103	
104	Because "blocking" a chat transcript on a leak is useless — the secret
105	is already in the file system, in the shell history, in the agent's
106	conversation context. The only defense left is "don't let it hit
107	`origin/`". Rewriting the file is the cheapest way to achieve that
108	while keeping the surrounding prose intact for future readers.
109	
110	## Layer 2: gitleaks-system
111	
112	The upstream `github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks` hook (pinned at `v8.22.1` in
113	the template). Runs after Layer 1 so it sees the redacted file. With
114	`.gitleaks.toml` in the repo root, custom rules apply automatically.
115	
116	### Allowlist design
117	
118	Four allowlists in `gitleaks.toml.template`:
119	
120	- **Global** (`[[allowlists]]`, line-scoped): tolerates `*_REDACTED*`
121	  sentinels emitted by older Layer 1 runs, plus truncated example shapes like
122	  `sk-proj-abc...`.
123	- **Shared sentinel** (`[[allowlists]]`, `regexTarget = "match"`): the
124	  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` shape written by both Layer 0 and Layer 1. Scoped to
125	  the match rather than the line on purpose — at line scope, a line carrying
126	  both a placeholder and a live key would be allowlisted wholesale.
127	- **Skill test corpus** (`[[allowlists]]`, path-only): `npx skills add`
128	  installs this skill's `tests/` into the consuming repo, and that suite
129	  exists to be detected. Without this, every repo installing the skill fails
130	  its first commit on the skill's own test data. The `detect-private-key` hook
131	  has no allowlist mechanism, so the pre-commit template excludes the same
132	  path there instead.
133	- **Path-scoped** (`[[allowlists]]` with `paths`): inside agent
134	  artifact directories, tolerate example markers (`example-key`,
135	  `your-api-key-here`) and truncated example shapes. Both the **path
136	  AND a regex** must match — a real `sk-ant-api03-<95 chars>AA` inside
137	  a transcript still fires.
138	
139	Real leaks take precedence over documentation because gitleaks evaluates
140	the finding's actual bytes, and truncated-example shapes don't have
141	enough entropy to match the strict rules in the first place.
142	
143	## Layer 3: scan-staged.sh
144	
145	Belt-and-suspenders wrapper:
146	
147	```bash
148	bash /path/to/skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh
149	```
150	
151	Runs `gitleaks git --staged` and translates the outcome into exit codes
152	agents can branch on:
153	
154	| Exit | Meaning                              | Typical agent reaction                                  |
155	|-----:|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
156	|    0 | Clean                                | Proceed with `git commit`                               |
157	|   10 | Leaks found, `--redact` passed       | Run `redact_secrets.py --fix`, re-stage, re-run         |
158	|   20 | Leaks found, no redaction            | Rotate secret at provider, then redact + re-stage       |
159	|   30 | gitleaks not installed               | Surface install hint; fall back to bare pre-commit      |
160	|    2 | Not inside a git repo                | Abort or bootstrap a repo first                         |
161	
162	Scripts always emit **JSON-lines findings on stdout** so the agent can
163	feed them to follow-up tooling without parsing prose.
164	
165	## Releasing / updating the pinned hook
166	
167	`assets/redact_secrets.py` is the single source; it's published to
168	consuming repos through this repo's root `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`, pinned
169	by tag. To ship a fix:
170	
171	```bash
172	# 1. edit assets/redact_secrets.py + tests, run the suite

174

4	---
5	
6	# git-workflow
7	
8	One consistent, opinionated git workflow that scales from a solo weekend
9	project to a multi-person, multi-month repo — so you (and your agents) stop
10	improvising commit messages, branch names, and release habits per project.
11	The defaults here favor a **clean, linear, reviewable history**.
12	
13	Surfaces, separated by the question they answer:
14	
15	| Surface | Question it answers |
16	|---|---|
17	| `references/project-tiers.md` | "Do I commit to `main`, use a `dev` branch, or open PRs?" |
18	| `references/conventional-commits.md` | "What exactly goes in the commit message, including AI provenance?" |
19	| `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md` | "How do I run parallel agents without collisions?" |
20	| `references/versioning-and-releases.md` | "When and how do I tag a version?" |
21	| `references/branch-hygiene.md` | "Which local branches are done vs still in-dev?" |
22	| `scripts/branch-status.sh` | Same, as data — classify every local branch. |
23	| `scripts/check-commit-msg.sh` | "Is this commit message valid?" |
24	| `references/lazygit-cheatsheet.md` | "How do I do this in lazygit?" (learning aid) |
25	
26	## Core principles
27	
28	1. **Commit messages are English and follow Conventional Commits**, even when
29	   the prompt/conversation is in Chinese. Code history is read by tooling
30	   (changelogs, SemVer bumps) and future collaborators; a mixed-language log
31	   is harder to grep and automate. Prompts stay whatever language you like.
32	2. **Prefer a linear history.** Default to `pull --rebase` and fast-forward
33	   merges; reserve merge commits and squashes for PR integration points. A
34	   linear log makes `git bisect`, `git revert`, and blame legible.
35	3. **One logical change = one commit; one workflow phase = one commit.** For
36	   multi-phase / `/workflows` work, commit at each phase boundary so you can
37	   roll back or resume cleanly if interrupted. Don't batch unrelated changes.
38	4. **Never leak secrets into history.** Secret scanning + agent-transcript
39	   handling is owned by the [`agent-history-hygiene`](../agent-history-hygiene/SKILL.md)
40	   skill — this skill *defers* to it at commit/merge time rather than
41	   reimplementing it.
42	5. **Keep authorship, AI provenance, and cryptographic signing separate.** The
43	   human remains Git author/committer; agent harness + model live in canonical
44	   trailers; SSH/GPG signing proves key possession, not who wrote each line.
45	
46	## Pick your tier first
47	
48	Match the workflow to the project's real collaboration needs, not its
49	ambitions. Promote a tier only when the **signal** actually appears.
50	
51	| Tier | Shape | Branching | Integration | Promote when… |
52	|---|---|---|---|---|
53	| **1 — Solo / early** | one `main` | commit to `main`; short-lived local branches optional | `pull --rebase`, `merge --ff-only` | you need a stable line separate from WIP |
54	| **2 — prod/dev split** | `main` = released, `dev` = integration | feature branches off `dev` | merge to `dev`; fast-forward `dev`→`main` at release | others rely on a deployed/tagged version |
55	| **3 — Team / grown vibe-coding** | `main` always deployable | short-lived `feat/…` etc. → PR | PR review/CI → squash-merge | ≥2 contributors, or you want a per-feature ship+review gate |
56	
57	A **solo vibe-coding** project can jump straight to Tier 3 even with one human:
58	the PR becomes the "ship a feature" boundary that separates finished work from
59	in-progress work, and gives CI a place to run. See
60	`references/project-tiers.md` for per-tier command recipes and the GitHub-Flow
61	summary. Read it when deciding whether to branch/PR or when a project outgrows
62	committing straight to `main`.
63	
64	## Commit messages
65	
66	Format (full spec + type table in `references/conventional-commits.md` — read
67	it when writing a non-obvious commit or wiring `check-commit-msg.sh`):
68	
69	```
70	<type>(<optional scope>): <subject>
71	
72	<body — the "why" for non-trivial agent commits, wrapped ~72 cols>
73	
74	<optional standard/native footers>
75	<canonical agent trailers — AI-Assisted-By / Agent-Transcript / Agent-Plan>
76	```
77	
78	- **Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`,
79	  `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`.
80	- **Subject**: imperative mood, lowercase start, no trailing period, keep the
81	  header ≤ ~72 chars. "add retry to client", not "Added retry." / "Adds…".
82	- **Breaking change**: `feat!:` / `refactor(api)!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:`
83	  footer → drives a **major** SemVer bump.
84	- Validate before committing when unsure:
85	
86	```bash
87	printf 'feat(auth): add token refresh\n' | \
88	  bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh
89	```
90	
91	- Install the message template so the shape is always in front of you:
92	
93	```bash
94	git config commit.template skills/local/git-workflow/assets/commit-template.txt
95	```
96	
97	### Agentic commit contract
98	
99	Use this portable minimum for commits produced with Claude Code, Codex,
100	Cursor, OpenCode, or another coding-agent harness:
101	
102	```text
103	feat(scope): add concise imperative summary
104	
105	Explain why the change was needed, the resulting behavior, and meaningful
106	validation. Keep this in English even when the prompt was not English.
107	
108	AI-Assisted-By: Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol)
109	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/session.md
110	Agent-Plan: .claude/plans/plan.md
111	```
112	
113	- A non-trivial agent commit requires a body. Use the validator's
114	  `--allow-no-body` only for a genuinely self-explanatory change such as a typo.
115	- Repeat `AI-Assisted-By` for every distinct harness/model that materially
116	  contributed. Never invent a vendor email merely to make GitHub show an AI as
117	  a co-author.
118	- Repeat transcript/plan trailers for every staged artifact, using repo-relative
119	  paths. Omit `Agent-Plan` when no plan file is in the commit.
120	- Preserve tool-native metadata (for example Claude's `Co-Authored-By`) as
121	  additive evidence. Put the canonical fields in the **final Git trailer
122	  block** so `git interpret-trailers --parse` can query them.
123	- When `agent-history-hygiene` is installed, generate the block from the staged
124	  snapshot instead of copying paths/model names by hand:
125	
126	```bash
127	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh
128	```
129	
130	Validate the complete message before committing:
131	
132	```bash
133	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh \
134	  --agentic --staged --file /path/to/commit-message.txt
135	```
136	
137	Cryptographic signing is opt-in and user-owned. Configure SSH/GPG signing only
138	when the user explicitly asks; never silently change global Git or harness
139	settings. A vendor-signed cloud-agent commit must not be amended solely to add
140	metadata, because amending replaces the signed commit object.
141	
142	## Branch naming
143	
144	Use a `<prefix>/<kebab-desc>` namespace so branches sort and clean up by
145	intent, and so agent-generated branches are visually distinct from yours:
146	
147	- **Human intent**: `feat/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`, `refactor/…`,
148	  `exp/…` (throwaway experiments). Optionally embed an issue: `feat/123-oauth`.
149	- **Agent / vibe-coding**: `agent/<desc>` — a dedicated namespace you can bulk-
150	  triage or delete separately from hand-authored branches.
151	- **Claude worktrees**: `worktree-<name>` (auto-created by `claude --worktree`)
152	  is a third namespace — see below.
153	
154	Keeping these separate is what makes `branch-status.sh` and
155	`git branch --list 'agent/*'` cleanup targeted rather than risky.
156	
157	## Merge & sync
158	
159	Set linear-history defaults (per-repo, or `--global` to your taste):
160	
161	```bash
162	git config pull.rebase true      # rebase local work onto upstream on pull
163	git config merge.ff only         # refuse merges that can't fast-forward
164	```
165	
166	- **Solo/local**: `git pull --rebase`, then `git merge --ff-only <branch>` to
167	  land a short-lived branch with no merge commit.
168	- **PRs (Tier 3)**: prefer **squash-merge** for vibe-coding branches (collapses
169	  noisy WIP into one clean `feat: …` commit on `main`); use **rebase-merge**
170	  when every commit is already meaningful and you want them preserved.
171	- Drive PRs from the terminal with the **forge CLI** — `gh` (GitHub) or `glab`
172	  (GitLab). These are strongly recommended (not required — the scripts here
173	  degrade to plain git if absent):
174	
175	```bash
176	gh pr create --fill            # or: glab mr create --fill
177	gh pr checks                   # watch CI
178	gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch   # glab mr merge --squash --remove-source-branch
179	```
180	
181	  The vendored `create-pull-request` skill (github-workflow group) is a
182	  companion for richer PR bodies.
183	
184	## Worktrees for parallel agents
185	
186	Run each parallel agent/session in its own git worktree so file edits never
187	collide. Full mechanics + caveats in `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md`
188	— read it before setting up parallel agents or debugging a missing `.env` in
189	a worktree.
190	
191	Essentials:
192	
193	```bash
194	claude --worktree feature-auth   # → .claude/worktrees/worktree-feature-auth/
195	```
196	
197	- Worktrees branch from `origin/HEAD` by default; set `worktree.baseRef: "head"`
198	  in settings to branch from your local HEAD (unpushed work).
199	- Subagents: add `isolation: worktree` frontmatter, or ask Claude to "use
200	  worktrees for your agents".
201	- **Gitignore `.claude/worktrees/`** so worktree contents don't show as
202	  untracked files in the main checkout.
203	- Bring **gitignored** files (e.g. `.env`) into new worktrees with a
204	  `.worktreeinclude` at the repo root (see `assets/worktreeinclude.template`).
205	  It uses `.gitignore` syntax and copies **only gitignored** matches — already-
206	  tracked files are in the checkout already, so don't list them.
207	- Bonus: because SpecStory tracks transcripts by *directory*, a worktree's
208	  fresh dir cleanly separates each parallel agent's chat history.
209	
210	## Versioning & releases
211	
212	Use **SemVer** (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) and let commit types imply the bump:
213	`fix:` → PATCH, `feat:` → MINOR, `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` → MAJOR. Tag releases
214	with an **annotated, `v`-prefixed** tag on the release commit:
215	
216	```bash
217	git tag -a v1.4.0 -m "release: v1.4.0" && git push origin v1.4.0
218	```
219	
220	When the whole project **is** a Python package, make the git tag the single
221	source of truth (setuptools-scm or hatch-vcs) instead of hand-editing a
222	version string. Details + config in `references/versioning-and-releases.md` —
223	read it when cutting a release or wiring package versioning.
224	
225	## Before you merge / ship
226	
227	1. **Phase commits**: ensure each phase of the work is its own commit (easy
228	   rollback / resume).
229	2. **Dev-env reproducibility (optional, recommended)**: commit
230	   `.vscode/settings.json` + `.vscode/extensions.json` so a fresh clone gets
231	   the same editor setup. (These are *tracked*, so they don't belong in
232	   `.worktreeinclude`.)
233	3. **Secret + agent-artifact hygiene** — defer to
234	   [`agent-history-hygiene`](../agent-history-hygiene/SKILL.md):
235	
236	```bash
237	# clean = exit 0; redacted = 10; leaks = 20 → stop and remediate
238	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh
239	```
240	
241	   If the project **doesn't** check in agent transcripts/plans, drop them
242	   before a squash-merge; if it does, stage them with that skill's
243	   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`. Either way, a leaked secret is remediated via
244	   its `references/remediation.md` (rotate first — never reflexive
245	   `git push --force`).
246	4. **Agentic squash metadata**: a squash merge creates a new commit, so copy the
247	   canonical `AI-Assisted-By` / artifact trailers into the squash message. The
248	   source commit's cryptographic signature cannot survive object replacement.
249	5. **Branch cleanup** after the PR merges:
250	
251	```bash
252	git fetch --prune
253	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/branch-status.sh   # find gone/merged/stale
254	```
255	
256	## When to use this skill
257	
258	- "Commit this" / "幫我 commit" / "整理一下 git" / "write a commit message".
259	- "Should I branch or just commit to main?" / "should I open a PR?".
260	- "Set up worktrees for parallel agents" / "carry my `.env` into the worktree".
261	- "How do I tag / release a version?" / "bump the version".
262	- "My local branches are a mess — which are done?" / "clean up branches".
263	- Starting a new repo and wanting a consistent commit/branch/release convention.
264	
265	## When NOT to use
266	
267	- **Secret leaked / scrubbing transcripts / committing chat history** — that's
268	  [`agent-history-hygiene`](../agent-history-hygiene/SKILL.md); come back here
269	  only for the surrounding commit/merge flow.
270	- **GitHub platform automation** (CI diagnosis, issue triage, rich PR bodies)
271	  — the vendored `github-workflow` group skills own that.
272	- A single trivial `git add` + `git commit` the agent already does correctly —
273	  no skill needed.
274	
275	## Available scripts
276	
277	- **`scripts/branch-status.sh [--json] [--stale-days N] [--help]`** — classify
278	  every local branch as `active` / `merged` / `gone` (upstream deleted, e.g.
279	  after a squash-merge) / `stale` (no commits in N days, default 30). TSV on
280	  stdout by default, `--json` for callers, prose on stderr. Always exits 0
281	  (state is data). Enriches `merged`/`gone` with `gh`/`glab` when available,
282	  falling back to pure git otherwise.
283	- **`scripts/check-commit-msg.sh [--file PATH] [--agentic] [--staged] [--allow-no-body] [--types]`**
284	  — default mode validates a Conventional Commits header. `--agentic` also
285	  requires an English body + canonical harness/model trailers; `--staged`
286	  cross-checks transcript/plan paths against the index. Exit **0** valid /
287	  **1** invalid / **2** bad args or repository context.
288	
289	## Bundled assets
290	
291	- `assets/commit-template.txt` — commit message skeleton for
292	  `git config commit.template`.
293	- `assets/worktreeinclude.template` — example `.worktreeinclude` (gitignored
294	  env files only; annotated so tracked files aren't added by mistake).
295	
296	## Reference files
297	
298	- `references/project-tiers.md` — read when deciding main-vs-dev-vs-PR or when
299	  a project outgrows its current tier. Per-tier recipes + GitHub-Flow summary.
300	- `references/conventional-commits.md` — read when writing a non-trivial commit
301	  or wiring the validator. Full type table, footers, examples.
302	- `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md` — read before setting up parallel
303	  agents or debugging worktree file-copy / cleanup issues.
304	- `references/versioning-and-releases.md` — read when cutting a release or
305	  wiring Python tag-driven versioning (setuptools-scm / hatch-vcs).
306	- `references/branch-hygiene.md` — read when local branches are confusing
307	  (PR merged but branch lingers; work continued after merge).
308	- `references/lazygit-cheatsheet.md` — read when you'd rather drive git through
309	  lazygit; a learning aid, safe to ignore once the CLI is second nature.
310	
311	## Gotchas
312	
313	- **`merge.ff only` refuses a diverged pull.** If upstream moved and you have
314	  local commits, a plain `git pull`/`merge` errors instead of making a merge
315	  commit — that's intended. Resolve with `git pull --rebase` (or an explicit
316	  `git merge --no-ff` when you truly want the merge commit).
317	- **Squash-merge orphans the source branch.** After a squashed PR, the branch's
318	  commits never appear on `main`, so `git branch --merged` won't list it; it
319	  shows up as `gone` upstream (`git branch -vv`). `branch-status.sh` classifies
320	  this correctly — delete with `git branch -D`, not `-d`.
321	- **A PR can merge and work still continue on the branch.** "Merged" is not
322	  always "done". `branch-status.sh` flags `gone` upstream but won't delete —
323	  confirm the branch has no un-pushed commits before removing it.
324	- **Tracked files in `.worktreeinclude` do nothing.** It copies only gitignored
325	  matches. A committed `.vscode/settings.json` is already in the worktree; put
326	  only truly-ignored files (`.env`, `.env.local`, `config/secrets.json`) there.
327	- **`.worktreeinclude` is skipped with a custom `WorktreeCreate` hook.** For
328	  non-git VCS (SVN/Perforce/hg) the hook replaces default logic — copy local
329	  files inside the hook script instead.
330	- **English-commit rule holds under Chinese prompts.** Don't mirror the
331	  prompt's language into the commit subject; translate the intent to English.
332	- **A commit template does not affect `git commit -m`.** Agent harnesses usually
333	  pass `-m` directly, so the template is guidance, not enforcement. Use
334	  `check-commit-msg.sh --agentic` for the actual contract.
335	- **Native attribution is not cryptographic signing.** `Co-Authored-By` and
336	  `AI-Assisted-By` are message metadata; a Verified badge comes from a signed
337	  commit object. Preserve both when present, but do not describe them as the
338	  same guarantee.
339	- **Don't tag before the release commit exists.** An annotated tag points at a
340	  commit — create/land the release commit first, then `git tag -a`, then push
341	  the tag. A tag on the wrong commit means re-tagging (`-f`) and a force-push.
342	- **`gh`/`glab` are optional.** Recommend them, but never make a workflow step
343	  hard-depend on a forge CLI being installed or authenticated.
344

90	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
91	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.

93	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.

95	### 4. Scaffold
96	
97	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
98	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the

101	`.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
102	`--social` is on.
103	
104	```bash
105	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
106	  --site-name "My Project" \
107	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
108	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
109	```
110	
111	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
112	files unless `--force` is passed.
113	
114	Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
115	are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
116	the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
117	
118	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
119	
120	```bash
121	uv sync --extra docs
122	uv run mkdocs build --strict
123	```

125	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
126	
127	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
128	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
129	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
130	Only proceed on explicit yes.
131	
132	```bash
133	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
134	  --repo owner/repo
135	```
136	
137	Flags:
138	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
139	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
140	
141	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
142	in preferences.
143	
144	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
145	
146	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
147	`mkdocs.yml`:
148	
149	```bash
150	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
151	  --section workflows \
152	  --title "My new workflow" \
153	  --slug my-new-workflow
154	```
155	
156	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
157	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
158	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
159	
160	If the project has additional languages configured in
161	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
162	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
163	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
164	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
165	
166	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
167	
168	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
169	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
170	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
171	
172	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
173	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
174	
175	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
176	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
177	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
178	
179	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
180	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
181	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
182	`Makefile` for you):
183	
184	```bash
185	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
186	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
187	```
188	
189	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
190	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
191	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
192	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
193	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
194	is a no-op.
195	
196	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
197	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
198	
199	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
200	
201	```bash
202	uv sync --extra docs
203	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
204	```
205	
206	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
207	
208	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
209	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
210	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
211	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
212	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
213	canonical).
214	
215	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
216	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
217	
218	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
219	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
220	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
221	> invent translations)."
222	
223	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
224	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
225	
226	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
227	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
228	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
229	user may want one without the other.

310	## Gotchas
311	
312	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
313	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
314	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
315	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
316	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
317	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
318	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
319	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
320	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
321	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
322	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
323	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
324	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
325	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
326	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
327	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
328	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
329	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
330	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
331	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
332	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
333	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
334	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
335	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
336	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
337	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
338	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
339	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
340	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
341	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
342	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
343	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
344	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
345	  `select()` form.
346	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
347	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
348	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
349	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
350	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
351	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
352	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
353	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
354	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
355	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
356	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
357	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
358	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
359	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
360	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
361	  Counter-intuitive name.
362	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
363	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
364	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
365	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
366	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
367	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
368	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
369	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
370	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
371	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
372	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
373	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
374	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
375	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
376	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
377	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
378	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
379	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
380	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
381	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
382	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
383	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
384	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
385	  is just acting on it.
386	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
387	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
388	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
389	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
390	
391	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
392	
393	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
394	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
395	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
396	have customizations the templates don't know about.
397
```

139	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
140	
141	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
142	in preferences.
143	
144	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
145	
146	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
147	`mkdocs.yml`:
148	
149	```bash
150	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
151	  --section workflows \
152	  --title "My new workflow" \
153	  --slug my-new-workflow
154	```
155	
156	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
157	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
158	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
159	
160	If the project has additional languages configured in
161	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
162	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
163	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
164	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
165	
166	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
167	
168	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
169	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
170	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
171	
172	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
173	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
174	
175	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
176	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
177	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
178	
179	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
180	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
181	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
182	`Makefile` for you):
183	
184	```bash
185	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
186	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
187	```
188	
189	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
190	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
191	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
192	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
193	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
194	is a no-op.
195	
196	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
197	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
198	
199	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
200	
201	```bash
202	uv sync --extra docs
203	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
204	```
205	
206	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
207	
208	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
209	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
210	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
211	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
212	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
213	canonical).
214	
215	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
216	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
217	
218	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
219	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
220	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
221	> invent translations)."
222	
223	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
224	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
225	
226	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
227	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
228	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
229	user may want one without the other.

310	## Gotchas
311	
312	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
313	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
314	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
315	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
316	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
317	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
318	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
319	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
320	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
321	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
322	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
323	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
324	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
325	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
326	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
327	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
328	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
329	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
330	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
331	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
332	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
333	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
334	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
335	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
336	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
337	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
338	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
339	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
340	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
341	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
342	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
343	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
344	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
345	  `select()` form.
346	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
347	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
348	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
349	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
350	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
351	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
352	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
353	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
354	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
355	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
356	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
357	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
358	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
359	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
360	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
361	  Counter-intuitive name.
362	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
363	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
364	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
365	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
366	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
367	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
368	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
369	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
370	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
371	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
372	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
373	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
374	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
375	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
376	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
377	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
378	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
379	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
380	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
381	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
382	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
383	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
384	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
385	  is just acting on it.
386	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
387	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
388	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
389	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
390	
391	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
392	
393	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
394	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
395	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
396	have customizations the templates don't know about.
397
```

77	- 每篇 notes page 使用統一 frontmatter：`kind`、`status`、`as_of`、`last_verified`、`upstreams`、`confidence`；正文區分 Fact、Observation、Inference、Opinion、Open question。
78	- Pi 兩頁涵蓋定位、minimal core、extension/resource/provider/session surfaces、SDK/RPC、security/trust 與「高可塑性不等於 benchmark 第一」。Oh My Pi 與 DeepSeek Harness 各自先建立 layer/interface/lifecycle/target-user，再比較與 Pi 的相似／不同；DeepSeek Harness 不預設為 Pi-like terminal replacement。
79	- Paradigm pages把 `LLM + harness → agent` 拆成可檢驗的心智模型，並把 `prompt → context → harness/meta-harness → loop → graph engineering` 明示為本站 editorial framework，而非公認線性標準。
80	- Coding-agent index 提供一致比較矩陣；六篇 profile 固定使用 instruction discovery、tools、permissions/sandbox、context/session、extensibility、orchestration、model/provider boundary、platform/license、change signals、sources/open questions 等欄位，方便後續更新。
81	- `best-practices.md` 收斂 controlled evaluation、context/tool budget、single/subagent/workflow/graph 選擇、verification、permission/sandbox 與 extension supply-chain checklist；避免把產品比較寫成無來源結論。
82	
83	## 5. 雙語作者規則
84	
85	- 先穩定 English page，再成對翻譯 title、headings、body、tables、admonitions、link text 與 alt text。
86	- zh-TW 技術名詞首次出現採「中文 (English original)」；沒有公認譯名就保留 English。CLI flags、API/package names、environment variables、paths、filenames、code 不翻譯。
87	- 兩語 sibling 保持相同 dates、versions、citations、research metadata 與章節語意；相對連結永遠指 canonical unsuffixed `.md`，不手寫 `.zh-TW.md` link。
88	- English/zh-TW pair 是一個完成單位：通過 `docs:check` 與 strict build 才算完成。
89	
90	## 6. README 與 isolated docs CI
91	
92	- 精簡更新 `README.md`：統一定位與 non-goals、拆開 core 與 handoff prerequisites、說明 empty learning combos／first-run auth、更新新 docs links；部署成功前以 repository-relative docs 為主，成功驗證後才提升 live-site URL。
93	- 新增 `.github/workflows/docs.yml`，不改現有 app CI：
94	  - PR 對 docs 相關 path 執行 parity check + frozen uv sync + strict build。
95	  - push `main` 自動 build/deploy，並支援 `workflow_dispatch`；deploy 僅允許 `main`、非 PR event。
96	  - filters 包含 `docs/**`、`mkdocs.yml`、`pyproject.toml`、`uv.lock`、`package.json`、`scripts/check-docs.ts` 與 workflow 自身。
97	  - 使用 official Pages artifact/deploy actions、`github-pages` environment、concurrency；將 `contents: read` 與 deploy 所需 `pages: write` / `id-token: write` 壓到最小 job scope。
98	
99	## 7. End-to-end verification
100	
101	依序執行：
102	
103	```sh
104	uv lock
105	uv sync --extra docs --frozen
106	npm run docs:check
107	uv run mkdocs build --strict
108	npm run test:all
109	git diff --check
110	git status --short --branch
111	```
112	
113	另外用本地 `mkdocs serve`／generated site 檢查 `/`、`/zh-TW/`、每個 top-level section 的 nested route、context-preserving language switch、translated nav/search、mobile nav、tables/code、internal anchors，以及 site 中沒有 English fallback、raw transcripts、placeholder 或生成目錄。最後和初始 status baseline 比對，確保既有 uncommitted skill/specstory 內容仍 untouched/unstaged。
114	
115	## 8. Commit、push 與 GitHub Pages consent boundary
116	
117	- 本地實作與驗證完成後先停止並回報；未另行指示前不 commit/push。
118	- workflow 必須先經使用者選定的 commit/push/merge 路徑進入 `main`。在實際啟用前，再明確確認將影響 `daviddwlee84/pi-agents` 且會執行：
119	
120	```sh
121	gh api -X POST repos/daviddwlee84/pi-agents/pages -f build_type=workflow
122	gh workflow run docs.yml --repo daviddwlee84/pi-agents
123	```
124	
125	- 若 private-repo Pages eligibility 因 GitHub plan 失敗，停止並如實回報；不自動改 visibility、billing、建立 `gh-pages` branch 或換部署平台。
126	- 成功後從 Actions/Pages API 取得實際 URL（預期 `https://daviddwlee84.github.io/pi-agents/`）並檢查首頁；只有驗證上線後才把 preferences 設為 `pages_deployed: true` / `pages_enabled_at` 並更新 README live link。

133	- Skill utility reused: `.agents/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh`; scaffold/i18n scripts intentionally not used because their current worktree/existing-doc behavior is unsafe for this migration.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# add-docs-page.sh — Create a new docs/ page and insert it into mkdocs.yml nav.
3	#
4	# Bash 3.2 compatible. Requires `yq` (mikefarah/yq v4+) for nav editing.
5	
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
9	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
10	ASSETS="$SKILL_DIR/assets"
11	
12	usage() {
13	  cat <<'EOF'
14	Usage: add-docs-page.sh [OPTIONS]
15	
16	Create docs/<section>/<slug>.md from a template and insert a nav entry into
17	mkdocs.yml under the matching section heading.
18	
19	Options:
20	  --section NAME      Section name (must match an existing top-level nav section
21	                      heading in mkdocs.yml, e.g. "Workflows", "Reference").
22	                      Use "_root" to add at top level (no section).
23	  --title TITLE       Display title (e.g., "My new workflow"). Required.
24	  --slug SLUG         Filename slug without .md (default: derived from --title).
25	  --template PATH     Page template (default: skill's assets/page.md.template).
26	  --target-dir DIR    Repo root (default: walk up from CWD looking for mkdocs.yml).
27	  --lang LANG         Create the page only for LANG (e.g. zh-TW). Skips the
28	                      default-language file and the nav-insertion step
29	                      (mkdocs-static-i18n auto-discovers language siblings).
30	                      If omitted, creates the default-language page plus
31	                      *.<LANG>.md stubs for every non-default language listed
32	                      in .skills/preferences.yaml.
33	  --dry-run           Print actions without writing.
34	  --force             Overwrite existing page file.
35	  --help, -h          Show this help and exit.
36	
37	Examples:
38	  add-docs-page.sh --section Workflows --title "My new workflow"
39	  add-docs-page.sh --section Reference --title "API schema" --slug api-schema
40	  add-docs-page.sh --section _root --title "About" --slug about
41	  add-docs-page.sh --section _root --title "About" --slug about --lang zh-TW
42	
43	Exit codes:
44	  0  success (idempotent: re-running with same slug is a no-op)
45	  1  invalid arguments
46	  2  mkdocs.yml not found
47	  3  refusing to overwrite (use --force)
48	  4  yq error or section not found in nav
49	EOF
50	}
51	
52	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
53	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
54	
55	SECTION=""
56	TITLE=""
57	SLUG=""
58	TEMPLATE=""
59	TARGET=""
60	LANG_ONLY=""
61	DRY_RUN=0
62	FORCE=0
63	
64	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
65	  case "$1" in
66	    --section)     SECTION="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
67	    --title)       TITLE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
68	    --slug)        SLUG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
69	    --template)    TEMPLATE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
70	    --target-dir)  TARGET="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
71	    --lang)        LANG_ONLY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
72	    --dry-run)     DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
73	    --force)       FORCE=1; shift ;;
74	    --help|-h)     usage; exit 0 ;;
75	    -*)            die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
76	    *)             die "unexpected positional argument: $1" 1 ;;
77	  esac
78	done
79	
80	[ -n "$SECTION" ] || die "--section is required (use _root for top-level)" 1
81	[ -n "$TITLE" ]   || die "--title is required" 1
82	
83	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "yq not found in PATH (install: brew install yq)" 4
84	
85	# Resolve target.
86	if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
87	  cur="$(pwd)"
88	  while [ "$cur" != "/" ]; do
89	    if [ -f "$cur/mkdocs.yml" ]; then TARGET="$cur"; break; fi
90	    cur="$(dirname "$cur")"
91	  done
92	  [ -n "$TARGET" ] || die "could not find mkdocs.yml walking up from $(pwd)" 2
93	fi
94	[ -f "$TARGET/mkdocs.yml" ] || die "no mkdocs.yml in $TARGET" 2
95	
96	# Derive slug from title if not given.
97	if [ -z "$SLUG" ]; then
98	  SLUG=$(printf '%s' "$TITLE" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -cs '[:alnum:]' '-' | sed 's/^-//; s/-$//')
99	fi
100	
101	# Compute paths.
102	if [ "$SECTION" = "_root" ]; then
103	  REL_PATH="${SLUG}.md"
104	else
105	  # Section dir = lowercased section name (matches our convention).
106	  SECTION_DIR=$(printf '%s' "$SECTION" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr ' ' '-')
107	  REL_PATH="${SECTION_DIR}/${SLUG}.md"
108	fi
109	ABS_PATH="$TARGET/docs/$REL_PATH"
110	
111	[ -n "$TEMPLATE" ] || TEMPLATE="$ASSETS/page.md.template"
112	[ -f "$TEMPLATE" ] || die "template not found: $TEMPLATE" 4
113	
114	STUB_TEMPLATE="$ASSETS/translation-stub.md.template"
115	MKDOCS="$TARGET/mkdocs.yml"
116	
117	# Helper: write a stub for a non-default language at <base>.<LANG>.md.
118	write_lang_stub() {
119	  local base_path="$1" lang="$2"
120	  local stub_path="${base_path%.md}.${lang}.md"
121	  if [ -e "$stub_path" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
122	    log "Stub already exists: $stub_path (use --force to overwrite)"
123	    return 0
124	  fi
125	  [ -f "$STUB_TEMPLATE" ] || die "stub template missing: $STUB_TEMPLATE" 4
126	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
127	    log "[dry-run] write stub $stub_path"
128	    return 0
129	  fi
130	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$stub_path")"
131	  sed -e "s|{{PAGE_TITLE}}|${TITLE}|g" \
132	      -e "s|{{LANG}}|${lang}|g" \
133	      "$STUB_TEMPLATE" > "$stub_path"
134	  log "Created stub: $stub_path"
135	}
136	
137	# --- --lang shortcut: only create the language stub, skip default + nav ---
138	if [ -n "$LANG_ONLY" ]; then
139	  write_lang_stub "$ABS_PATH" "$LANG_ONLY"
140	  printf '{"page":"%s","lang":"%s","status":"stub_created"}\n' \
141	    "${REL_PATH%.md}.${LANG_ONLY}.md" "$LANG_ONLY"
142	  exit 0
143	fi
144	
145	# --- 1. Create the default-language page ---
146	if [ -e "$ABS_PATH" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
147	  log "Page already exists: $ABS_PATH (use --force to overwrite)"
148	  log "Skipping page creation; will still ensure nav entry."
149	else
150	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
151	    log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $(dirname "$ABS_PATH"); cp $TEMPLATE → $ABS_PATH"
152	  else
153	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ABS_PATH")"
154	    cp "$TEMPLATE" "$ABS_PATH"
155	    sed -i.bak \
156	      -e "s|{{PAGE_TITLE}}|${TITLE}|g" \
157	      "$ABS_PATH"
158	    rm -f "${ABS_PATH}.bak"
159	    log "Created: $ABS_PATH"
160	  fi
161	fi
162	
163	# --- 2. Insert into mkdocs.yml nav ---
164	
165	# Idempotency check: does the nav already mention this path?
166	if grep -qF "$REL_PATH" "$MKDOCS"; then
167	  log "Nav already references $REL_PATH — checking language stubs only."
168	  NAV_STATUS="already_exists"
169	else
170	  if [ "$SECTION" = "_root" ]; then
171	    EXPR=".nav += [{\"$TITLE\": \"$REL_PATH\"}]"
172	  else
173	    # Find the index of the section in nav (top-level dict whose only key is $SECTION).
174	    IDX=$(SEC="$SECTION" yq 'env(SEC) as $s | [.nav[] | keys | .[0]] | to_entries | map(select(.value == $s)) | .[0].key' \
175	      "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "null")
176	    if [ "$IDX" = "null" ] || [ -z "$IDX" ]; then
177	      EXISTING_SECTIONS=$(yq '[.nav[] | keys | .[0]] | join(",")' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
178	      die "section '$SECTION' not found at top of nav: in $MKDOCS (existing: $EXISTING_SECTIONS)" 4
179	    fi
180	    EXPR=".nav[$IDX].\"$SECTION\" += [{\"$TITLE\": \"$REL_PATH\"}]"
