1	# Tests for agent-history-hygiene
2	
3	Run the full suite:
4	
5	```bash
6	# From repo root
7	make test-skill
8	
9	# Or directly
10	uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/ -q
11	/bin/bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/test_scan_staged.sh
12	/bin/bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/test_find_session.sh
13	/bin/bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/test_stage_agent_artifacts.sh
14	/bin/bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/test_agent_commit_metadata.sh
15	```
16	
17	`make test-skill` uses `SYSTEM_BASH ?= /bin/bash`. The new suites print
18	`BASH_VERSION` and fail on Darwin unless the running shell is Bash 3.x, so a
19	Homebrew Bash earlier on `PATH` cannot make the compatibility claim vacuous.
20	The target also sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` so host-global hooks cannot
21	alter throwaway commits. Override these variables only for deliberate testing.
22	
23	## Layout
24	
25	- `fixtures/` — paired `.md` files exercising gitleaks rules + allowlist.
26	  Each filename encodes its expected behavior (e.g. `real_anthropic.md`
27	  should fire, `example_shapes.md` should be allowlisted when staged
28	  inside an agent-artifact directory).
29	- `conftest.py` — shared pytest fixtures; loads the PEP 723 script
30	  `assets/redact_secrets.py` as an importable module.
31	- `test_redact_secrets.py` — unit tests for pure functions in the
32	  redactor (`redact_secret`, `filter_by_prefixes`,
33	  `find_private_key_files`, `redact_file`, `redact_private_keys`).
34	- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus tests: stages each fixture
35	  in a throwaway git repo and asserts `gitleaks git --staged` returns
36	  the expected findings (or lack thereof). Skipped if `gitleaks` is
37	  not on `PATH`.
38	- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
39	  `scripts/scan-staged.sh`: `0` clean, `20` leak, `30` missing
40	  gitleaks, `2` not a git repo.
41	- `test_find_session.sh` — real bounded prologues/local time, strict JSONL and
42	  canonical roots, symlink/control/UTF-8 safety, conditional dependencies,
43	  aliases, same-checkout leakage, subdirectory launches, and worktree isolation.
44	- `test_stage_agent_artifacts.sh` — explicit policy, configured/trailing-slash
45	  dirs, ignore/conflict/status parsing, real index-lock race and cleanup,
46	  exact trailers, validation-only normal/`-a`/`--only` commits, and
47	  primary/linked hook-path probes.
48	- `test_agent_commit_metadata.sh` — staged transcript parsing, model
49	  deduplication, spaced paths, JSON output, overrides, and bootstrap's global
50	  `core.hooksPath` refusal.
51	- `test_bootstrap_project.py` — verifies precise, idempotent nested SpecStory
52	  ignores; confirms `history/` stays visible; checks dry-run and the explicit
53	  `--untrack-specstory-state` migration contract.
54	
55	## Test-vector hygiene (why the fixtures carry `gitleaks:allow`)
56	
57	The firing fixtures (`real_anthropic.md`, `real_openai.md`, `private_key.md`,
58	`webhook_urls.md`) hold deliberately-fake test vectors. Most use realistic
59	secret shapes plus an inline marker so a repo-root, downstream, or
60	`npx skills add`-installed gitleaks scan **skips them by default**:
61	
62	```
63	<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->                      # markdown fixtures
64	```
65	
66	Two classes of secret need more than a marker, because the scanner that would
67	flag them does not read markers at all:
68	
69	- **Stripe webhook secrets** — GitHub's provider-level scanner does not honour
70	  gitleaks markers, so the fixture source uses
71	  `__SYNTHETIC_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET__`.
72	- **Private-key headers** — pre-commit's `detect-private-key` greps its
73	  BLACKLIST as plain substrings and honours *no* allowlist mechanism. Since
74	  `npx skills add` installs this whole directory into the consumer's repo at
75	  `.agents/skills/agent-history-hygiene/`, a literal header here fails **their**
76	  `git commit`, with nothing they can put in the file to stop it. So fixtures
77	  use `__SYNTHETIC_PEM_BEGIN__` / `__SYNTHETIC_PEM_END__` /
78	  `__SYNTHETIC_PEM_HEADER_OPENSSH__`, and Python tests build headers at runtime
79	  via `pem_header()` / `pem_block()` from `conftest.py`.
80	
81	`FIXTURE_PLACEHOLDERS` (conftest.py) is the single source of truth for the
82	expansions; `_stage_fixture_at` and the shell `stage_fixture` both apply them
83	inside their throwaway repos. `test_shipped_file_hygiene.py` enforces that no
84	shipped file regains a literal header. The other corpus + shell tests **strip the marker
85	before staging** (`_GITLEAKS_MARKER_RE` in `test_gitleaks_corpus.py`; the `sed`
86	in `stage_fixture` in `test_scan_staged.sh`), so the secret bytes have the exact
87	shape the rules expect and the assertions still fire. Principle: **fake test
88	vectors are out of scan scope by default, and only "fire" when a test re-plants
89	them.**
90	
91	Invariant — **the strip must be byte-identical**: never change a secret's length
92	or the length-sensitive rules (`sk-proj-…{80,}`, `sk-ant-api\d{2}-…{93}AA`, the
93	webhook regexes) stop matching. When adding a new firing fixture, append the
94	marker with a single leading space (`<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->`); the
95	strip regex reclaims exactly that separator. `clean.md` / `example_shapes.md`
96	carry no marker (the strip is a no-op) and must keep their must-not-fire
97	behavior. GitHub-native secret scanning ignores the marker; it's excluded
98	separately via the repo's `.github/secret_scanning.yml`. This replaced a former
99	repo-root `.gitleaksignore` whose `file:rule:line` fingerprints silently drifted.
100	
101	## Why these three levels
102	
103	The skill already surfaced three regressions during initial hand
104	verification — each one would have been caught here:
105	
106	| Regression                                                  | Caught by                |
107	|-------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
108	| Allowlist defaulted to `OR` between paths + regex           | `test_gitleaks_corpus`   |
109	| `[allowlist]` singular clashed with `[[allowlists]]` plural | `test_gitleaks_corpus`   |
110	| `gitleaks dir` silently skipped hidden paths                | `test_redact_secrets`    |
111	| JSON report `[]` treated as "leaks found"                   | `test_scan_staged.sh`    |
112	
113	## Requirements
114	
115	- `uv` (for `uv run --extra dev pytest`)
116	- `gitleaks` on `PATH` (corpus tests + shell test skip gracefully when
117	  missing — the pytest file xfails with a clear message, the shell
118	  test exits 0 for the "no gitleaks" case)
119	- `git` configured with a user identity (the shell test uses
120	  `-c user.email=...`)
121

1	# Pre-commit hooks for a project bootstrapped by agent-history-hygiene.
2	#
3	# Installed by `bootstrap-project.sh`. The redact-agent-secrets hook is a
4	# PINNED REMOTE hook provided by the agent-skills repo -- fixes propagate with
5	# `pre-commit autoupdate` (bumps the `rev:` below), so there is no vendored
6	# scripts/redact_secrets.py to drift out of date.
7	#
8	# artifact-dirs.txt still feeds the gitleaks allowlist (.gitleaks.toml) and
9	# stage-agent-artifacts.sh; the redact hook's own `files:` default lives in the
10	# hook repo's .pre-commit-hooks.yaml (override here only if you must).
11	#
12	# See https://pre-commit.com
13	
14	repos:
15	  # Auto-redact leaked secrets in agent artifacts BEFORE gitleaks runs.
16	  # If a file is rewritten pre-commit surfaces "files were modified by this
17	  # hook" and you `git add` + recommit -- same UX as end-of-file-fixer.
18	  - repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
19	    rev: ahh-v1.1.0
20	    hooks:
21	      - id: redact-agent-secrets
22	        # Override the default artifact-dir scope only if needed, e.g.:
23	        # files: ^(\.specstory/history|\.claude/plans|\.cursor/plans|\.cursor/rules|\.opencode/plans|\.specify|\.codex)/.*\.md$
24	
25	  # Gitleaks -- block commit when unallowlisted secrets are detected.
26	  - repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
27	    rev: v8.22.1
28	    hooks:
29	      # Prefer system-installed gitleaks to avoid Go toolchain build issues.
30	      - id: gitleaks-system
31	        pass_filenames: false
32	
33	  # Standard pre-commit hygiene. Feel free to trim per project needs.
34	  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
35	    rev: v5.0.0
36	    hooks:
37	      - id: detect-private-key
38	        # This hook honours neither `gitleaks:allow` markers nor
39	        # .github/secret_scanning.yml -- it greps for `BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY`
40	        # as a plain substring. agent-history-hygiene's installed test suite
41	        # carries those headers on purpose, so exclude that one directory.
42	        exclude: ^\.(agents|claude)/skills/agent-history-hygiene/tests/
43	      - id: check-added-large-files
44	        args: ['--maxkb=2048']
45	      - id: check-merge-conflict
46	      - id: end-of-file-fixer
47	        exclude: ^\.specstory/
48	      - id: trailing-whitespace
49	        args: [--markdown-linebreak-ext=md]
50	        exclude: ^\.specstory/
51

153	  tags        = ["webhook", "zapier", "auto"]

159	  tags        = ["webhook", "make", "integromat", "auto"]

170	# identity copied between machines, and sudo/root passwords pasted into chat
171	# while walking through an on-box deploy.

178	  # is the ONE secret that cannot be rotated cheaply, because it decrypts every

1	# Context
2	
3	目前 repository 只有五篇 English Markdown 文件，沒有 MkDocs、雙語導覽、文件建置或 GitHub Pages。使用者希望把它改造成 English 為預設、Traditional Chinese (`zh-TW`) 為第二語言的網站：一方面讓第一次接觸的人快速理解 `pia` 自製 CLI 的用途與安全邊界，另一方面建立可長期累積 Pi、agent harness、相關生態、coding agents 與 best practices 的研究筆記區。
4	
5	`pia` 的可信來源是目前程式碼、schema、測試與 CI；兩份 `.specstory/references/chatgpt-*.md` 只作為選題線索，因為其中有過期、互相衝突與不可攜引用。GitHub repository `daviddwlee84/pi-agents` 目前為 private、Pages 尚未啟用；文件實作與本地驗證先完成，commit/push、Pages API 與首次 workflow dispatch 仍是分開的 outward-facing consent gates。
6	
7	## 1. 保護現況並記錄 docs 偏好
8	
9	- 先保存 `git status --short --branch` baseline；不 stage、改寫或刪除既有的 `skills-lock.json`、`.agents/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/`、`.claude/skills/...` 與 `.specstory/` 變更。
10	- 不執行目前有 worktree root detection 與 existing-docs `wrap` 缺陷的 `init-docs-site.sh` / `add-language.sh`，也不使用 `--force`；改為手動建立站點設定。
11	- 唯一重用的 skill helper 是 `.agents/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh`，以明確 `--file <repo>/.skills/preferences.yaml` 寫入：`enabled: true`、執行日期、`stack: mkdocs-material`、`auto_deploy: true`、`pages_deployed: false`、`existing_docs_decision: wrapped`、repo/site URL、`languages: [en, zh-TW]`、`keep_english_terms: true`、`i18n_structure: suffix`。
12	
13	## 2. 建立嚴格、精簡的雙語 MkDocs stack
14	
15	新增／修改：

63	### Project / CLI content contract
64	
65	- Home 在首屏回答：`pia` 是 Git-versioned Pi/OMP combo manager、安全 materializer、session isolator 與 launcher；它不安裝 agent binaries、不管理 model/provider/credentials，也不把 Pi/OMP session formats 假裝成相容。

25	  --repo-name NAME         Python package-ish name for pyproject.toml (default: repo basename).
26	  --target-dir DIR         Repo root (default: walk up from CWD looking for .git).
27	  --existing skip|wrap     How to handle existing docs/ (default: skip — leave as-is, empty nav).
28	                           wrap: add files to nav alphabetically.

30	  --no-skeleton            Don't create the docs/ skeleton (use existing docs/ as-is).
31	  --social                 Enable the Material social plugin (OG/Twitter preview

33	                           (and mkdocs-material[imaging]), so a plain scaffold
34	                           stays dependency-free. See SKILL.md § Social cards.
35	  --dry-run                Print actions without writing.
36	  --force                  Overwrite existing files (mkdocs.yml, pyproject.toml).

39	Examples:
40	  init-docs-site.sh \
41	    --site-name "My Project" \
42	    --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/ \
43	    --repo-slug owner/repo
44	
45	  init-docs-site.sh --dry-run --site-name X --site-url https://x.io/ --repo-slug a/b
46

145	copy_template() {

159	# --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
160	# With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
161	# (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
162	# marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
163	expand_marker() {
164	  local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
165	  [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
166	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
167	    log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"

172	    awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
173	      index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
174	      { print }
175	    ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
176	  else
177	    awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
178	  fi
179	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regression tests for MkDocs bootstrap root discovery and existing-doc handling.
# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).

set -u

TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/.." && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SKILL_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
INIT="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/init-docs-site.sh"
PREFERENCES="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/check-preferences.sh"
BASE="$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-mkdocs-bootstrap.XXXXXX)"
BASE="$(cd "$BASE" && pwd -P)"
FAKE_BIN="$BASE/bin"
SYSTEM_PATH="/bin:/usr/bin:$PATH"
PASS_COUNT=0
FAIL_COUNT=0

trap 'rm -rf "$BASE"' EXIT

printf 'bash-under-test: %s (%s)\n' "$BASH_VERSION" "$BASH"
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && [ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" != "3" ]; then
  printf 'error: Darwin compatibility suite must run with /bin/bash 3.x\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

pass() { PASS_COUNT=$((PASS_COUNT + 1)); printf '  PASS %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { FAIL_COUNT=$((FAIL_COUNT + 1)); printf '  FAIL %s\n' "$1"; }
contains() { printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -Fq -- "$2"; }

assert_contains() {
  local name="$1" value="$2" expected="$3"
  if contains "$value" "$expected"; then pass "$name"; else
    fail "$name"
    printf '    expected output to contain: %s\n' "$expected" >&2
  fi
}

assert_file() {
  local name="$1" path="$2"
  if [ -f "$path" ]; then pass "$name"; else fail "$name"; fi
}

assert_no_file() {
  local name="$1" path="$2"
  if [ ! -e "$path" ]; then pass "$name"; else fail "$name"; fi
}

fingerprint_tree() {
  local root="$1"
  find "$root" -type f -print | LC_ALL=C sort | while IFS= read -r path; do
    printf '%s  %s\n' "$(git hash-object --no-filters "$path")" "${path#"$root"/}"
  done
}

run_init() {
  local target="$1" mode="$2"
  "$INIT" \
    --target-dir "$target" \
    --site-name "Fixture Docs" \
    --site-url "https://example.test/docs/" \
    --repo-slug "owner/repo" \
    --existing "$mode" \
    --no-workflow
}

validate_config() {
  local config="$1" mode="$2"
  shift 2
  uv run --project "$REPO_ROOT" --extra docs python - "$config" "$mode" "$@" <<'PY'
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

config = Path(sys.argv[1])
mode = sys.argv[2]
expected = sys.argv[3:]
data = yaml.safe_load(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

plugins = data["plugins"]
llmstxt = next(item["llmstxt"] for item in plugins if isinstance(item, dict) and "llmstxt" in item)
guides = llmstxt["sections"]["Guides"]

if mode == "fresh":
    assert data["nav"] == [{"Home": "index.md"}, {"Getting Started": "getting-started.md"}]
    assert guides == ["index.md", "getting-started.md"]
elif mode == "skip":
    assert "nav" not in data
    assert guides == expected
elif mode == "wrap":
    assert data["nav"] == expected
    assert guides == expected
else:
    raise AssertionError(f"unknown mode: {mode}")
PY
}

build_fixture() {
  local target="$1"
  uv run --project "$REPO_ROOT" --extra docs mkdocs build \
    --strict \
    --config-file "$target/mkdocs.yml" \
    --site-dir "$target/site" >/dev/null
}

mkdir -p "$FAKE_BIN"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 97\n' > "$FAKE_BIN/yq"
chmod +x "$FAKE_BIN/yq"

# Linked-worktree root discovery from a nested directory.
PRIMARY="$BASE/primary"
WORKTREE="$BASE/linked-worktree"
mkdir -p "$PRIMARY"
git -C "$PRIMARY" init -q -b main
printf 'base\n' > "$PRIMARY/base.txt"
git -C "$PRIMARY" add base.txt
git -C "$PRIMARY" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null \
  -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com commit -q -m init
git -C "$PRIMARY" worktree add -q -b linked "$WORKTREE"
mkdir -p "$WORKTREE/nested/deep" "$WORKTREE/.skills"
printf 'fixture: linked-worktree\n' > "$WORKTREE/.skills/preferences.yaml"

OUTPUT=$(
  cd "$WORKTREE/nested/deep" &&
  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null "$INIT" --dry-run --site-name Test \
    --site-url https://example.test/ --repo-slug owner/repo --no-workflow 2>&1
)
assert_contains "init resolves linked-worktree root" "$OUTPUT" "Target: $WORKTREE"

OUTPUT=$(
  cd "$WORKTREE/nested/deep" &&
  PATH="$FAKE_BIN:$SYSTEM_PATH" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null "$PREFERENCES" --list
)
assert_contains "preferences resolve linked-worktree root" "$OUTPUT" "fixture: linked-worktree"

# Outside Git, both scripts keep the invocation directory fallback.
OUTSIDE="$BASE/outside/nested"
mkdir -p "$OUTSIDE/.skills"
printf 'fixture: outside-git\n' > "$OUTSIDE/.skills/preferences.yaml"
OUTPUT=$(
  cd "$OUTSIDE" &&
  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null "$INIT" --dry-run --site-name Test \
    --site-url https://example.test/ --repo-slug owner/repo --no-workflow 2>&1
)
assert_contains "init falls back outside Git" "$OUTPUT" "Target: $OUTSIDE"
OUTPUT=$(
  cd "$OUTSIDE" &&
  PATH="$FAKE_BIN:$SYSTEM_PATH" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null "$PREFERENCES" --list
)
assert_contains "preferences fall back outside Git" "$OUTPUT" "fixture: outside-git"

# Fresh scaffold keeps the starter pages and starter configuration.
FRESH="$BASE/fresh"
mkdir -p "$FRESH"
run_init "$FRESH" skip >/dev/null
assert_file "fresh scaffold creates index" "$FRESH/docs/index.md"
assert_file "fresh scaffold creates getting started" "$FRESH/docs/getting-started.md"
if validate_config "$FRESH/mkdocs.yml" fresh; then pass "fresh config keeps starter entries"; else fail "fresh config keeps starter entries"; fi
if build_fixture "$FRESH"; then pass "fresh scaffold builds strictly"; else fail "fresh scaffold builds strictly"; fi

# Skip preserves existing docs and omits explicit navigation.
SKIP="$BASE/skip"
mkdir -p "$SKIP/docs/nested"
printf '# Alpha\n' > "$SKIP/docs/alpha.md"
printf '# Beta Notes\n' > "$SKIP/docs/nested/Beta notes.md"
printf 'static text\n' > "$SKIP/docs/notes.txt"
BEFORE="$(fingerprint_tree "$SKIP/docs")"
run_init "$SKIP" skip >/dev/null
AFTER="$(fingerprint_tree "$SKIP/docs")"
if [ "$BEFORE" = "$AFTER" ]; then pass "skip preserves existing docs byte-for-byte"; else fail "skip preserves existing docs byte-for-byte"; fi
assert_no_file "skip creates no starter page" "$SKIP/docs/getting-started.md"
if validate_config "$SKIP/mkdocs.yml" skip alpha.md "nested/Beta notes.md"; then pass "skip omits nav and refreshes llmstxt paths"; else fail "skip omits nav and refreshes llmstxt paths"; fi
if build_fixture "$SKIP"; then pass "skip scaffold builds strictly"; else fail "skip scaffold builds strictly"; fi

# Wrap preserves docs and writes deterministic path-only navigation.
WRAP="$BASE/wrap"
mkdir -p "$WRAP/docs/nested" "$WRAP/docs/assets"
printf '# Last\n' > "$WRAP/docs/z-last.md"
printf '# Alpha\n' > "$WRAP/docs/Alpha page.md"
printf '# Beta\n' > "$WRAP/docs/nested/Beta notes.md"
printf '# Owner\n' > "$WRAP/docs/owner's guide.md"
printf 'asset\n' > "$WRAP/docs/assets/readme.txt"
BEFORE="$(fingerprint_tree "$WRAP/docs")"
run_init "$WRAP" wrap >/dev/null
AFTER="$(fingerprint_tree "$WRAP/docs")"
if [ "$BEFORE" = "$AFTER" ]; then pass "wrap preserves existing docs byte-for-byte"; else fail "wrap preserves existing docs byte-for-byte"; fi
assert_no_file "wrap creates no starter page" "$WRAP/docs/getting-started.md"
if validate_config "$WRAP/mkdocs.yml" wrap \
  "Alpha page.md" "nested/Beta notes.md" "owner's guide.md" "z-last.md"; then
  pass "wrap writes sorted path-only nav and llmstxt paths"
else
  fail "wrap writes sorted path-only nav and llmstxt paths"
fi
if build_fixture "$WRAP"; then pass "wrap scaffold builds strictly"; else fail "wrap scaffold builds strictly"; fi

# Dry-run does not create or alter files.
DRY="$BASE/dry-run"
mkdir -p "$DRY/docs"
printf '# Existing\n' > "$DRY/docs/existing.md"
BEFORE="$(fingerprint_tree "$DRY")"
"$INIT" --target-dir "$DRY" --dry-run --site-name Test \
  --site-url https://example.test/ --repo-slug owner/repo --existing wrap --no-workflow >/dev/null 2>&1
AFTER="$(fingerprint_tree "$DRY")"
if [ "$BEFORE" = "$AFTER" ]; then pass "dry-run leaves target unchanged"; else fail "dry-run leaves target unchanged"; fi
assert_no_file "dry-run creates no config" "$DRY/mkdocs.yml"

printf '\n%d passed, %d failed\n' "$PASS_COUNT" "$FAIL_COUNT"
[ "$FAIL_COUNT" -eq 0 ]

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).

66	
67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
76	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
77	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
78	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
79	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
80	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
81	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
82	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
83	
84	Active series in this repo:
85	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
86	
87	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
88	
89	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
90	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
91	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
92	
93	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
94	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
95	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
96	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
97	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
98	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
99	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
100	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
101	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
102	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
103	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
104	
105	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
106	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
107	
108	## Marketplace Catalog
109	
110	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
111	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
112	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
113	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
114	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
115	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
116	for the full mechanism.
117	
118	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
119	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
120	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
121	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
122	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
123	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
124	
125	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
126	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
127	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
128	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
129	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
130	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
131	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
132	within-group caveat in
133	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
134	
135	## SKILL.md Format
136	
137	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
138	
139	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
140	
141	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
142	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
143	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
144	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
145	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
146	
147	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
148	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
149	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
150	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
151	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
152	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
153	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
154	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
155	
156	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
157	
158	```bash
159	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
160	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
161	
162	# …or remove them afterward
163	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
164	```
165	
166	## Project Memory Workflow
167	
168	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
169	
170	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
171	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
172	
173	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
174	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
175	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
176	
177	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
178	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
179	
180	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
181	
182	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
183	
184	   ```bash
185	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
186	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
187	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
188	   ```
189	
190	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
191	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
192	
193	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
194	
195	   ```bash
196	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
197	   ```
198	
199	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
200	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
201	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
202	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
203	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
204	
205	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
206	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
207	   afterwards to catch drift.
208	
209	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
210	
211	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
212	
213	```bash
214	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
215	```
216	
217	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
218	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
219	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
220	
221	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
222	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
223	
224	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
225	
226	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
227	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
228	own conventions). It has four subareas:
229	
230	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
231	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
232	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
233	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
234	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
235	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
236	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
237	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
238	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
239	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
240	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
241	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
242	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
243	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
244	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
245	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
246	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
247	  status / license / last_verified`).
248	
249	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
250	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
251	
252	| Status | Meaning |
253	|---|---|
254	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
255	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
256	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
257	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
258	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
259	
260	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
261	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
262	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
263	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
264	
265	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
266	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
267	
268	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
269	
270	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
271	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
272	
273	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
274	2. The root cause
275	3. The workaround
276	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
277	
278	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
279	the explanation they do not know yet.
280
```
</details></tool-use>

 # check-preferences.sh — Read, set, or reset .skills/preferences.yaml.
 #
 # Per-repo preferences for skills that need to remember user decisions across
 # sessions. See references/preferences-schema.md for the schema.
 #
 # Bash 3.2 compatible. Requires `yq` (mikefarah/yq v4+).

 usage() {

 Usage: check-preferences.sh [OPTIONS]
 
 Read, write, or reset entries in .skills/preferences.yaml (per-repo).
 
 Options:
   --get KEY                  Print the value at KEY (e.g., mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled).
                              Prints empty string + exits 0 if absent.
   --set KEY=VALUE            Set a key. Repeatable. VALUE is parsed as YAML
                              (so 'true', '42', '2026-04-23', and bare strings
                              all work). Quote complex values.
   --reset NAMESPACE          Delete the entire top-level NAMESPACE key (returns

 ### 1. Read preferences first
 
 Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
 decision:
 
 ```bash
 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
   --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
 ```
 
 Possible states:
 
 | State | Meaning | What to do |
 |---|---|---|
 | File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
 | `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
 
 ### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
 
 Ask the user explicitly:
 
 1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
    (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
 2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
    (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
 
 Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
 
 ```bash
 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
 ```
 
 If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
 future invocations.
 
 ### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
 
 Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
 `references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
 the short version:
 
 - If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
   exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
 - If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
-  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them;
-  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my files included as-is in the nav;
+  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
+  with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
+  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
+  explicit, alphabetical nav;
   (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
 - If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
 
 Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
 
 ### 4. Scaffold
 
 Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
 `pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
 `docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
 copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
 `.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
 `--social` is on.
 
 ```bash
 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
   --site-name "My Project" \
   --repo-slug owner/repo \
   --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
 ```
 
 Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
 files unless `--force` is passed.
 
 Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
 are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
 the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
 
 After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
 
 ```bash
 uv sync --extra docs
 uv run mkdocs build --strict
 ```
 
 ### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
 
 This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
 and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
 say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
 Only proceed on explicit yes.
 
 ```bash
 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
   --repo owner/repo
 ```
 
 Flags:
 - `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
 - `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet

 # Handling existing `docs/` content
 
 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
 
 ## Decision tree
 
 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
 
 ```
 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
 │         on the existing site.
 └── NO  → continue
     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
 ```
 
 ## Three options to present
 
 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
 for an honest consent gate.
 
 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
 
 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
   `docs/` untouched**.
-- The generated `mkdocs.yml` will have `docs_dir: docs` pointing at their
-  files and an **empty** `nav:` so MkDocs auto-generates the nav from the
-  filesystem.
+- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
+  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
+  pages.)
 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
 
 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
 
-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing markdown files into an
-  explicit `nav:` block** so the user can see/reorder them later.
-- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to
-  pick a reasonable initial order (alphabetical by default).
+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
+  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
+  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
+  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
+- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
+  deterministic alphabetical order.
 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
   content is already there.
 
 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
 
 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
   has been asked once.
 
 ## What "non-hidden files" means
 
 For the purposes of this check:
 
 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
   "no existing content".
 
 Implementation hint:
 
 ```bash
 find docs -type f \
   -not -path '*/\.*' \
   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
   | head -50
 ```
 
 ## Things this skill must NOT do
 
 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
   absolute" without an explicit ask.
 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
   breaks rendering.
 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
 
 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
 
 ## After bootstrap

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# check-preferences.sh — Read, set, or reset .skills/preferences.yaml.
3	#
4	# Per-repo preferences for skills that need to remember user decisions across
5	# sessions. See references/preferences-schema.md for the schema.
6	#
7	# Bash 3.2 compatible. Requires `yq` (mikefarah/yq v4+).
8	
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	usage() {
12	  cat <<'EOF'
13	Usage: check-preferences.sh [OPTIONS]
14	
15	Read, write, or reset entries in .skills/preferences.yaml (per-repo).
16	
17	Options:
18	  --get KEY                  Print the value at KEY (e.g., mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled).
19	                             Prints empty string + exits 0 if absent.
20	  --set KEY=VALUE            Set a key. Repeatable. VALUE is parsed as YAML
21	                             (so 'true', '42', '2026-04-23', and bare strings
22	                             all work). Quote complex values.
23	  --reset NAMESPACE          Delete the entire top-level NAMESPACE key (returns
24	                             that skill to "never asked" state).
25	  --list                     Print the entire file (or "(empty)" if missing).
26	  --file PATH                Override file location (default: .skills/preferences.yaml
27	                             at the current Git worktree root, or in the current
28	                             directory when outside Git).
29	  --json                     Format --get / --list output as JSON.
30	  --dry-run                  Print actions but don't write.
31	  --help, -h                 Show this help and exit.
32	
33	Examples:
34	  check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
35	  check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
36	                       --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
37	  check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
38	  check-preferences.sh --list --json
39	
40	Exit codes:
41	  0  success (key absent on --get is also success — empty stdout)
42	  1  invalid arguments
43	  2  file/dir not accessible
44	  3  yq missing or yq error
45	EOF
46	}
47	
48	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
49	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
50	
51	# --- arg parsing ---
52	ACTION=""
53	KEY=""
54	NAMESPACE=""
55	FILE=""
56	JSON=0
57	DRY_RUN=0
58	SET_PAIRS=()
59	
60	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
61	  case "$1" in
62	    --get)        ACTION="get"; KEY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
63	    --set)        ACTION="set"; SET_PAIRS+=("${2:-}"); shift 2 ;;
64	    --reset)      ACTION="reset"; NAMESPACE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
65	    --list)       ACTION="list"; shift ;;
66	    --file)       FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
67	    --json)       JSON=1; shift ;;
68	    --dry-run)    DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
69	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
70	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
71	    *)            die "unexpected positional argument: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
72	  esac
73	done
74	
75	[ -n "$ACTION" ] || die "must specify one of --get/--set/--reset/--list (try --help)" 1
76	
77	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "yq not found in PATH (install: brew install yq)" 3
78	
79	# --- file resolution ---
80	if [ -z "$FILE" ]; then
81	  if ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; then
82	    :
83	  else
84	    ROOT="$(pwd)"
85	  fi
86	  FILE="$ROOT/.skills/preferences.yaml"
87	fi
88	
89	ensure_file() {
90	  local dir
91	  dir="$(dirname "$FILE")"
92	  if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
93	    [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ] && { log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $dir"; return 0; }
94	    mkdir -p "$dir"
95	  fi
96	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
97	    [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ] && { log "[dry-run] touch $FILE with header"; return 0; }
98	    cat >"$FILE" <<'EOF'
99	# .skills/preferences.yaml
100	# Per-repo preferences recorded by skills. Each top-level key is a skill
101	# namespace. See:
102	#   skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/preferences-schema.md
103	EOF
104	  fi
105	}
106	
107	# --- actions ---
108	case "$ACTION" in
109	
110	get)
111	  [ -n "$KEY" ] || die "--get requires KEY" 1
112	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
113	    if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then printf 'null\n'; fi
114	    exit 0
115	  fi
116	  # yq prints "null" for missing; convert to empty string for shell-friendliness.
117	  VALUE=$(yq -r ".${KEY}" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "null")
118	  if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then
119	    yq -o=json ".${KEY}" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null || printf 'null\n'
120	  else
121	    if [ "$VALUE" = "null" ]; then
122	      printf ''
123	    else
124	      printf '%s\n' "$VALUE"
125	    fi
126	  fi
127	  ;;
128	
129	set)
130	  [ "${#SET_PAIRS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || die "--set requires at least one KEY=VALUE" 1
131	  ensure_file
132	
133	  # Build a single yq expression so we make one atomic write.
134	  EXPR=""
135	  for pair in "${SET_PAIRS[@]}"; do
136	    case "$pair" in
137	      *=*) ;;
138	      *) die "--set value must be KEY=VALUE (got '$pair')" 1 ;;
139	    esac
140	    k="${pair%%=*}"
141	    v="${pair#*=}"
142	    # Quote v as a YAML scalar; let yq interpret bool/int unquoted.
143	    # Dates and everything else go through as strings (quoted) — yq treats
144	    # ISO-8601 unquoted as arithmetic / invalid expression.
145	    case "$v" in
146	      true|false|null) yv="$v" ;;
147	      \[*\]|\{*\}) yv="$v" ;;  # YAML flow sequence/mapping pass-through
148	      ''|*[!0-9]*) yv="\"${v//\"/\\\"}\"" ;;
149	      *) yv="$v" ;;
150	    esac
151	    if [ -z "$EXPR" ]; then
152	      EXPR=".${k} = ${yv}"
153	    else
154	      EXPR="${EXPR} | .${k} = ${yv}"
155	    fi
156	  done
157	
158	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
159	    log "[dry-run] yq -i '$EXPR' $FILE"
160	    exit 0
161	  fi
162	
163	  TMP="${FILE}.tmp.$$"
164	  yq "$EXPR" "$FILE" > "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; die "yq failed applying: $EXPR" 3; }
165	  mv "$TMP" "$FILE"
166	  log "Updated $FILE"
167	  ;;
168	
169	reset)
170	  [ -n "$NAMESPACE" ] || die "--reset requires NAMESPACE" 1
171	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
172	    log "Nothing to reset (file does not exist): $FILE"
173	    exit 0
174	  fi
175	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
176	    log "[dry-run] yq -i 'del(.${NAMESPACE})' $FILE"
177	    exit 0
178	  fi
179	  TMP="${FILE}.tmp.$$"
180	  yq "del(.${NAMESPACE})" "$FILE" > "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; die "yq failed deleting .${NAMESPACE}" 3; }
181	  mv "$TMP" "$FILE"
182	  log "Reset namespace .${NAMESPACE} in $FILE"
183	  ;;
184	
185	list)
186	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
187	    if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then printf '{}\n'; else printf '(empty: %s)\n' "$FILE"; fi
188	    exit 0
189	  fi
190	  if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then
191	    yq -o=json '.' "$FILE"
192	  else
193	    cat "$FILE"
194	  fi
195	  ;;
196	
197	esac
198

1	---
2	name: mkdocs-site-bootstrap
3	description: Bootstrap MkDocs Material docs sites with optional GitHub Pages deploy, uv-pinned tooling, llms.txt/copy-to-LLM support, page/nav helpers, and mkdocs-static-i18n languages such as zh-TW. Use when the user asks to set up docs, publish docs to GitHub Pages, create an MkDocs site, turn README or markdown notes into a site, add bilingual/multilingual docs, add zh-TW/Traditional Chinese, i18n, or translate docs. Consent-gated; records repo preferences and never auto-migrates existing docs.
4	---
5	
6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
10	
11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
22	- User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
23	  applied to a new project
24	- User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
25	- User asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual",
26	  "add Traditional Chinese", "add zh-TW", "translate the docs", or to add
27	  any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7
28	
29	## When NOT to trigger
30	
31	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
32	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
33	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
34	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
35	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
36	
37	## Workflow
38	
39	### 1. Read preferences first
40	
41	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
42	decision:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
46	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
47	```
48	
49	Possible states:
50	
51	| State | Meaning | What to do |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
54	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
55	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
56	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
57	
58	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
59	
60	Ask the user explicitly:
61	
62	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
63	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
64	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
65	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
66	
67	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
68	
69	```bash
70	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
71	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
72	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
73	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
74	```
75	
76	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
77	future invocations.
78	
79	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
80	
81	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
82	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
83	the short version:
84	
85	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
86	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
87	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
88	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
89	  with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
90	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
91	  explicit, alphabetical nav;
92	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
93	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
94	
95	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
96	
97	### 4. Scaffold
98	
99	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
100	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
101	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
102	copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
103	`.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
104	`--social` is on.
105	
106	```bash
107	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
108	  --site-name "My Project" \
109	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
110	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
111	```
112	
113	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
114	files unless `--force` is passed.
115	
116	Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
117	are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
118	the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
119	
120	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
121	
122	```bash
123	uv sync --extra docs
124	uv run mkdocs build --strict
125	```
126	
127	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
128	
129	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
130	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
131	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
132	Only proceed on explicit yes.
133	
134	```bash
135	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
136	  --repo owner/repo
137	```
138	
139	Flags:
140	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
141	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
142	
143	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
144	in preferences.
145	
146	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
147	
148	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
149	`mkdocs.yml`:
150	
151	```bash
152	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
153	  --section workflows \
154	  --title "My new workflow" \
155	  --slug my-new-workflow
156	```
157	
158	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
159	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
160	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
161	
162	If the project has additional languages configured in
163	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
164	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
165	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
166	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
167	
168	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
169	
170	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
171	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
172	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
173	
174	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
175	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
176	
177	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
178	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
179	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
180	
181	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
182	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
183	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
184	`Makefile` for you):
185	
186	```bash
187	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
188	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
189	```
190	
191	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
192	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
193	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
194	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
195	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
196	is a no-op.
197	
198	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
199	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
200	
201	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
202	
203	```bash
204	uv sync --extra docs
205	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
206	```
207	
208	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
209	
210	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
211	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
212	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
213	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
214	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
215	canonical).
216	
217	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
218	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
219	
220	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
221	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
222	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
223	> invent translations)."
224	
225	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
226	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
227	
228	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
229	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
230	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
231	user may want one without the other.
232	
233	## Available scripts
234	
235	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
236	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
237	  - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
238	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
239	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
240	  - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,
241	    `--no-workflow`, `--no-skeleton`, `--social`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
242	  - Always appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to `.gitignore`,
243	    idempotently.
244	  - `--social` opts into OG/Twitter cards: expands the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers in
245	    the templates with the blocks in `assets/social/`, and adds `/.cache/` to
246	    `.gitignore`. Off by default (keeps the scaffold Cairo/Pango-free).
247	- **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via
248	  `gh api`. Requires `gh auth status` to pass first.
249	  - Flags: `--repo OWNER/REPO`, `--no-trigger`, `--dry-run`.
250	- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page and insert it into
251	  `mkdocs.yml`'s nav. If multiple languages are configured, also writes
252	  `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.
253	  - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--lang LANG`
254	    (single-language stub only), `--dry-run`, `--force`.
255	- **`scripts/add-language.sh`** — Retrofit a non-default language into an
256	  existing site. Inserts `plugins.i18n`, creates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs with
257	  the terminology admonition, updates preferences, uncomments the static-i18n
258	  dep. Keeps `mkdocs-llmstxt` by default; auto-patches CI to drop `--strict`
259	  with `--drop-strict`. Idempotent.
260	  - Flags: `--lang LANG` (required), `--name NAME`, `--default-lang LANG`,
261	    `--target-dir DIR`, `--no-stubs`, `--remove-llmstxt`, `--drop-strict`,
262	    `--dry-run`, `--force`.
263	
264	## Reference files
265	
266	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
267	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
268	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
269	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
270	  user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
271	  step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
272	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
273	  pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
274	  exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
275	- `references/i18n-guide.md` — Bilingual / multi-language docs setup using
276	  `mkdocs-static-i18n`. Read this **before** running `add-language.sh`. Includes
277	  the verbatim "preserve English originals" terminology rule for zh-TW pages.
278	- `references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md` — Why the stack pins `mkdocs<2` and
279	  `mkdocs-material<10`. Captures the MkDocs 2.0 plugin-removal situation,
280	  Material team's Zensical replacement, and the criteria for lifting the
281	  caps. Read whenever a user asks about upgrading MkDocs or why the docs
282	  build is on 1.x.
283	
284	## Bundled assets
285	
286	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
287	
288	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
289	  plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,

291	  `init-docs-site.sh` expands (with `--social`) or deletes.
292	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs

294	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with

296	  marker for the Cairo/Pango + card-cache steps.
297	- `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when
298	  `init-docs-site.sh --social` is passed: `mkdocs-plugin.yml` (the `social`
299	  plugin block), `pyproject-dep.txt` (`mkdocs-material[imaging]`), and
300	  `ci-steps.yml` (the Cairo/Pango install + `.cache/plugin/social` cache).
301	  Pre-indented for their insertion points — keep the indentation.
302	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
303	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
304	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
305	- `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
306	  pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
307	  terminology-rule admonition.
308	- `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
309	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
310	  builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
311	
312	## Gotchas
313	
314	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
315	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
316	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
317	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
318	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
319	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
320	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
321	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
322	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
323	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
324	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
325	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
326	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
327	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
328	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
329	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
330	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
331	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
332	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
333	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
334	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
335	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
336	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
337	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
338	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
339	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
340	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
341	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
342	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
343	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
344	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
345	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
346	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
347	  `select()` form.
348	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
349	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
350	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
351	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
352	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
353	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
354	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
355	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
356	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
357	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
358	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
359	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
360	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
361	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
362	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
363	  Counter-intuitive name.
364	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
365	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
366	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
367	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
368	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
369	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
370	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
371	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
372	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
373	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
374	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
375	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
376	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
377	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
378	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
379	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
380	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
381	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
382	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
383	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
384	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
385	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
386	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
387	  is just acting on it.
388	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
389	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
390	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
391	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
392	
393	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
394	
395	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
396	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
397	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
398	have customizations the templates don't know about.
399
```
