1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
36	  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
37	  pages.)
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
46	  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
47	  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
48	  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
49	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
50	  deterministic alphabetical order.
51	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
52	  content is already there.
53	
54	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
55	
56	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
57	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
58	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
59	  has been asked once.
60	
61	## What "non-hidden files" means
62	
63	For the purposes of this check:
64	
65	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
66	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
67	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
68	  "no existing content".
69	
70	Implementation hint:
71	
72	```bash
73	find docs -type f \
74	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
75	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
76	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
77	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
78	  | head -50
79	```
80	
81	## Things this skill must NOT do
82	
83	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
84	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
85	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
86	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
87	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
88	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
89	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
90	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
91	  breaks rendering.
92	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
93	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
94	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
95	
96	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
97	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
98	
99	## After bootstrap
100	
101	Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
102	for option a) and report:
103	
104	- Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
105	- Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
106	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
107	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
108	
109	## Recording the decision
110	
111	```bash
112	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
113	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
114	```
115	
116	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
117	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).

+replace_marked_block() {
+  local file="$1" begin="$2" end="$3" replacement="$4" tmp rc
+  tmp="${file}.tmp.$$"
+  if awk -v begin="$begin" -v end="$end" -v replacement="$replacement" '
+    BEGIN { inside = 0; begin_count = 0; end_count = 0 }
+    index($0, begin) {
+      begin_count++
+      inside = 1
+      while ((getline line < replacement) > 0) print line
+      close(replacement)
+      next
+    }
+    index($0, end) { end_count++; inside = 0; next }
+    !inside { print }
+    END {
+      if (inside || begin_count != 1 || end_count != 1) exit 2

+    mv "$tmp" "$file"
+  else
+    rc=$?
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    return "$rc"
+  fi

+strip_starter_markers() {

175	      { print }

177	  else

17	Options:

19	                             Prints empty string + exits 0 if absent.
20	  --set KEY=VALUE            Set a key. Repeatable. VALUE is parsed as YAML
21	                             (so 'true', '42', '2026-04-23', and bare strings
22	                             all work). Quote complex values.
23	  --reset NAMESPACE          Delete the entire top-level NAMESPACE key (returns
24	                             that skill to "never asked" state).
25	  --list                     Print the entire file (or "(empty)" if missing).
26	  --file PATH                Override file location (default: .skills/preferences.yaml
27	                             at the current Git worktree root, or in the current
28	                             directory when outside Git).
29	  --json                     Format --get / --list output as JSON.
30	  --dry-run                  Print actions but don't write.
31	  --help, -h                 Show this help and exit.
32	
33	Examples:
34	  check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
35	  check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
36	                       --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
37	  check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
38	  check-preferences.sh --list --json
39	
40	Exit codes:
41	  0  success (key absent on --get is also success — empty stdout)
42	  1  invalid arguments
43	  2  file/dir not accessible
44	  3  yq missing or yq error
45	EOF
46	}
47	
48	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }

2	# check-preferences.sh — Read, set, or reset .skills/preferences.yaml.
3	#
4	# Per-repo preferences for skills that need to remember user decisions across

9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	usage() {
12	  cat <<'EOF'
13	Usage: check-preferences.sh [OPTIONS]
14	
15	Read, write, or reset entries in .skills/preferences.yaml (per-repo).
16	
17	Options:
18	  --get KEY                  Print the value at KEY (e.g., mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled).
19	                             Prints empty string + exits 0 if absent.
20	  --set KEY=VALUE            Set a key. Repeatable. VALUE is parsed as YAML
21	                             (so 'true', '42', '2026-04-23', and bare strings
22	                             all work). Quote complex values.
23	  --reset NAMESPACE          Delete the entire top-level NAMESPACE key (returns
24	                             that skill to "never asked" state).
25	  --list                     Print the entire file (or "(empty)" if missing).
26	  --file PATH                Override file location (default: .skills/preferences.yaml
27	                             at the current Git worktree root, or in the current
28	                             directory when outside Git).
29	  --json                     Format --get / --list output as JSON.
30	  --dry-run                  Print actions but don't write.
31	  --help, -h                 Show this help and exit.
32	
33	Examples:
34	  check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
35	  check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
36	                       --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
37	  check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
38	  check-preferences.sh --list --json
39	
40	Exit codes:
41	  0  success (key absent on --get is also success — empty stdout)
42	  1  invalid arguments
43	  2  file/dir not accessible
44	  3  yq missing or yq error
45	EOF
46	}
47	
48	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
49	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
50	
51	# --- arg parsing ---
52	ACTION=""
53	KEY=""
54	NAMESPACE=""
55	FILE=""
56	JSON=0
57	DRY_RUN=0
58	SET_PAIRS=()
59	
60	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
61	  case "$1" in
62	    --get)        ACTION="get"; KEY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
63	    --set)        ACTION="set"; SET_PAIRS+=("${2:-}"); shift 2 ;;
64	    --reset)      ACTION="reset"; NAMESPACE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
65	    --list)       ACTION="list"; shift ;;
66	    --file)       FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
67	    --json)       JSON=1; shift ;;
68	    --dry-run)    DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
69	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
70	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
71	    *)            die "unexpected positional argument: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
72	  esac
73	done
74	
75	[ -n "$ACTION" ] || die "must specify one of --get/--set/--reset/--list (try --help)" 1
76	
77	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "yq not found in PATH (install: brew install yq)" 3
78	
79	# --- file resolution ---
80	if [ -z "$FILE" ]; then
81	  if ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; then
82	    :
83	  else
84	    ROOT="$(pwd)"
85	  fi
86	  FILE="$ROOT/.skills/preferences.yaml"
87	fi
88	
89	ensure_file() {
90	  local dir
91	  dir="$(dirname "$FILE")"
92	  if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
93	    [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ] && { log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $dir"; return 0; }
94	    mkdir -p "$dir"
95	  fi
96	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
97	    [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ] && { log "[dry-run] touch $FILE with header"; return 0; }
98	    cat >"$FILE" <<'EOF'
99	# .skills/preferences.yaml
100	# Per-repo preferences recorded by skills. Each top-level key is a skill
101	# namespace. See:
102	#   skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/preferences-schema.md
103	EOF
104	  fi
105	}
106	
107	# --- actions ---
108	case "$ACTION" in
109	
110	get)
111	  [ -n "$KEY" ] || die "--get requires KEY" 1
112	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
113	    if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then printf 'null\n'; fi
114	    exit 0
115	  fi
116	  # yq prints "null" for missing; convert to empty string for shell-friendliness.
117	  VALUE=$(yq -r ".${KEY}" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "null")
118	  if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then
119	    yq -o=json ".${KEY}" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null || printf 'null\n'
120	  else
121	    if [ "$VALUE" = "null" ]; then
122	      printf ''
123	    else
124	      printf '%s\n' "$VALUE"
125	    fi
126	  fi
127	  ;;
128	
129	set)
130	  [ "${#SET_PAIRS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || die "--set requires at least one KEY=VALUE" 1
131	  ensure_file
132	
133	  # Build a single yq expression so we make one atomic write.
134	  EXPR=""
135	  for pair in "${SET_PAIRS[@]}"; do
136	    case "$pair" in
137	      *=*) ;;
138	      *) die "--set value must be KEY=VALUE (got '$pair')" 1 ;;
139	    esac
140	    k="${pair%%=*}"
141	    v="${pair#*=}"

143	    # Dates and everything else go through as strings (quoted) — yq treats
144	    # ISO-8601 unquoted as arithmetic / invalid expression.
145	    case "$v" in
146	      true|false|null) yv="$v" ;;
147	      \[*\]|\{*\}) yv="$v" ;;  # YAML flow sequence/mapping pass-through
148	      ''|*[!0-9]*) yv="\"${v//\"/\\\"}\"" ;;
149	      *) yv="$v" ;;
150	    esac
151	    if [ -z "$EXPR" ]; then
152	      EXPR=".${k} = ${yv}"
153	    else
154	      EXPR="${EXPR} | .${k} = ${yv}"
155	    fi
156	  done
157	
158	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
159	    log "[dry-run] yq -i '$EXPR' $FILE"
160	    exit 0
161	  fi
162	
163	  TMP="${FILE}.tmp.$$"
164	  yq "$EXPR" "$FILE" > "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; die "yq failed applying: $EXPR" 3; }
165	  mv "$TMP" "$FILE"
166	  log "Updated $FILE"
167	  ;;
168	
169	reset)
170	  [ -n "$NAMESPACE" ] || die "--reset requires NAMESPACE" 1
171	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
172	    log "Nothing to reset (file does not exist): $FILE"
173	    exit 0
174	  fi
175	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
176	    log "[dry-run] yq -i 'del(.${NAMESPACE})' $FILE"
177	    exit 0
178	  fi
179	  TMP="${FILE}.tmp.$$"
180	  yq "del(.${NAMESPACE})" "$FILE" > "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; die "yq failed deleting .${NAMESPACE}" 3; }
181	  mv "$TMP" "$FILE"
182	  log "Reset namespace .${NAMESPACE} in $FILE"
183	  ;;
184	
185	list)
186	  if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
187	    if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then printf '{}\n'; else printf '(empty: %s)\n' "$FILE"; fi
188	    exit 0
189	  fi
190	  if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then
191	    yq -o=json '.' "$FILE"

193	    cat "$FILE"
194	  fi

197	esac

9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.

11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
22	- User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
23	  applied to a new project
24	- User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
25	- User asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual",
26	  "add Traditional Chinese", "add zh-TW", "translate the docs", or to add
27	  any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7
28	
29	## When NOT to trigger
30	
31	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
32	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
33	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
34	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
35	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
36	
37	## Workflow
38	
39	### 1. Read preferences first
40	
41	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
42	decision:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
46	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
47	```
48	
49	Possible states:
50	
51	| State | Meaning | What to do |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
54	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
55	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
56	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
57	
58	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
59	
60	Ask the user explicitly:
61	
62	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
63	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
64	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
65	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
66	
67	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
68	
69	```bash
70	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
71	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
72	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
73	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
74	```
75	
76	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
77	future invocations.
78	
79	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
80	
81	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
82	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
83	the short version:
84	
85	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
86	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
87	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
88	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
89	  with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
90	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
91	  explicit, alphabetical nav;
92	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
93	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
94	
95	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
96	
97	### 4. Scaffold
98	
99	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
100	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
101	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
102	copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
103	`.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
104	`--social` is on.
105	
106	```bash
107	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
108	  --site-name "My Project" \
109	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
110	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
111	```
112	
113	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
114	files unless `--force` is passed.
115	
116	Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
117	are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
118	the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
119	
120	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
121	
122	```bash
123	uv sync --extra docs
124	uv run mkdocs build --strict
125	```
126	
127	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
128	
129	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
130	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
131	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
132	Only proceed on explicit yes.
133	
134	```bash
135	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
136	  --repo owner/repo
137	```
138	
139	Flags:
140	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
141	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
142	
143	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
144	in preferences.
145	
146	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
147	
148	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
149	`mkdocs.yml`:
150	
151	```bash
152	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
153	  --section workflows \
154	  --title "My new workflow" \
155	  --slug my-new-workflow
156	```
157	
158	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
159	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
160	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
161	
162	If the project has additional languages configured in
163	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
164	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
165	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
166	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
167	
168	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
169	
170	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
171	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
172	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
173	
174	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
175	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
176	
177	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
178	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
179	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
180	
181	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
182	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
183	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
184	`Makefile` for you):
185	
186	```bash
187	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
188	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
189	```
190	
191	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
192	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
193	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
194	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
195	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
196	is a no-op.
197	
198	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
199	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
200	
201	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
202	
203	```bash
204	uv sync --extra docs
205	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
206	```
207	
208	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
209	
210	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
211	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
212	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
213	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
214	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
215	canonical).
216	
217	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
218	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
219	
220	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
221	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
222	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
223	> invent translations)."
224	
225	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
226	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
227	
228	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
229	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
230	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
231	user may want one without the other.

235	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
236	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.

238	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
239	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.

242	  - Always appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to `.gitignore`,

312	## Gotchas
313	
314	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
315	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
316	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
317	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
318	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
319	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
320	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
321	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
322	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
323	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
324	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
325	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
326	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
327	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
328	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
329	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
330	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
331	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
332	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
333	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
334	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
335	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
336	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
337	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
338	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
339	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
340	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
341	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
342	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
343	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
344	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
345	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
346	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
347	  `select()` form.
348	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
349	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
350	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
351	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
352	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
353	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
354	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
355	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
356	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
357	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
358	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
359	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
360	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
361	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
362	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
363	  Counter-intuitive name.
364	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
365	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
366	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
367	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
368	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
369	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
370	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
371	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
372	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
373	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
374	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
375	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
376	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
377	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
378	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
379	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
380	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
381	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
382	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
383	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
384	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
385	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
386	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
387	  is just acting on it.
388	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
389	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
390	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
391	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
392	
393	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
394	
395	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
396	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
397	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
398	have customizations the templates don't know about.
399
```

```text
1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
36	  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
37	  pages.)
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
46	  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
47	  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
48	  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
49	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
50	  deterministic alphabetical order.
51	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
52	  content is already there.
53	
54	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
55	
56	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
57	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
58	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
59	  has been asked once.
60	
61	## What "non-hidden files" means
62	
63	For the purposes of this check:
64	
65	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
66	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
67	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
68	  "no existing content".
69	
70	Implementation hint:
71	
72	```bash
73	find docs -type f \
74	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
75	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
76	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
77	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
78	  | head -50
79	```
80	
81	## Things this skill must NOT do
82	
83	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
84	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
85	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
86	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
87	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
88	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
89	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
90	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
91	  breaks rendering.
92	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
93	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
94	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
95	
96	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
97	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
98	
99	## After bootstrap
100	
101	Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
102	for option a) and report:
103	
104	- Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
105	- Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
106	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
107	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
108	
109	## Recording the decision
110	
111	```bash
112	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
113	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
114	```
115	
116	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
117	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).
118
```
</details></tool-use>

214	      inside = 1
215	      while ((getline line < replacement) > 0) print line
216	      close(replacement)

220	    !inside { print }
221	    END {
222	      if (inside || begin_count != 1 || end_count != 1) exit 2
223	    }

 ## Decision tree
 
 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
 
 ```
 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
 │         on the existing site.
 └── NO  → continue
     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
 ```
 
 ## Three options to present
 
 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
 for an honest consent gate.
 
 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
 
 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
   `docs/` untouched**.
-- The generated `mkdocs.yml` will have `docs_dir: docs` pointing at their
-  files and an **empty** `nav:` so MkDocs auto-generates the nav from the
-  filesystem.
+- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
+  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
+  pages.)
 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
 
 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
 
-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing markdown files into an
-  explicit `nav:` block** so the user can see/reorder them later.
-- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to
-  pick a reasonable initial order (alphabetical by default).
+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
+  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
+  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
+  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
+- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
+  deterministic alphabetical order.

 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
 
 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
   has been asked once.
 
 ## What "non-hidden files" means
 
 For the purposes of this check:
 
 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
   "no existing content".

12	#      page, with the terminology-rule admonition pre-injected.
13	#   4. Records the choice in .skills/preferences.yaml.
14	#   5. Un-comments mkdocs-static-i18n in pyproject.toml if it's commented out.
15	
16	set -euo pipefail
17	
18	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
19	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
20	ASSETS="$SKILL_DIR/assets"
21	
22	usage() {
23	  cat <<'EOF'
24	Usage: add-language.sh --lang LANG [OPTIONS]
25	
26	Retrofit a non-default language into an existing MkDocs site (uses
27	mkdocs-static-i18n with docs_structure: suffix).
28	
29	Required:
30	  --lang LANG          Language code to add (e.g. zh-TW, ja, fr, de).
31	
32	Options:
33	  --name NAME          Display name (default: derived from LANG, e.g.
34	                       zh-TW → "繁體中文 (zh-TW)"). Falls back to LANG.
35	  --default-lang LANG  Default language already on the site (default: en).
36	                       Used to seed theme.language and i18n.languages[0].
37	  --target-dir DIR     Repo root (default: walk up from CWD looking for mkdocs.yml).
38	  --no-stubs           Skip creating *.<LANG>.md sibling stubs.
39	  --remove-llmstxt     Remove the mkdocs-llmstxt plugin entry from mkdocs.yml.
40	                       Default behaviour KEEPS llmstxt because /llms.txt is the
41	                       LLM-friendly feature most users wanted in the first place.
42	                       Trade-off: llmstxt's source-path lookups break under
43	                       mkdocs-static-i18n's reconfigure_material, so 'mkdocs
44	                       build --strict' aborts with "Page URI not found" warnings.
45	                       Pair --remove-llmstxt with keeping --strict; OR keep
46	                       llmstxt (default) and pass --drop-strict to patch your
47	                       CI/Makefile so the build doesn't fail on warnings.
48	  --drop-strict        Patch .github/workflows/docs.yml and Makefile to remove
49	                       '--strict' from any 'mkdocs build --strict' invocation.
50	                       Use when keeping llmstxt with i18n. Idempotent.
51	  --dry-run            Print actions without writing.
52	  --force              Overwrite existing *.<LANG>.md stubs (default: skip).
53	  --help, -h           Show this help and exit.
54	
55	Examples:
56	  add-language.sh --lang zh-TW                              # add Traditional Chinese
57	  add-language.sh --lang ja --name "日本語"                 # add Japanese with custom name
58	  add-language.sh --lang zh-TW --dry-run                    # preview changes
59	  add-language.sh --lang fr --no-stubs                      # plugin only, no stubs
60	
61	Exit codes:
62	  0  success
63	  1  invalid arguments
64	  2  mkdocs.yml not found
65	  3  refusing to overwrite (use --force)
66	  4  yq error
67	EOF
68	}
69	
70	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
71	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
72	
73	LOCALE=""
74	LOCALE_NAME=""
75	DEFAULT_LANG="en"
76	TARGET=""
77	NO_STUBS=0
78	REMOVE_LLMSTXT=0
79	DROP_STRICT=0
80	DRY_RUN=0
81	FORCE=0
82	
83	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
84	  case "$1" in
85	    --lang)            LOCALE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
86	    --name)            LOCALE_NAME="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
87	    --default-lang)    DEFAULT_LANG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
88	    --target-dir)      TARGET="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
89	    --no-stubs)        NO_STUBS=1; shift ;;
90	    --remove-llmstxt)  REMOVE_LLMSTXT=1; shift ;;
91	    --drop-strict)     DROP_STRICT=1; shift ;;
92	    --dry-run)         DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
93	    --force)           FORCE=1; shift ;;
94	    --help|-h)         usage; exit 0 ;;
95	    -*)                die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
96	    *)                 die "unexpected positional argument: $1" 1 ;;
97	  esac
98	done
99	
100	[ -n "$LOCALE" ] || die "--lang is required (try --help)" 1
101	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "yq not found in PATH (install: brew install yq)" 4
102	
103	# --- Locate mkdocs.yml ---
104	if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
105	  cur="$(pwd)"
106	  while [ "$cur" != "/" ]; do
107	    if [ -f "$cur/mkdocs.yml" ]; then TARGET="$cur"; break; fi
108	    cur="$(dirname "$cur")"
109	  done
110	  [ -n "$TARGET" ] || die "could not find mkdocs.yml walking up from $(pwd)" 2
111	fi
112	MKDOCS="$TARGET/mkdocs.yml"
113	[ -f "$MKDOCS" ] || die "no mkdocs.yml in $TARGET" 2
114	DOCS_DIR="$TARGET/docs"
115	
116	# --- Derive display name if not given ---
117	if [ -z "$LOCALE_NAME" ]; then
118	  case "$LOCALE" in
119	    zh-TW) LOCALE_NAME="繁體中文 (zh-TW)" ;;
120	    zh-CN) LOCALE_NAME="简体中文 (zh-CN)" ;;
121	    ja)    LOCALE_NAME="日本語 (ja)" ;;
122	    ko)    LOCALE_NAME="한국어 (ko)" ;;
123	    fr)    LOCALE_NAME="Français (fr)" ;;
124	    de)    LOCALE_NAME="Deutsch (de)" ;;
125	    es)    LOCALE_NAME="Español (es)" ;;
126	    pt)    LOCALE_NAME="Português (pt)" ;;
127	    it)    LOCALE_NAME="Italiano (it)" ;;
128	    en)    LOCALE_NAME="English" ;;
129	    *)     LOCALE_NAME="$LOCALE" ;;
130	  esac
131	fi
132	
133	DEFAULT_NAME="English"
134	[ "$DEFAULT_LANG" = "en" ] || DEFAULT_NAME="$DEFAULT_LANG"
135	
136	log "Target: $TARGET"
137	log "Locale: $LOCALE ($LOCALE_NAME)"
138	log "Default language: $DEFAULT_LANG"
139	
140	# --- Detect current i18n state ---
141	HAS_I18N=$(yq '[.plugins[]? | select(type == "!!map") | keys | .[0]] | contains(["i18n"])' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
142	HAS_LOCALE="false"
143	if [ "$HAS_I18N" = "true" ]; then
144	  HAS_LOCALE=$(LOC="$LOCALE" yq '[.plugins[]? | select(has("i18n")) | .i18n.languages[].locale] | contains([env(LOC)])' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
145	fi
146	
147	log "i18n plugin present: $HAS_I18N"
148	log "Locale already configured: $HAS_LOCALE"
149	
150	# --- yq write helper ---
151	yq_inplace() {
152	  local expr="$1"
153	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
154	    log "[dry-run] yq -i '$expr' $MKDOCS"
155	    return 0
156	  fi
157	  local tmp="${MKDOCS}.tmp.$$"
158	  yq "$expr" "$MKDOCS" > "$tmp" || { rm -f "$tmp"; die "yq failed: $expr" 4; }
159	  mv "$tmp" "$MKDOCS"
160	}
161	
162	# --- Step 1: insert / extend plugins.i18n ---
163	if [ "$HAS_I18N" = "false" ]; then
164	  log "Inserting plugins.i18n block..."
165	  yq_inplace "
166	    .plugins = (
167	      [{
168	        \"i18n\": {
169	          \"docs_structure\": \"suffix\",
170	          \"fallback_to_default\": true,
171	          \"reconfigure_material\": true,
172	          \"reconfigure_search\": true,
173	          \"languages\": [
174	            {\"locale\": \"$DEFAULT_LANG\", \"name\": \"$DEFAULT_NAME\", \"default\": true},
175	            {\"locale\": \"$LOCALE\", \"name\": \"$LOCALE_NAME\"}
176	          ]
177	        }
178	      }] + (.plugins // [])
179	    )
180	  "
181	elif [ "$HAS_LOCALE" = "false" ]; then
182	  log "Appending $LOCALE to existing plugins.i18n.languages..."
183	  yq_inplace "
184	    (.plugins[] | select(has(\"i18n\")) | .i18n.languages)
185	      += [{\"locale\": \"$LOCALE\", \"name\": \"$LOCALE_NAME\"}]
186	  "
187	else
188	  log "Locale $LOCALE already in plugins.i18n.languages — no plugin change."
189	fi
190	
191	# --- Step 2: set theme.language if missing ---
192	THEME_LANG=$(yq -r '.theme.language // ""' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
193	if [ -z "$THEME_LANG" ]; then
194	  log "Setting theme.language: $DEFAULT_LANG"
195	  yq_inplace ".theme.language = \"$DEFAULT_LANG\""
196	elif [ "$THEME_LANG" != "$DEFAULT_LANG" ]; then
197	  log "Note: theme.language is already '$THEME_LANG' (not '$DEFAULT_LANG'). Leaving as-is."
198	fi
199	
200	# --- Step 2a: give the social plugin a CJK-capable card font ---
201	# The `social` plugin's default card font (Roboto) is Latin-only, so CJK page
202	# titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on the generated OG cards. If we're adding
203	# a CJK language AND the social plugin is present, set a Noto Sans <script>
204	# font_family — these cover Latin + CJK + arrows + fullwidth punctuation.
205	# Only sets it when unset, so a user's explicit choice is never overwritten.
206	case "$LOCALE" in
207	  zh-TW|zh-Hant*) SOCIAL_FONT="Noto Sans TC" ;;
208	  zh-CN|zh-Hans*|zh) SOCIAL_FONT="Noto Sans SC" ;;
209	  ja*) SOCIAL_FONT="Noto Sans JP" ;;
210	  ko*) SOCIAL_FONT="Noto Sans KR" ;;
211	  *) SOCIAL_FONT="" ;;
212	esac
213	if [ -n "$SOCIAL_FONT" ]; then
214	  HAS_SOCIAL=$(yq '[.plugins[]? | select(has("social"))] | length > 0' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
215	  CUR_FONT=$(yq -r '(.plugins[]? | select(has("social")) | .social.cards_layout_options.font_family) // ""' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
216	  if [ "$HAS_SOCIAL" = "true" ] && [ -z "$CUR_FONT" ]; then
217	    log "Setting social card font_family: $SOCIAL_FONT (CJK-capable; avoids tofu titles)..."
218	    yq_inplace "
219	      (.plugins[] | select(has(\"social\")) | .social.cards_layout_options.font_family)
220	        = \"$SOCIAL_FONT\"
221	    "
222	  elif [ "$HAS_SOCIAL" = "true" ] && [ -n "$CUR_FONT" ]; then
223	    log "Note: social card font_family already '$CUR_FONT' — leaving as-is."
224	    log "  If $LOCALE titles show as boxes, switch it to '$SOCIAL_FONT'."
225	  fi
226	fi
227	
228	# --- Step 2b: drop theme features incompatible with mkdocs-static-i18n ---
229	# The plugin's contextual language switcher is incompatible with
230	# navigation.instant (DOM links injected via instant nav can't be rewritten
231	# per language). Removing navigation.instant on first i18n add.
232	HAS_INSTANT=$(yq '.theme.features // [] | contains(["navigation.instant"])' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
233	if [ "$HAS_INSTANT" = "true" ]; then
234	  log "Removing navigation.instant / navigation.instant.progress (incompatible with i18n language switcher)..."
235	  yq_inplace '.theme.features |= ((. // []) - ["navigation.instant", "navigation.instant.progress"])'
236	fi
237	
238	# --- Step 2c: handle mkdocs-llmstxt incompatibility ---
239	# mkdocs-llmstxt resolves source URIs against the page index, which
240	# mkdocs-static-i18n's reconfigure_material remaps. Result: every entry in
241	# llmstxt.sections triggers a "Page URI not found" warning, which aborts
242	# `mkdocs build --strict`. Auto-discovery isn't an option (sections: is
243	# required by the llmstxt schema).
244	# Default: KEEP llmstxt — most users opted into this skill BECAUSE of the
245	# /llms.txt feature. Pair with --drop-strict to neutralise the warnings in
246	# CI. --remove-llmstxt is the opt-out for users who'd rather keep --strict.
247	HAS_LLMSTXT=$(yq '[.plugins[]? | select(has("llmstxt"))] | length > 0' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
248	if [ "$HAS_LLMSTXT" = "true" ]; then
249	  if [ "$REMOVE_LLMSTXT" = "1" ]; then
250	    log "Removing mkdocs-llmstxt plugin entry (--remove-llmstxt)..."
251	    yq_inplace 'del(.plugins[] | select(has("llmstxt")))'
252	  else
253	    log "Keeping mkdocs-llmstxt (default). 'mkdocs build --strict' will fail"
254	    log "  with 'Page URI not found' warnings — pair with --drop-strict, or"
255	    log "  drop --strict from your CI manually."
256	  fi
257	fi
258	
259	# --- Step 2d: optionally drop --strict from CI files ---
260	if [ "$DROP_STRICT" = "1" ]; then
261	  for ci_file in "$TARGET/.github/workflows/docs.yml" "$TARGET/Makefile"; do
262	    [ -f "$ci_file" ] || continue
263	    if ! grep -q 'mkdocs build --strict' "$ci_file" 2>/dev/null; then
264	      continue
265	    fi
266	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
267	      log "[dry-run] drop --strict in $ci_file"
268	    else
269	      sed -i.bak -E 's|mkdocs build --strict|mkdocs build|g' "$ci_file"
270	      rm -f "${ci_file}.bak"
271	      log "Dropped --strict from $ci_file"
272	    fi
273	  done
274	fi
275	
276	# --- Step 3: collect all configured locales for stub-skipping ---
277	# Compute deterministically so dry-run shows the post-state, not the pre-state.
278	if [ "$HAS_LOCALE" = "true" ]; then
279	  ALL_LOCALES=$(yq '.plugins[]? | select(has("i18n")) | .i18n.languages[].locale' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')
280	elif [ "$HAS_I18N" = "true" ]; then
281	  OLD_LOCALES=$(yq '.plugins[]? | select(has("i18n")) | .i18n.languages[].locale' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')
282	  ALL_LOCALES="${OLD_LOCALES}${LOCALE}"
283	else
284	  ALL_LOCALES="$DEFAULT_LANG $LOCALE"
285	fi
286	log "All configured locales: $ALL_LOCALES"
287	
288	# --- Step 4: create *.LANG.md sibling stubs ---
289	STUBS_CREATED=0
290	STUBS_EXISTING=0
291	STUBS_SKIPPED=0
292	STUB_TEMPLATE="$ASSETS/translation-stub.md.template"
293	
294	if [ "$NO_STUBS" = "1" ]; then
295	  log "Skipping stub creation (--no-stubs)."
296	elif [ ! -d "$DOCS_DIR" ]; then
297	  log "No docs/ dir — skipping stub creation."
298	elif [ ! -f "$STUB_TEMPLATE" ]; then
299	  die "stub template missing: $STUB_TEMPLATE" 4
300	else
301	  TMP_LIST="$(mktemp)"
302	  find "$DOCS_DIR" -type f -name '*.md' \
303	    -not -path "$DOCS_DIR/_snippets/*" \
304	    -not -path "$DOCS_DIR/assets/*" \
305	    > "$TMP_LIST" 2>/dev/null || true
306	
307	  while IFS= read -r src; do
308	    [ -z "$src" ] && continue
309	    base="${src%.md}"
310	    # Skip if this file is itself a locale-suffixed sibling.
311	    is_locale=0
312	    for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
313	      case "${base}" in
314	        *.$loc) is_locale=1; break ;;
315	      esac
316	    done
317	    [ "$is_locale" = "1" ] && { STUBS_SKIPPED=$((STUBS_SKIPPED + 1)); continue; }
318	
319	    target="${base}.${LOCALE}.md"
320	    if [ -e "$target" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
321	      STUBS_EXISTING=$((STUBS_EXISTING + 1))
322	      continue
323	    fi
324	
325	    # Extract title from source (first '# ' heading), fallback to filename.
326	    src_title=$(grep -m1 '^# ' "$src" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^# *//' || true)
327	    [ -n "$src_title" ] || src_title="$(basename "$src" .md)"
328	
329	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
330	      log "[dry-run] create $target  (title: $src_title)"
331	    else
332	      sed -e "s|{{PAGE_TITLE}}|${src_title}|g" \
333	          -e "s|{{LANG}}|${LOCALE}|g" \
334	          "$STUB_TEMPLATE" > "$target"
335	    fi
336	    STUBS_CREATED=$((STUBS_CREATED + 1))
337	  done < "$TMP_LIST"
338	  rm -f "$TMP_LIST"
339	fi
340	
341	log "Stubs: $STUBS_CREATED created, $STUBS_EXISTING already existed, $STUBS_SKIPPED skipped (locale-suffixed)"
342	
343	# --- Step 5: update preferences ---
344	PREFS="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/check-preferences.sh"
345	ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="["
346	first=1
347	for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
348	  [ -z "$loc" ] && continue
349	  if [ "$first" = "1" ]; then
350	    ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}\"$loc\""
351	    first=0
352	  else
353	    ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}, \"$loc\""
354	  fi
355	done
356	ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}]"
357	
358	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
359	  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=$ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL"
360	  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms=true"
361	  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure=suffix"
362	else
363	  bash "$PREFS" \
364	    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=$ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL" \
365	    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms=true" \
366	    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure=suffix" \
367	    >/dev/null
368	fi
369	
370	# --- Step 6: uncomment mkdocs-static-i18n in pyproject.toml ---
371	PYPROJECT="$TARGET/pyproject.toml"
372	if [ -f "$PYPROJECT" ]; then
373	  if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*"mkdocs-static-i18n' "$PYPROJECT"; then
374	    log "pyproject.toml already lists mkdocs-static-i18n — leaving alone."
375	  elif grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*"mkdocs-static-i18n' "$PYPROJECT"; then
376	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
377	      log "[dry-run] uncomment mkdocs-static-i18n in $PYPROJECT"
378	    else
379	      sed -i.bak -E 's|^([[:space:]]*)#[[:space:]]*("mkdocs-static-i18n[^"]*",)|\1\2|' "$PYPROJECT"
380	      rm -f "${PYPROJECT}.bak"
381	      log "Uncommented mkdocs-static-i18n in $PYPROJECT"
382	    fi
383	  else
384	    log "Note: mkdocs-static-i18n not found in $PYPROJECT. Add manually:"
385	    log '        "mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2",'
386	  fi
387	else

389	fi
390	
391	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
392	  log "Dry run complete."
393	  exit 0
394	fi
395	
396	# --- Structured success output ---
397	LANGUAGES_JSON=""
398	for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
399	  [ -z "$loc" ] && continue
400	  if [ -z "$LANGUAGES_JSON" ]; then
401	    LANGUAGES_JSON="\"$loc\""
402	  else
403	    LANGUAGES_JSON="$LANGUAGES_JSON,\"$loc\""
404	  fi
405	done
406	
407	printf '{"lang":"%s","stubs_created":%d,"stubs_existing":%d,"languages":[%s]}\n' \
408	  "$LOCALE" "$STUBS_CREATED" "$STUBS_EXISTING" "$LANGUAGES_JSON"
409	
410	# --- Post-run tips (stderr, agent-readable) ---
411	# These nudge the next step without taking action. The script's job is the
412	# structural retrofit; translation and nav-label decisions are deliberate
413	# authoring work that needs human judgment.
414	if [ "$STUBS_CREATED" -gt 0 ] || [ "$STUBS_EXISTING" -gt 0 ]; then
415	  log ""
416	  log "Next steps:"
417	  log "  1. Stubs are placeholders. Each $LOCALE page contains the terminology"
418	  log "     admonition + a 'Translation pending' warning, and is otherwise empty."
419	  log "     Ask the user whether to translate them page-by-page now"
420	  log "     (recommended batch size: 4-6 pages, run 'mkdocs build' between batches)."
421	  log "     Translation is a separate authoring task — proceed only on explicit yes."
422	  log ""
423	  log "  2. Section headings in mkdocs.yml's nav stay in the default language."
424	  log "     To translate them (e.g. 'Reference' -> '參考資料'), add a"
425	  log "     nav_translations: block under the $LOCALE entry in mkdocs.yml."
426	  log "     See references/i18n-guide.md §nav_translations."
427	fi

18	
19	Options:

52	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }

55	SECTION=""
56	TITLE=""
57	SLUG=""
58	TEMPLATE=""
59	TARGET=""
60	LANG_ONLY=""

63	
64	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do

313	#!/usr/bin/env bash
314	if [ -n "${GIT_INDEX_FILE:-}" ] && [ ! -e "$RACE_SYNC/inside-transaction" ]; then

317	fi

319	SH
320	chmod +x "$race_bin/git"
321	index_path="$(HOME="$FAKE_HOME" git -C "$repo_race" rev-parse --git-path index)"
322	case "$index_path" in /*) ;; *) index_path="$repo_race/$index_path" ;; esac
323	(
324	  cd "$repo_race" || exit 1
325	  PATH="$race_bin:$SYSTEM_PATH" REAL_GIT="$real_git" RACE_SYNC="$race_sync" HOME="$FAKE_HOME" \
326	    "$BASH" "$STAGE" --session-only --session-id "$UUID_C" --plan '.claude/plans/plan.md'
327	) >"$BASE/race-stage-out" 2>"$BASE/race-stage-err" &
328	race_pid=$!
329	race_wait=0
330	while [ ! -e "$race_sync/inside-transaction" ] && [ "$race_wait" -lt 500 ]; do
331	  sleep 0.02
332	  race_wait=$((race_wait + 1))
333	done
334	git -C "$repo_race" restore --staged feature.txt >/dev/null 2>"$BASE/race-writer-err"
335	concurrent_rc=$?

337	wait "$race_pid"
338	race_stage_rc=$?
339	race_names="$(staged_names "$repo_race")"
340	leftover_temp="$(find "$(dirname "$index_path")" -maxdepth 1 -name "$(basename "$index_path").agent-history.*" -print -quit)"
341	if [ "$race_stage_rc" = "0" ] && [ "$concurrent_rc" != "0" ] && \
342	   contains "$race_names" 'feature.txt' && contains "$race_names" '.specstory/history/session.md' && \
343	   contains "$race_names" '.claude/plans/plan.md' && [ ! -e "$index_path.lock" ] && \
344	   [ -z "$leftover_temp" ]; then

346	else
347	  fail "index lock prevents concurrent writer across staged guard and exact add"
348	fi
349	
350	# Broad mode must stage unstaged deletion and rename pairs from one porcelain

353	mkdir -p "$repo_status/.specstory/history" "$repo_status/.claude/plans"
354	printf '# delete me\n' > "$repo_status/.specstory/history/deleted.md"
355	printf '# rename me\n' > "$repo_status/.claude/plans/old-name.md"
356	git -C "$repo_status" add .specstory/history/deleted.md .claude/plans/old-name.md
357	git -C "$repo_status" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com \
358	  commit -q -m artifacts
359	printf '%s\n' changed >> "$repo_status/feature.txt"
360	git -C "$repo_status" add feature.txt
361	rm "$repo_status/.specstory/history/deleted.md"

363	run_stage "$repo_status"
364	name_status="$(git -C "$repo_status" diff --cached --name-status --find-renames)"

366	   contains "$name_status" $'R100\t.claude/plans/old-name.md\t.claude/plans/new-name.md'; then
367	  pass "broad snapshot stages deleted and paired renamed artifacts"
368	else
369	  fail "broad snapshot stages deleted and paired renamed artifacts"
370	fi
371	
372	# A staged artifact-only rename plus an unstaged modification produces an RM
373	# porcelain pair. Its origin is metadata, not a fake non-artifact feature path.
374	repo_origin="$(make_repo 'rename origin guard')"
375	mkdir -p "$repo_origin/.claude/plans"
376	printf '# original\n' > "$repo_origin/.claude/plans/old.md"
377	git -C "$repo_origin" add .claude/plans/old.md

379	  commit -q -m artifact

381	printf '%s\n' changed >> "$repo_origin/.claude/plans/new.md"

388	fi

390	# Neither broad nor exact mode may use git add to collapse an unmerged artifact
391	# into a stage-0 blob containing conflict markers.

393	conflict_transcript="$(write_transcript "$repo_artifact_conflict" 'conflict.md' "$UUID_A")"
394	printf '%s\n' base >> "$conflict_transcript"
395	git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" add .specstory/history/conflict.md
396	git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com \
397	  commit -q -m transcript
398	git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" checkout -q -b conflict-side
399	write_transcript "$repo_artifact_conflict" 'conflict.md' "$UUID_A" >/dev/null
400	printf '%s\n' side >> "$conflict_transcript"
401	git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" add .specstory/history/conflict.md
402	git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com \
403	  commit -q -m side
404	git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" checkout -q main
405	write_transcript "$repo_artifact_conflict" 'conflict.md' "$UUID_A" >/dev/null
406	printf '%s\n' main >> "$conflict_transcript"
407	git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" add .specstory/history/conflict.md
408	git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com \
409	  commit -q -m main

412	write_jsonl "$repo_artifact_conflict" "$UUID_A"
413	conflict_index_before="$(git -C "$repo_artifact_conflict" ls-files -s)"

415	broad_conflict_rc="$LAST_RC"

423	else
424	  fail "unmerged transcript is rejected without resolving the index"
425	fi
426	
427	# A code conflict is not a staged feature diff. It cannot authorize staging an
428	# otherwise addable artifact.

430	git -C "$repo_code_conflict" checkout -q -b code-side
431	printf '%s\n' side > "$repo_code_conflict/feature.txt"
432	git -C "$repo_code_conflict" add feature.txt
433	git -C "$repo_code_conflict" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com \
434	  commit -q -m side
435	git -C "$repo_code_conflict" checkout -q main
436	printf '%s\n' main > "$repo_code_conflict/feature.txt"
437	git -C "$repo_code_conflict" add feature.txt
438	git -C "$repo_code_conflict" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com \
439	  commit -q -m main
440	git -C "$repo_code_conflict" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null merge code-side >/dev/null 2>&1

443	code_conflict_before="$(git -C "$repo_code_conflict" ls-files -s)"

445	if [ "$LAST_RC" = "4" ] && [ "$(git -C "$repo_code_conflict" ls-files -s)" = "$code_conflict_before" ] && \

450	  fail "unmerged code does not satisfy the staged feature guard"
451	fi
452	
453	# Historical broad mode remains available and stages every dirty Markdown
454	# artifact under configured directories without requiring exact headers.
455	repo_broad="$(make_repo 'broad compatibility')"
456	printf '%s\n' changed >> "$repo_broad/feature.txt"

469	  fail "broad branch-wide compatibility mode stages all dirty artifacts"
470	fi

472	printf '\n== bootstrap exact hook ==\n'
473	
474	# Install with a local no-op pre-commit executable so the test never downloads.

483	chmod +x "$failing_bin/pre-commit"

533	# A normal commit with only feature code staged must fail validation without

537	commit_count_before="$(git -C "$repo_hook" rev-list --count HEAD)"
538	index_before_commit="$(git -C "$repo_hook" ls-files -s)"
539	(cd "$repo_hook" && HOME="$FAKE_HOME" PATH="$SYSTEM_PATH" AGENT_HISTORY_SESSION_ID="$UUID_C" \
540	  AGENT_HISTORY_SPECSTORY_PATH='.specstory/history/hook session.md' \
541	  AGENT_HISTORY_PLAN='.claude/plans/hook plan.md' \
542	  git -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com commit -m 'test: validation hook') \

546	if [ "$missing_commit_rc" != "0" ] && \

551	else
552	  fail "normal commit rejects unstaged artifacts without index mutation"
553	fi
554	
555	run_stage "$repo_hook" --session-only --session-id "$UUID_C" \
556	  --specstory-path '.specstory/history/hook session.md' \
557	  --plan '.claude/plans/hook plan.md'
558	(cd "$repo_hook" && HOME="$FAKE_HOME" PATH="$SYSTEM_PATH" AGENT_HISTORY_SESSION_ID="$UUID_C" \

570	  fail "normal commit succeeds after explicit exact staging"
571	fi

573	# `commit -a` prepares a temporary index with tracked code but excludes untracked

583	commit_a_count="$(git -C "$repo_commit_a" rev-list --count HEAD)"
584	(cd "$repo_commit_a" && HOME="$FAKE_HOME" PATH="$SYSTEM_PATH" AGENT_HISTORY_SESSION_ID="$UUID_A" \

596	# `commit --only` can exclude artifacts that are staged in the real index. The

623	  git -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com commit -m 'test: normal after only') \

628	else
629	  fail "normal commit succeeds after commit --only validation failure"

632	# Relative .git/hooks works in the primary checkout but becomes non-traversable
633	# in a linked worktree where .git is a file. Prove the asymmetry with real
634	# commits, then require bootstrap to refuse both checkouts.

645	printf '%s\n' primary >> "$repo_relative_hooks/feature.txt"

648	primary_relative_commit_rc=$?

660	if [ "$primary_relative_commit_rc" = "0" ] && [ "$linked_relative_commit_rc" = "0" ] && \

662	   [ "$linked_bootstrap_rc" = "6" ]; then

665	  fail "relative core.hooksPath is refused after primary/linked commit probe"
666	fi

668	repo_empty_hooks="$(make_repo 'empty hooks path')"

671	  "$BASH" "$BOOTSTRAP" --install-hook --dry-run) \
672	  >"$BASE/empty-hooks-out" 2>"$BASE/empty-hooks-err"
673	empty_hooks_rc=$?
674	empty_hooks_output="$(<"$BASE/empty-hooks-out")$(<"$BASE/empty-hooks-err")"

678	else
679	  fail "configured-empty core.hooksPath fails before constructing a root hook path"
680	fi
681	
682	repo_global="$(make_repo 'global hooks path')"
683	git -C "$repo_global" config core.hooksPath .githooks

690	  fail "global core.hooksPath refusal remains pre-write"

67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
76	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
77	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
78	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
79	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
80	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
81	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
82	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
83	
84	Active series in this repo:
85	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
86	
87	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
88	
89	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
90	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
91	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
92	
93	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
94	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
95	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
96	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
97	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
98	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
99	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
100	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
101	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
102	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
103	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
104	
105	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
106	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.

108	## Marketplace Catalog
109	
110	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
111	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
112	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
113	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
114	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
115	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
116	for the full mechanism.
117	
118	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
119	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
120	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
121	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
122	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
123	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
124	
125	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
126	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
127	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
128	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
129	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
130	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
131	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
132	within-group caveat in
133	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).

136	
137	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.

140	
141	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
142	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
143	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
144	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
145	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.

148	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
149	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
150	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
151	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
152	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
153	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
154	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
155	
156	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
157	
158	```bash
159	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
160	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
161	
162	# …or remove them afterward
163	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
164	```

166	## Project Memory Workflow
167	
168	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
169	
170	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
171	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
172	
173	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
174	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
175	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
176	
177	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
178	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
179	
180	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
181	
182	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
183	
184	   ```bash
185	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
186	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
187	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
188	   ```
189	
190	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
191	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
192	
193	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
194	
195	   ```bash
196	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
197	   ```
198	
199	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
200	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
201	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
202	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
203	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
204	
205	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
206	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
207	   afterwards to catch drift.
208	
209	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
210	
211	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
212	
213	```bash
214	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"

3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
8	
9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash

15	make sync
16

19

31	# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
32	make lint-frontmatter

35	# CI additionally runs `make native-marketplace-smoke` with pinned CLIs.

66	
67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
76	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
77	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
78	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
79	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
80	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
81	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
82	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
83	
84	Active series in this repo:
85	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
86	
87	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
88	
89	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
90	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
91	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
92	
93	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
94	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
95	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
96	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
97	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
98	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
99	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
100	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
101	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
102	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
103	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
104	
105	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
106	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
107

109	
110	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
111	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
112	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
113	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from

115	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
116	for the full mechanism.
117	
118	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the

120	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
121	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
122	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
123	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
124	
125	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
126	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
127	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a

174	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`

 # --- helper: copy template, refusing to overwrite unless --force ---

   local src="$1" dst="$2"

     die "exists, refusing to overwrite: $dst (use --force)" 3
   fi
   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then

     return 0
   fi

 # --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
 # With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
 # (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
 # marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
 expand_marker() {
   local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
   [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
     log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"
     return 0
   fi
   if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
     [ -f "$snippet" ] || die "social snippet missing: $snippet" 4
     awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
       index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
       { print }
     ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
   else
     awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
