1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# add-language.sh — Retrofit a non-default language into an existing MkDocs site.
3	#
4	# Bash 3.2 compatible. Requires `yq` (mikefarah/yq v4+).
5	# Idempotent: re-running with the same --lang is a no-op.
6	#
7	# What it does (see references/i18n-guide.md for the full story):
8	#   1. Inserts (or augments) a `plugins.i18n` block in mkdocs.yml using
9	#      docs_structure: suffix.
10	#   2. Sets theme.language to the default language if not already set.
11	#   3. Creates *.<LANG>.md sibling stubs for every existing default-language
12	#      page, with the terminology-rule admonition pre-injected.
13	#   4. Records the choice in .skills/preferences.yaml.
14	#   5. Un-comments mkdocs-static-i18n in pyproject.toml if it's commented out.
15	
16	set -euo pipefail
17	
18	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
19	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
20	ASSETS="$SKILL_DIR/assets"
21	
22	usage() {
23	  cat <<'EOF'
24	Usage: add-language.sh --lang LANG [OPTIONS]
25	
26	Retrofit a non-default language into an existing MkDocs site (uses
27	mkdocs-static-i18n with docs_structure: suffix).
28	
29	Required:
30	  --lang LANG          Language code to add (e.g. zh-TW, ja, fr, de).
31	
32	Options:
33	  --name NAME          Display name (default: derived from LANG, e.g.
34	                       zh-TW → "繁體中文 (zh-TW)"). Falls back to LANG.
35	  --default-lang LANG  Default language already on the site (default: en).
36	                       Used to seed theme.language and i18n.languages[0].
37	  --target-dir DIR     Repo root (default: walk up from CWD looking for mkdocs.yml).
38	  --no-stubs           Skip creating *.<LANG>.md sibling stubs.
39	  --remove-llmstxt     Remove the mkdocs-llmstxt plugin entry from mkdocs.yml.
40	                       Default behaviour KEEPS llmstxt because /llms.txt is the
41	                       LLM-friendly feature most users wanted in the first place.
42	                       Trade-off: llmstxt's source-path lookups break under
43	                       mkdocs-static-i18n's reconfigure_material, so 'mkdocs
44	                       build --strict' aborts with "Page URI not found" warnings.
45	                       Pair --remove-llmstxt with keeping --strict; OR keep
46	                       llmstxt (default) and pass --drop-strict to patch your
47	                       CI/Makefile so the build doesn't fail on warnings.
48	  --drop-strict        Patch .github/workflows/docs.yml and Makefile to remove
49	                       '--strict' from any 'mkdocs build --strict' invocation.
50	                       Use when keeping llmstxt with i18n. Idempotent.
51	  --dry-run            Print actions without writing.
52	  --force              Overwrite existing *.<LANG>.md stubs (default: skip).
53	  --help, -h           Show this help and exit.
54	
55	Examples:
56	  add-language.sh --lang zh-TW                              # add Traditional Chinese
57	  add-language.sh --lang ja --name "日本語"                 # add Japanese with custom name
58	  add-language.sh --lang zh-TW --dry-run                    # preview changes
59	  add-language.sh --lang fr --no-stubs                      # plugin only, no stubs
60	
61	Exit codes:
62	  0  success
63	  1  invalid arguments
64	  2  mkdocs.yml not found
65	  3  refusing to overwrite (use --force)
66	  4  yq error
67	EOF
68	}
69	
70	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
71	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
72

74	LOCALE_NAME=""
75	DEFAULT_LANG="en"
76	TARGET=""

78	REMOVE_LLMSTXT=0
79	DROP_STRICT=0

81	FORCE=0

251	    yq_inplace 'del(.plugins[] | select(has("llmstxt")))'
252	  else
253	    log "Keeping mkdocs-llmstxt (default). 'mkdocs build --strict' will fail"
254	    log "  with 'Page URI not found' warnings — pair with --drop-strict, or"
255	    log "  drop --strict from your CI manually."
256	  fi
257	fi
258	
259	# --- Step 2d: optionally drop --strict from CI files ---
260	if [ "$DROP_STRICT" = "1" ]; then
261	  for ci_file in "$TARGET/.github/workflows/docs.yml" "$TARGET/Makefile"; do
262	    [ -f "$ci_file" ] || continue
263	    if ! grep -q 'mkdocs build --strict' "$ci_file" 2>/dev/null; then
264	      continue
265	    fi
266	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
267	      log "[dry-run] drop --strict in $ci_file"
268	    else
269	      sed -i.bak -E 's|mkdocs build --strict|mkdocs build|g' "$ci_file"
270	      rm -f "${ci_file}.bak"
271	      log "Dropped --strict from $ci_file"
272	    fi
273	  done
274	fi
275	
276	# --- Step 3: collect all configured locales for stub-skipping ---
277	# Compute deterministically so dry-run shows the post-state, not the pre-state.
278	if [ "$HAS_LOCALE" = "true" ]; then
279	  ALL_LOCALES=$(yq '.plugins[]? | select(has("i18n")) | .i18n.languages[].locale' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')
280	elif [ "$HAS_I18N" = "true" ]; then
281	  OLD_LOCALES=$(yq '.plugins[]? | select(has("i18n")) | .i18n.languages[].locale' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')
282	  ALL_LOCALES="${OLD_LOCALES}${LOCALE}"
283	else
284	  ALL_LOCALES="$DEFAULT_LANG $LOCALE"
285	fi
286	log "All configured locales: $ALL_LOCALES"
287	
288	# --- Step 4: create *.LANG.md sibling stubs ---
289	STUBS_CREATED=0
290	STUBS_EXISTING=0
291	STUBS_SKIPPED=0
292	STUB_TEMPLATE="$ASSETS/translation-stub.md.template"
293	
294	if [ "$NO_STUBS" = "1" ]; then
295	  log "Skipping stub creation (--no-stubs)."
296	elif [ ! -d "$DOCS_DIR" ]; then
297	  log "No docs/ dir — skipping stub creation."
298	elif [ ! -f "$STUB_TEMPLATE" ]; then
299	  die "stub template missing: $STUB_TEMPLATE" 4
300	else
301	  TMP_LIST="$(mktemp)"
302	  find "$DOCS_DIR" -type f -name '*.md' \
303	    -not -path "$DOCS_DIR/_snippets/*" \
304	    -not -path "$DOCS_DIR/assets/*" \
305	    > "$TMP_LIST" 2>/dev/null || true
306	
307	  while IFS= read -r src; do
308	    [ -z "$src" ] && continue
309	    base="${src%.md}"
310	    # Skip if this file is itself a locale-suffixed sibling.
311	    is_locale=0
312	    for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
313	      case "${base}" in
314	        *.$loc) is_locale=1; break ;;
315	      esac
316	    done
317	    [ "$is_locale" = "1" ] && { STUBS_SKIPPED=$((STUBS_SKIPPED + 1)); continue; }
318	
319	    target="${base}.${LOCALE}.md"
320	    if [ -e "$target" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
321	      STUBS_EXISTING=$((STUBS_EXISTING + 1))
322	      continue
323	    fi
324	
325	    # Extract title from source (first '# ' heading), fallback to filename.
326	    src_title=$(grep -m1 '^# ' "$src" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^# *//' || true)
327	    [ -n "$src_title" ] || src_title="$(basename "$src" .md)"
328	
329	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
330	      log "[dry-run] create $target  (title: $src_title)"
331	    else
332	      sed -e "s|{{PAGE_TITLE}}|${src_title}|g" \
333	          -e "s|{{LANG}}|${LOCALE}|g" \
334	          "$STUB_TEMPLATE" > "$target"
335	    fi
336	    STUBS_CREATED=$((STUBS_CREATED + 1))
337	  done < "$TMP_LIST"
338	  rm -f "$TMP_LIST"
339	fi
340	
341	log "Stubs: $STUBS_CREATED created, $STUBS_EXISTING already existed, $STUBS_SKIPPED skipped (locale-suffixed)"
342	
343	# --- Step 5: update preferences ---
344	PREFS="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/check-preferences.sh"
345	ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="["
346	first=1
347	for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
348	  [ -z "$loc" ] && continue
349	  if [ "$first" = "1" ]; then
350	    ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}\"$loc\""
351	    first=0
352	  else
353	    ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}, \"$loc\""
354	  fi
355	done
356	ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}]"
357	
358	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
359	  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=$ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL"
360	  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms=true"
361	  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure=suffix"
362	else
363	  bash "$PREFS" \
364	    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=$ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL" \
365	    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms=true" \
366	    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure=suffix" \
367	    >/dev/null
368	fi
369	
370	# --- Step 6: uncomment mkdocs-static-i18n in pyproject.toml ---
371	PYPROJECT="$TARGET/pyproject.toml"
372	if [ -f "$PYPROJECT" ]; then
373	  if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*"mkdocs-static-i18n' "$PYPROJECT"; then
374	    log "pyproject.toml already lists mkdocs-static-i18n — leaving alone."
375	  elif grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*"mkdocs-static-i18n' "$PYPROJECT"; then
376	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
377	      log "[dry-run] uncomment mkdocs-static-i18n in $PYPROJECT"
378	    else
379	      sed -i.bak -E 's|^([[:space:]]*)#[[:space:]]*("mkdocs-static-i18n[^"]*",)|\1\2|' "$PYPROJECT"
380	      rm -f "${PYPROJECT}.bak"
381	      log "Uncommented mkdocs-static-i18n in $PYPROJECT"
382	    fi
383	  else
384	    log "Note: mkdocs-static-i18n not found in $PYPROJECT. Add manually:"
385	    log '        "mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2",'
386	  fi
387	else
388	  log "Note: no pyproject.toml in $TARGET. Install mkdocs-static-i18n yourself."
389	fi
390	
391	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
392	  log "Dry run complete."
393	  exit 0
394	fi
395	
396	# --- Structured success output ---
397	LANGUAGES_JSON=""
398	for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
399	  [ -z "$loc" ] && continue
400	  if [ -z "$LANGUAGES_JSON" ]; then
401	    LANGUAGES_JSON="\"$loc\""
402	  else
403	    LANGUAGES_JSON="$LANGUAGES_JSON,\"$loc\""
404	  fi
405	done
406	
407	printf '{"lang":"%s","stubs_created":%d,"stubs_existing":%d,"languages":[%s]}\n' \
408	  "$LOCALE" "$STUBS_CREATED" "$STUBS_EXISTING" "$LANGUAGES_JSON"
409	
410	# --- Post-run tips (stderr, agent-readable) ---
411	# These nudge the next step without taking action. The script's job is the
412	# structural retrofit; translation and nav-label decisions are deliberate
413	# authoring work that needs human judgment.
414	if [ "$STUBS_CREATED" -gt 0 ] || [ "$STUBS_EXISTING" -gt 0 ]; then
415	  log ""
416	  log "Next steps:"
417	  log "  1. Stubs are placeholders. Each $LOCALE page contains the terminology"
418	  log "     admonition + a 'Translation pending' warning, and is otherwise empty."
419	  log "     Ask the user whether to translate them page-by-page now"
420	  log "     (recommended batch size: 4-6 pages, run 'mkdocs build' between batches)."
421	  log "     Translation is a separate authoring task — proceed only on explicit yes."
422	  log ""
423	  log "  2. Section headings in mkdocs.yml's nav stay in the default language."
424	  log "     To translate them (e.g. 'Reference' -> '參考資料'), add a"
425	  log "     nav_translations: block under the $LOCALE entry in mkdocs.yml."
426	  log "     See references/i18n-guide.md §nav_translations."
427	fi

```text
1	# `.skills/preferences.yaml` schema
2	
3	Per-repo preferences file used by `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` and any future
4	skill that needs to remember a user decision across sessions.
5	
6	## Location
7	
8	Always at `<repo-root>/.skills/preferences.yaml`. **Per-repo, not global.**
9	Each repository carries its own decisions; never write to `~/.skills/` or
10	`~/.config/`.
11	
12	The directory is created on first write. Add `.skills/preferences.yaml` to
13	`.gitignore` if the user prefers it private, but the default assumption is
14	that it's committed (decisions about *this repo's tooling* belong in the
15	repo).
16	
17	## Top-level structure
18	
19	```yaml
20	# .skills/preferences.yaml
21	# Decisions recorded by skills. Each top-level key is a skill namespace.
22	
23	mkdocs_site_bootstrap:
24	  enabled: true                  # null = never asked, true = opted in, false = opted out
25	  decided_at: 2026-04-23
26	  stack: mkdocs-material         # which docs stack variant
27	  auto_deploy: true              # deploy via GitHub Actions on push
28	  pages_deployed: true           # has the first deploy succeeded
29	  pages_enabled_at: 2026-04-23
30	  existing_docs_decision: skipped  # skipped | wrapped | none
31	  site_url: https://owner.github.io/repo/
32	  repo_slug: owner/repo
33	  # i18n keys — written by add-language.sh, read by add-docs-page.sh.
34	  languages: ["en", "zh-TW"]      # ordered list; first is default
35	  keep_english_terms: true         # injects terminology admonition into non-default stubs
36	  i18n_structure: suffix           # suffix | folder (folder reserved, not yet implemented)
37	
38	# Future skills add their own top-level keys with the same shape.
39	# example_other_skill:
40	#   enabled: true
41	#   decided_at: 2026-05-01
42	```
43	
44	## Conventions for skill namespaces
45	
46	- **Namespace key matches the skill's directory name** with `-` → `_`
47	  (YAML-friendly): `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` → `mkdocs_site_bootstrap`.
48	- **Always include `enabled` and `decided_at`.** These are the universal
49	  fields. `enabled` is the consent state; `decided_at` lets the agent see
50	  how stale the decision is.
51	- **Don't store secrets.** This file is meant to be safely committable.
52	  API tokens, passwords, etc. go in `.env` (gitignored) or in CI secrets.
53	- **Don't store derived state.** Anything reproducible from other files
54	  (e.g., "is mkdocs.yml present") should be re-checked, not cached. Only
55	  store decisions and timestamps.
56	
57	## Three-state semantics for `enabled`
58	
59	| Value | Meaning | Agent behavior |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| key absent or `null` | Never asked | Run the interview |
62	| `true` | User opted in | Proceed without re-asking |
63	| `false` | User opted out | Don't pester. If the user is now asking for it, confirm they want to reverse the decision, then `--reset` and re-interview |
64	
65	This three-state model is why we don't use a marker file (presence-only)
66	or a boolean (only two states). The "never asked" state matters.
67	
68	## Reading and writing
69	
70	Always go through `scripts/check-preferences.sh` rather than parsing the YAML
71	yourself. It handles:
72	
73	- Creating the file and `.skills/` dir if missing
74	- Preserving the comment header
75	- Atomic writes (write to `.tmp`, then `mv`)
76	- Friendly errors for malformed input
77	
78	```bash
79	# Read one key
80	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
81	
82	# Set one or more keys
83	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
84	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
85	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
86	
87	# Reset an entire skill namespace (returns to "never asked" state)
88	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
89	
90	# Dump everything
91	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --list
92	```
93	
94	The script supports `--json` for structured output that an agent can parse
95	reliably.
96	
97	## When to reset
98	
99	The user explicitly says one of:
100	
101	- "I changed my mind about <skill>" → `--reset <namespace>`
102	- "Stop nagging me about docs" → `--set <namespace>.enabled=false`
103	- "Re-ask me next time" → `--reset <namespace>`
104	
105	Don't reset proactively. The whole point is to *avoid* re-asking.
106	
107	## Cross-skill coordination
108	
109	Two skills shouldn't share namespace keys. If `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` and
110	some hypothetical `docs-publisher` skill both care about whether a docs site
111	exists, the answer is to **detect from the filesystem** (does `mkdocs.yml`
112	exist?), not to share a preference key. Preferences record *intent*; the
113	filesystem records *state*.
114	
115	## i18n keys (added when `add-language.sh` runs)
116	
117	| Key | Type | Meaning |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| `languages` | ordered list of locale codes | First entry is the default language. Empty / missing means monolingual (default). |
120	| `keep_english_terms` | bool | Whether to inject the "Terminology rule" admonition into non-default-language stubs. Defaults to `true`; the user can flip this if they don't want the admonition. |
121	| `i18n_structure` | `suffix` \| `folder` | How translated files are laid out. **Currently only `suffix` is implemented.** `folder` is reserved for future work; setting it now will not change script behavior. |
122	
123	`add-docs-page.sh` reads `languages` to decide whether to generate
124	`*.<LANG>.md` siblings alongside the default-language page. If the key is
125	missing or has only one entry, it stays mono-lingual (existing behavior).
126	
127	## Array values via `--set`
128	
129	`check-preferences.sh --set` recognises YAML flow sequences (`[…]`) and
130	mappings (`{…}`) and passes them through to `yq` unquoted. Use this for the
131	`languages` key:
132	
133	```bash
134	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
135	  --set 'mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=["en", "zh-TW"]'
136	```
137	
138	Bare strings, booleans, and numbers still work as before.
139	
140	## Schema versioning
141	
142	If we ever need to change the shape, add a top-level `schema_version: 1`
143	key and bump it. Until then, treat the schema as version 0 / implicit.
144	
145	## Validation
146	
147	`check-preferences.sh --validate` is a future addition (not yet implemented).
148	For now, trust the script's writes and don't hand-edit the file unless you
149	re-read it after to verify.
150
```

1	# Downstream docs stack recipe
2	
3	> This page is now maintained as part of the `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` skill.
4	>
5	> The full recipe lives in the skill's reference file:
6	> [`skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/docs-stack-recipe.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/docs-stack-recipe.md)
7	>
8	> The skill also bundles ready-to-copy templates for `mkdocs.yml`,
9	> `pyproject.toml`, the GitHub Actions workflow, and a docs skeleton — see
10	> the skill's [`assets/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/assets)
11	> directory.
12	
13	## Quick start
14	
15	If your project doesn't yet use `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`, the easiest way to
16	apply the same docs stack is to invoke the skill in your repo:
17	
18	```bash
19	# From your project's repo root
20	bash <path-to-agent-skills>/skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
21	  --site-name "My Project" \
22	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
23	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
24	```
25	
26	Then enable GitHub Pages and trigger the first deploy:
27	
28	```bash
29	bash <path-to-agent-skills>/skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
30	  --repo owner/repo
31	```
32	
33	For details on what the stack actually includes (Material theme +
34	mkdocs-llmstxt + mkdocs-copy-to-llm + pymdownx.snippets), the linking rules
35	that strict mode enforces, and how the GitHub Actions workflow is wired,
36	read the canonical reference linked above.

38	## See also

40	- [Skill page: mkdocs-site-bootstrap](../skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap.md) —
41	  detailed walkthrough of the full skill workflow including consent gates,
42	  preferences, and existing-docs handling.

```

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# init-docs-site.sh — Scaffold a MkDocs Material docs site in the current repo.
3	#
4	# Bash 3.2 compatible. See SKILL.md for the full workflow including consent
5	# gates and existing-docs handling (which the agent does, not this script).
6	
7	set -euo pipefail
8	
9	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
10	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
11	ASSETS="$SKILL_DIR/assets"
12	
13	usage() {
14	  cat <<'EOF'
15	Usage: init-docs-site.sh [OPTIONS]
16	
17	Scaffold mkdocs.yml, pyproject.toml (docs extras), .github/workflows/docs.yml,
18	and a starter docs/ tree in the current repo (or --target-dir).
19	
20	Options:
21	  --site-name NAME         Display name for the site (required).
22	  --site-description DESC  One-paragraph site description (default: derived from --site-name).
23	  --site-url URL           Public URL (e.g., https://owner.github.io/repo/) (required).
24	  --repo-slug owner/repo   GitHub slug (required).
25	  --repo-name NAME         Python package-ish name for pyproject.toml (default: repo basename).
26	  --target-dir DIR         Repo root (default: current Git worktree root, or CWD
27	                           when outside Git).
28	  --existing skip|wrap     How to handle existing docs/ (default: skip — leave as-is,
29	                           omit nav for MkDocs auto-navigation).
30	                           wrap: add Markdown paths to nav alphabetically.
31	  --no-workflow            Don't create .github/workflows/docs.yml.
32	  --no-skeleton            Don't create the docs/ skeleton (use existing docs/ as-is).
33	  --social                 Enable the Material social plugin (OG/Twitter preview
34	                           cards). Off by default: it needs system Cairo/Pango
35	                           (and mkdocs-material[imaging]), so a plain scaffold
36	                           stays dependency-free. See SKILL.md § Social cards.
37	  --dry-run                Print actions without writing.
38	  --force                  Overwrite existing files (mkdocs.yml, pyproject.toml).
39	  --help, -h               Show this help and exit.
40	
41	Examples:
42	  init-docs-site.sh \
43	    --site-name "My Project" \
44	    --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/ \
45	    --repo-slug owner/repo
46	
47	  init-docs-site.sh --dry-run --site-name X --site-url https://x.io/ --repo-slug a/b
48	
49	Exit codes:
50	  0  success
51	  1  invalid arguments
52	  2  target dir not found
53	  3  refusing to overwrite (use --force)
54	  4  template missing
55	EOF
56	}

160	# --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
161	# With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
162	# (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
163	# marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
164	expand_marker() {

167	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
168	    log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"

174	      index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
175	      { print }
176	    ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
177	  else

207	replace_marked_block() {
208	  local file="$1" begin="$2" end="$3" replacement="$4" tmp rc
209	  tmp="${file}.tmp.$$"
210	  if awk -v begin="$begin" -v end="$end" -v replacement="$replacement" '
211	    BEGIN { inside = 0; begin_count = 0; end_count = 0 }
212	    index($0, begin) {

214	      inside = 1
215	      while ((getline line < replacement) > 0) print line
216	      close(replacement)

218	    }
219	    index($0, end) { end_count++; inside = 0; next }
220	    !inside { print }
221	    END {
222	      if (inside || begin_count != 1 || end_count != 1) exit 2
223	    }

+  local file="$1" begin="$2" end="$3" replacement="$4" tmp rc
+  tmp="${file}.tmp.$$"
+  if awk -v begin="$begin" -v end="$end" -v replacement="$replacement" '
+    BEGIN { inside = 0; begin_count = 0; end_count = 0 }
+    index($0, begin) {
+      begin_count++
+      inside = 1
+      while ((getline line < replacement) > 0) print line
+      close(replacement)
+      next
+    }
+    index($0, end) { end_count++; inside = 0; next }
+    !inside { print }
+    END {

+  else

+    return "$rc"

 # Handling existing `docs/` content
 
 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
 
 ## Decision tree
 
 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
 
 ```
 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
 │         on the existing site.
 └── NO  → continue
     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
 ```
 
 ## Three options to present
 
 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
 for an honest consent gate.
 
 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
 
 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
   `docs/` untouched**.
-- The generated `mkdocs.yml` will have `docs_dir: docs` pointing at their
-  files and an **empty** `nav:` so MkDocs auto-generates the nav from the
-  filesystem.
+- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
+  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
+  pages.)
 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
 
 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
 
-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing markdown files into an
-  explicit `nav:` block** so the user can see/reorder them later.
-- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to
-  pick a reasonable initial order (alphabetical by default).
+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
+  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
+  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
+  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
+- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
+  deterministic alphabetical order.
 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
   content is already there.
 
 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
 
 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
   has been asked once.
 
 ## What "non-hidden files" means
 
 For the purposes of this check:
 
 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
   "no existing content".
 
 Implementation hint:
 
 ```bash
 find docs -type f \
   -not -path '*/\.*' \
   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
   | head -50
 ```
 
 ## Things this skill must NOT do
 
 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
   absolute" without an explicit ask.
 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
   breaks rendering.
 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
 
 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.

6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
10	
11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable

27	  any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7
28	
29	## When NOT to trigger
30	
31	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
32	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
33	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
34	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
35	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
36	
37	## Workflow
38	
39	### 1. Read preferences first
40	
41	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
42	decision:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
46	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
47	```
48	
49	Possible states:
50	
51	| State | Meaning | What to do |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
54	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
55	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
56	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
57	
58	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
59	
60	Ask the user explicitly:
61	
62	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
63	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
64	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
65	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
66	
67	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:

70	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
71	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
72	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
73	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true

76	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on

79	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
80	
81	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read

83	the short version:
84	
85	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
86	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
87	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:

91	  explicit, alphabetical nav;
92	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
93	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
94	
95	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
96	
97	### 4. Scaffold
98	
99	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
100	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
101	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for

124	uv run mkdocs build --strict

128	
129	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
130	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —

168	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
169	
170	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
171	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
172	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.

181	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —

206	```
207	
208	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
209	
210	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each

261	    `--target-dir DIR`, `--no-stubs`, `--remove-llmstxt`, `--drop-strict`,
262	    `--dry-run`, `--force`.
263	
264	## Reference files
265	
266	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
267	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
268	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
269	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
270	  user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
271	  step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
272	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
273	  pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
274	  exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
275	- `references/i18n-guide.md` — Bilingual / multi-language docs setup using
276	  `mkdocs-static-i18n`. Read this **before** running `add-language.sh`. Includes
277	  the verbatim "preserve English originals" terminology rule for zh-TW pages.
278	- `references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md` — Why the stack pins `mkdocs<2` and
279	  `mkdocs-material<10`. Captures the MkDocs 2.0 plugin-removal situation,
280	  Material team's Zensical replacement, and the criteria for lifting the
281	  caps. Read whenever a user asks about upgrading MkDocs or why the docs
282	  build is on 1.x.
283	
284	## Bundled assets
285	
286	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
287	
288	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
289	  plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
290	  `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`. Carries `__SOCIAL_*__` marker lines that
291	  `init-docs-site.sh` expands (with `--social`) or deletes.
292	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
293	  optional-deps group. Has a `__SOCIAL_IMAGING__` marker.
294	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
295	  paths filter, uv setup, strict build, Pages deploy. Has a `__SOCIAL_CI__`
296	  marker for the Cairo/Pango + card-cache steps.
297	- `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when
298	  `init-docs-site.sh --social` is passed: `mkdocs-plugin.yml` (the `social`
299	  plugin block), `pyproject-dep.txt` (`mkdocs-material[imaging]`), and
300	  `ci-steps.yml` (the Cairo/Pango install + `.cache/plugin/social` cache).
301	  Pre-indented for their insertion points — keep the indentation.
302	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
303	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
304	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
305	- `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
306	  pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
307	  terminology-rule admonition.
308	- `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
309	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
310	  builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
311	
312	## Gotchas
313	
314	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
315	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
316	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
317	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
318	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
319	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
320	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
321	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
322	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
323	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
324	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
325	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
326	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
327	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
328	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
329	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
330	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
331	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
332	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
333	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
334	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
335	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
336	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
337	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
338	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
339	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
340	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
341	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
342	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
343	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
344	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
345	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
346	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
347	  `select()` form.
348	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
349	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
350	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
351	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
352	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
353	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
354	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
355	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
356	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
357	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
358	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
359	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
360	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
361	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
362	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
363	  Counter-intuitive name.
364	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
365	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
366	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
367	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
368	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
369	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
370	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
371	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
372	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
373	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
374	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
375	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
376	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
377	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
378	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
379	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
380	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
381	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
382	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
383	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
384	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
385	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
386	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
387	  is just acting on it.
388	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
389	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
390	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
391	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
392	
393	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
394	
395	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
396	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
397	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
398	have customizations the templates don't know about.
399

```text
1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
36	  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
37	  pages.)
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
46	  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
47	  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
48	  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
49	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
50	  deterministic alphabetical order.
51	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
52	  content is already there.
53	
54	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
55	
56	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
57	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
58	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
59	  has been asked once.
60	
61	## What "non-hidden files" means
62	
63	For the purposes of this check:
64	
65	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
66	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
67	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
68	  "no existing content".
69	
70	Implementation hint:
71	
72	```bash
73	find docs -type f \
74	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
75	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
76	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
77	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
78	  | head -50
79	```
80	
81	## Things this skill must NOT do
82	
83	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
84	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
85	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
86	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
87	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
88	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
89	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
90	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
91	  breaks rendering.
92	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
93	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
94	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
95	
96	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
97	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
98	
99	## After bootstrap
100	
101	Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
102	for option a) and report:
103	
104	- Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
105	- Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
106	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
107	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
108	
109	## Recording the decision
110	
111	```bash
112	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
113	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
114	```
115	
116	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
117	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).
118

 ## Decision tree
 
 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
 
 ```
 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
 │         on the existing site.
 └── NO  → continue
     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
 ```
 
 ## Three options to present
 
 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
 for an honest consent gate.
 
 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
 
 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
   `docs/` untouched**.
-- The generated `mkdocs.yml` will have `docs_dir: docs` pointing at their
-  files and an **empty** `nav:` so MkDocs auto-generates the nav from the
-  filesystem.
+- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
+  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
+  pages.)
 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
 
 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
 
-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing markdown files into an
-  explicit `nav:` block** so the user can see/reorder them later.
-- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to
-  pick a reasonable initial order (alphabetical by default).
+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
+  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
+  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
+  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
+- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
+  deterministic alphabetical order.
 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
   content is already there.
 
 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
 
 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
   has been asked once.
 
 ## What "non-hidden files" means
 
 For the purposes of this check:
 
 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
   "no existing content".
 
 Implementation hint:

   -not -path '*/\.*' \
   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
   | head -50
 ```

21	FAIL_COUNT=0
22	FAIL_LOG=""

24	red()   { printf '\033[31m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
25	green() { printf '\033[32m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
26	dim()   { printf '\033[2m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }

28	pass() {

30	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(green PASS)" "$1"
31	}
32	fail() {

34	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(red FAIL)" "$1"
35	  FAIL_LOG="${FAIL_LOG}FAIL: $1\n"
36	}

38	# make_repo — spin up an isolated tmp repo with an initial commit.
39	# Prints the path to stdout.
40	make_repo() {
41	  local d
42	  d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-scan-staged.XXXXXX)
43	  git -C "$d" init -q -b main
44	  git -C "$d" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null \
45	      -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=test \
46	      commit -q --allow-empty -m init
47	  printf '%s' "$d"
48	}

50	# Copy fixture + stage it under the given relative path. Strips the inline
51	# `<!-- gitleaks:allow -->` marker so the rules still fire in the throwaway repo
52	# (byte-identical to the fixture otherwise). Line-based sed → newline never
53	# enters the pattern space, so [[:space:]]* only eats the horizontal separator.
54	#
55	# Also expands the `__SYNTHETIC_*__` placeholders, which keep provider-scanner
56	# and detect-private-key bait out of the fixture files themselves. Must stay in
57	# sync with FIXTURE_PLACEHOLDERS in conftest.py -- the PEM header is assembled
58	# from split literals here for the same reason it is there.
59	stage_fixture() {
60	  local repo="$1" fixture="$2" dest_rel="$3"
61	  local pk="PRIVATE"" KEY"
62	  # Built, never written: a literal `whsec_` + 32 chars in this file would be
63	  # a gitleaks `stripe-webhook-secret` finding in every repo that installs the
64	  # skill -- the same class of shipped-bait as the PEM headers above.
65	  local whsec="whsec_$(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 32))"
66	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$repo/$dest_rel")"
67	  sed -e 's/[[:space:]]*<!-- *gitleaks:allow *-->//g' \
68	      -e "s/__SYNTHETIC_PEM_BEGIN__/-----BEGIN RSA $pk-----/g" \
69	      -e "s/__SYNTHETIC_PEM_END__/-----END RSA $pk-----/g" \
70	      -e "s/__SYNTHETIC_PEM_HEADER_OPENSSH__/-----BEGIN OPENSSH $pk-----/g" \
71	      -e "s/__SYNTHETIC_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET__/$whsec/g" \
72	      "$FIXTURES/$fixture" > "$repo/$dest_rel"
73	  git -C "$repo" add -- "$dest_rel"
74	}
75	
76	if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
77	  printf '%s gitleaks binary missing\n' "$(dim SKIP)"
78	  printf '  (skipping positive cases; running the exit-30 contract only)\n\n'
79	  GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE=0
80	else
81	  GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE=1
82	fi
83	
84	printf '== scan-staged exit-code contract ==\n\n'
85	
86	# --- Case 1: clean file → exit 0 ---
87	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then
88	  REPO=$(make_repo)
89	  # Install the gitleaks config so rules apply.
90	  cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml"
91	  stage_fixture "$REPO" "clean.md" "notes.md"
92	  (cd "$REPO" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
93	  rc=$?
94	  if [ "$rc" = "0" ]; then pass "clean fixture → exit 0"
95	  else fail "clean fixture → exit 0 (got $rc)"
96	  fi
97	  rm -rf "$REPO"
98	fi
99	
100	# --- Case 2: real leak inside .claude/plans/ → exit 20 ---
101	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then
102	  REPO=$(make_repo)
103	  cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml"
104	  stage_fixture "$REPO" "real_anthropic.md" ".claude/plans/p1.md"
105	  (cd "$REPO" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
106	  rc=$?
107	  if [ "$rc" = "20" ]; then pass "real Anthropic key → exit 20"
108	  else fail "real Anthropic key → exit 20 (got $rc)"
109	  fi
110	  rm -rf "$REPO"
111	fi
112	
113	# --- Case 3: not in a git repo → exit 2 ---
114	OUTSIDE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-scan-outside.XXXXXX)
115	(cd "$OUTSIDE" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
116	rc=$?
117	if [ "$rc" = "2" ]; then pass "outside git repo → exit 2"
118	else fail "outside git repo → exit 2 (got $rc)"
119	fi
120	rm -rf "$OUTSIDE"
121	
122	# --- Case 4: gitleaks missing → exit 30 ---
123	# Simulate by running with an empty PATH so `command -v gitleaks` fails.
124	REPO=$(make_repo)
125	cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml" 2>/dev/null || true
126	# Keep /bin and /usr/bin so the script itself (bash, git, mktemp) runs.
127	FAKE_PATH="/bin:/usr/bin"
128	(cd "$REPO" && PATH="$FAKE_PATH" bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
129	rc=$?
130	if [ "$rc" = "30" ]; then pass "no gitleaks on PATH → exit 30"
131	else fail "no gitleaks on PATH → exit 30 (got $rc)"
132	fi
133	rm -rf "$REPO"
134	
135	# --- Case 5: empty JSON report `[]` handled as clean → exit 0 ---
136	# This is the regression we caught during initial verification: gitleaks
137	# writes `[]` for zero findings; scan-staged.sh must not treat that as
138	# "non-empty file → leaks found".
139	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then
140	  REPO=$(make_repo)
141	  cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml"
142	  stage_fixture "$REPO" "example_shapes.md" ".claude/plans/p1.md"
143	  (cd "$REPO" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
144	  rc=$?
145	  if [ "$rc" = "0" ]; then pass "allowlisted example shapes → exit 0 (empty [] report)"
146	  else fail "allowlisted example shapes → exit 0 (got $rc)"
147	  fi
148	  rm -rf "$REPO"
149	fi
150	
151	printf '\n== summary ==\n'
152	printf 'pass: %d\nfail: %d\n' "$PASS_COUNT" "$FAIL_COUNT"
153	if [ "$FAIL_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then

208	    write_lang_stub "$ABS_PATH" "$loc"

214	  "$REL_PATH" "$SECTION" "$NAV_STATUS" "$STUBS_CREATED"

```text
1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
36	  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
37	  pages.)
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
46	  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
47	  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
48	  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
49	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
50	  deterministic alphabetical order.
51	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
52	  content is already there.
53	
54	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
55	
56	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
57	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
58	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
59	  has been asked once.
60	
61	## What "non-hidden files" means
62	
63	For the purposes of this check:
64	
65	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
66	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
67	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
68	  "no existing content".
69	
70	Implementation hint:
71	
72	```bash
73	find docs -type f \
74	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
75	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
76	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
77	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
78	  | head -50
79	```
80	
81	## Things this skill must NOT do
82	
83	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
84	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
85	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
86	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
87	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
88	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
89	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
90	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
```

+      inside = 1
+      while ((getline line < replacement) > 0) print line

+      next
+    }
+    index($0, end) { end_count++; inside = 0; next }
+    !inside { print }
+    END {
+      if (inside || begin_count != 1 || end_count != 1) exit 2
+    }
+  ' "$file" > "$tmp"; then
+    mv "$tmp" "$file"
+  else
+    rc=$?
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    return "$rc"
+  fi
+}
+
+strip_starter_markers() {

+    return "$rc"
+  fi
+}

+    rm -f "$paths" "$nav" "$llmstxt"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Regression tests for MkDocs bootstrap root discovery and existing-doc handling.
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
+
+set -u
+
+TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/.." && pwd)"
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SKILL_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
+INIT="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/init-docs-site.sh"
+PREFERENCES="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/check-preferences.sh"
+BASE="$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-mkdocs-bootstrap.XXXXXX)"
+BASE="$(cd "$BASE" && pwd -P)"
+FAKE_BIN="$BASE/bin"
+SYSTEM_PATH="/bin:/usr/bin:$PATH"
+PASS_COUNT=0
+FAIL_COUNT=0
+
+trap 'rm -rf "$BASE"' EXIT
+
+printf 'bash-under-test: %s (%s)\n' "$BASH_VERSION" "$BASH"
+if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && [ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" != "3" ]; then
+  printf 'error: Darwin compatibility suite must run with /bin/bash 3.x\n' >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+pass() { PASS_COUNT=$((PASS_COUNT + 1)); printf '  PASS %s\n' "$1"; }
+fail() { FAIL_COUNT=$((FAIL_COUNT + 1)); printf '  FAIL %s\n' "$1"; }
+contains() { printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -Fq -- "$2"; }
+
+assert_contains() {
+  local name="$1" value="$2" expected="$3"
+  if contains "$value" "$expected"; then pass "$name"; else
+    fail "$name"
+    printf '    expected output to contain: %s\n' "$expected" >&2
+  fi
+}
+
+assert_line() {
+  local name="$1" value="$2" expected="$3"
+  if printf '%s\n' "$value" | grep -Fqx -- "$expected"; then pass "$name"; else
+    fail "$name"
+    printf '    expected exact output line: %s\n' "$expected" >&2
+  fi
+}
+
+assert_file() {
+  local name="$1" path="$2"
+  if [ -f "$path" ]; then pass "$name"; else fail "$name"; fi
+}
+
+assert_no_file() {
+  local name="$1" path="$2"
+  if [ ! -e "$path" ]; then pass "$name"; else fail "$name"; fi
+}
+
+fingerprint_tree() {
+  local root="$1"
+  find "$root" -type f -print | LC_ALL=C sort | while IFS= read -r path; do
+    printf '%s  %s\n' "$(git hash-object --no-filters "$path")" "${path#"$root"/}"
+  done
+}
+
+run_init() {
+  local target="$1" mode="$2"
+  "$INIT" \
+    --target-dir "$target" \
+    --site-name "Fixture Docs" \
+    --site-url "https://example.test/docs/" \
+    --repo-slug "owner/repo" \
+    --existing "$mode" \
+    --no-workflow
+}
+
+validate_config() {
+  local config="$1" mode="$2"
+  shift 2
+  uv run --project "$REPO_ROOT" --extra docs python - "$config" "$mode" "$@" <<'PY'
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import yaml
+
+config = Path(sys.argv[1])
+mode = sys.argv[2]
+expected = sys.argv[3:]
+data = yaml.safe_load(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+plugins = data["plugins"]
+llmstxt = next(item["llmstxt"] for item in plugins if isinstance(item, dict) and "llmstxt" in item)
+guides = llmstxt.get("sections", {}).get("Guides", [])
+
+if mode == "fresh":
+    assert data["nav"] == [{"Home": "index.md"}, {"Getting Started": "getting-started.md"}]
+    assert guides == ["index.md", "getting-started.md"]
+elif mode == "skip":
+    assert "nav" not in data
+    assert guides == expected
+elif mode == "wrap":
+    assert data["nav"] == expected
+    assert guides == expected
+else:
+    raise AssertionError(f"unknown mode: {mode}")
+PY
+}
+
+build_fixture() {

+  uv run --project "$REPO_ROOT" --extra docs mkdocs build \
+    --strict \

+chmod +x "$FAKE_BIN/yq"

+WORKTREE="$BASE/linked-worktree"

+git -C "$PRIMARY" init -q -b main
+printf 'base\n' > "$PRIMARY/base.txt"
+git -C "$PRIMARY" add base.txt
+git -C "$PRIMARY" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null \
+  -c user.name=test -c user.email=test@example.com commit -q -m init
+git -C "$PRIMARY" worktree add -q -b linked "$WORKTREE"
+mkdir -p "$WORKTREE/nested/deep" "$WORKTREE/.skills"
+printf 'fixture: linked-worktree\n' > "$WORKTREE/.skills/preferences.yaml"
+
+OUTPUT=$(
+  cd "$WORKTREE/nested/deep" &&
+  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null "$INIT" --dry-run --site-name Test \
+    --site-url https://example.test/ --repo-slug owner/repo --no-workflow 2>&1
+)
+assert_line "init resolves linked-worktree root" "$OUTPUT" "Target: $WORKTREE"
+
+OUTPUT=$(
+  cd "$WORKTREE/nested/deep" &&
+  PATH="$FAKE_BIN:$SYSTEM_PATH" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null "$PREFERENCES" --list
+)
+assert_contains "preferences resolve linked-worktree root" "$OUTPUT" "fixture: linked-worktree"
+
+# Outside Git, both scripts keep the invocation directory fallback.
+OUTSIDE="$BASE/outside/nested"
+mkdir -p "$OUTSIDE/.skills"
+printf 'fixture: outside-git\n' > "$OUTSIDE/.skills/preferences.yaml"
+OUTPUT=$(
+  cd "$OUTSIDE" &&
+  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null "$INIT" --dry-run --site-name Test \
+    --site-url https://example.test/ --repo-slug owner/repo --no-workflow 2>&1
+)
+assert_line "init falls back outside Git" "$OUTPUT" "Target: $OUTSIDE"
+OUTPUT=$(
+  cd "$OUTSIDE" &&
+  PATH="$FAKE_BIN:$SYSTEM_PATH" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null "$PREFERENCES" --list
+)
+assert_contains "preferences fall back outside Git" "$OUTPUT" "fixture: outside-git"
+
+# Fresh scaffold keeps the starter pages and starter configuration.
+FRESH="$BASE/fresh"
+mkdir -p "$FRESH"
+run_init "$FRESH" skip >/dev/null
+assert_file "fresh scaffold creates index" "$FRESH/docs/index.md"
+assert_file "fresh scaffold creates getting started" "$FRESH/docs/getting-started.md"
+if validate_config "$FRESH/mkdocs.yml" fresh; then pass "fresh config keeps starter entries"; else fail "fresh config keeps starter entries"; fi
+if build_fixture "$FRESH"; then pass "fresh scaffold builds strictly"; else fail "fresh scaffold builds strictly"; fi
+
+# --no-skeleton also removes starter references when no docs exist yet.
+NO_SKELETON="$BASE/no-skeleton"
+mkdir -p "$NO_SKELETON"
+"$INIT" --target-dir "$NO_SKELETON" --site-name "Fixture Docs" \

+  --no-skeleton --no-workflow >/dev/null
+assert_no_file "no-skeleton creates no docs directory" "$NO_SKELETON/docs"
+if validate_config "$NO_SKELETON/mkdocs.yml" skip; then
+  pass "no-skeleton removes starter references"
+else
+  fail "no-skeleton removes starter references"
+fi
+
+# Skip preserves existing docs and omits explicit navigation.
+SKIP="$BASE/skip"
+mkdir -p "$SKIP/docs/nested"
+printf '# Alpha\n' > "$SKIP/docs/alpha.md"
+printf '# Beta Notes\n' > "$SKIP/docs/nested/Beta notes.md"

+if validate_config "$SKIP/mkdocs.yml" skip alpha.md "nested/Beta notes.md"; then pass "skip omits nav and refreshes llmstxt paths"; else fail "skip omits nav and refreshes llmstxt paths"; fi
+if build_fixture "$SKIP"; then pass "skip scaffold builds strictly"; else fail "skip scaffold builds strictly"; fi
+
+# Wrap preserves docs and writes deterministic path-only navigation.
+WRAP="$BASE/wrap"

+if validate_config "$WRAP/mkdocs.yml" wrap \

+if build_fixture "$WRAP"; then pass "wrap scaffold builds strictly"; else fail "wrap scaffold builds strictly"; fi

   167	  log "Nav already references $REL_PATH — checking language stubs only."
   168	  NAV_STATUS="already_exists"
   169	else
   170	  if [ "$SECTION" = "_root" ]; then
   171	    EXPR=".nav += [{\"$TITLE\": \"$REL_PATH\"}]"
   172	  else
   173	    # Find the index of the section in nav (top-level dict whose only key is $SECTION).
   174	    IDX=$(SEC="$SECTION" yq 'env(SEC) as $s | [.nav[] | keys | .[0]] | to_entries | map(select(.value == $s)) | .[0].key' \
   175	      "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "null")
   176	    if [ "$IDX" = "null" ] || [ -z "$IDX" ]; then
   177	      EXISTING_SECTIONS=$(yq '[.nav[] | keys | .[0]] | join(",")' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
   178	      die "section '$SECTION' not found at top of nav: in $MKDOCS (existing: $EXISTING_SECTIONS)" 4
   179	    fi
   180	    EXPR=".nav[$IDX].\"$SECTION\" += [{\"$TITLE\": \"$REL_PATH\"}]"
   181	  fi
   182	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
   183	    log "[dry-run] yq -i '$EXPR' $MKDOCS"
   184	  else
   185	    TMP="${MKDOCS}.tmp.$$"
   186	    yq "$EXPR" "$MKDOCS" > "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; die "yq failed: $EXPR" 4; }
   187	    mv "$TMP" "$MKDOCS"
   188	    log "Updated nav in: $MKDOCS"
   189	  fi

195	@@ -8,162 +8,164 @@ description: Bootstrap MkDocs Material docs sites with optional GitHub Pages dep
196	 Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
197	 repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
198	 
199	 This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
200	 `.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
201	 asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
202	 mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
203	 starts fresh.
204	 
205	 ## When to trigger
206	 
207	 - User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
208	   site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
209	 - User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
210	 - User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
211	   applied to a new project
212	 - User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
213	 - User asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual",
214	   "add Traditional Chinese", "add zh-TW", "translate the docs", or to add
215	   any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7
216	 
217	 ## When NOT to trigger
218	 
219	 - User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
220	 - User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
221	   unless the user is now reversing that decision
222	 - User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
223	 - User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
224	 
225	 ## Workflow
226	 
227	 ### 1. Read preferences first
228	 
229	 Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
230	 decision:
231	 
232	 ```bash
233	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
234	   --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
235	 ```
236	 
237	 Possible states:
238	 
239	 | State | Meaning | What to do |
240	 |---|---|---|
241	 | File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
242	 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
243	 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
244	 | `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
245	 
246	 ### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
247	 
248	 Ask the user explicitly:
249	 
250	 1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
251	    (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
252	 2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
253	    (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
254	 
255	 Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
256	 
257	 ```bash
258	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
259	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
260	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
261	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
262	 ```
263	 
264	 If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
265	 future invocations.
266	 
267	 ### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
268	 
269	 Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
270	 `references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
271	 the short version:
272	 
273	 - If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
274	   exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
275	 - If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
276	-  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them;
277	-  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my files included as-is in the nav;
278	+  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
279	+  with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
280	+  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
281	+  explicit, alphabetical nav;
282	   (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
283	 - If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
284	 
285	 Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
286	 
287	 ### 4. Scaffold
288	 
289	 Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
290	 `pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
291	 `docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
292	 copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
293	 `.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
294	 `--social` is on.
295	 
296	 ```bash
297	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
298	   --site-name "My Project" \
299	   --repo-slug owner/repo \
300	   --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
301	 ```
302	 
303	 Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
304	 files unless `--force` is passed.
305	 
306	 Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
307	 are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
308	 the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
309	 
310	 After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
311	 
312	 ```bash
313	 uv sync --extra docs
314	 uv run mkdocs build --strict
315	 ```
316	 
317	 ### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
318	 
319	 This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
320	 and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
321	 say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
322	 Only proceed on explicit yes.
323	 
324	 ```bash
325	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
326	   --repo owner/repo
327	 ```
328	 
329	 Flags:
330	 - `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
331	 - `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
332	 
333	 After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
334	 in preferences.
335	 
336	 ### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
337	 
338	 For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
339	 `mkdocs.yml`:
340	 
341	 ```bash
342	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
343	   --section workflows \
344	   --title "My new workflow" \
345	   --slug my-new-workflow
346	 ```
347	 
348	 It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
349	 nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
350	 — re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
351	 
352	 If the project has additional languages configured in
353	 `.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
354	 also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
355	 terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
356	 translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
357	 
358	 ### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
359	 
360	 The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
361	 `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).

464	 # Handling existing `docs/` content
465	 
466	 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
467	 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
468	 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
469	 
470	 ## Decision tree
471	 
472	 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
473	 
474	 ```
475	 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
476	 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
477	 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
478	 │         on the existing site.
479	 └── NO  → continue
480	     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
481	     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
482	     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
483	     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
484	         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
485	         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
486	 ```
487	 
488	 ## Three options to present
489	 
490	 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
491	 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
492	 for an honest consent gate.
493	 
494	 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
495	 
496	 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
497	   `docs/` untouched**.
498	-- The generated `mkdocs.yml` will have `docs_dir: docs` pointing at their
499	-  files and an **empty** `nav:` so MkDocs auto-generates the nav from the
500	-  filesystem.
501	+- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
502	+  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
503	+  pages.)
504	 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
505	 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
506	   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
507	   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
508	 
509	 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
510	 
511	-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing markdown files into an
512	-  explicit `nav:` block** so the user can see/reorder them later.
513	-- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to
514	-  pick a reasonable initial order (alphabetical by default).
515	+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
516	+  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
517	+  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
518	+  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
519	+- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
520	+  deterministic alphabetical order.
521	 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
522	   content is already there.
523	 
524	 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
525	 
526	 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
527	 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
528	 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
529	   has been asked once.
530	 
531	 ## What "non-hidden files" means
532	 
533	 For the purposes of this check:
534	 
535	 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
536	 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
537	 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
538	   "no existing content".
539	 
540	 Implementation hint:
541	 
542	 ```bash
543	 find docs -type f \
544	   -not -path '*/\.*' \
545	   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
546	   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
547	   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
548	   | head -50
549	 ```
550	 
551	 ## Things this skill must NOT do
552	 
553	 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
554	   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
555	 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
556	   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
557	 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
558	   absolute" without an explicit ask.
559	 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
560	   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
561	   breaks rendering.
562	 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
563	   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
564	   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
565	 
566	 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
567	 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
568	 
569	 ## After bootstrap
570	 
571	 Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
572	 for option a) and report:
573	 
574	 - Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
575	 - Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
576	 - Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
577	   are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
578	 
579	 ## Recording the decision
580	 
581	 ```bash
582	 bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
583	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
584	 ```
585	 
586	 Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
587	 `wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).

605	 Usage: check-preferences.sh [OPTIONS]
606	 
607	 Read, write, or reset entries in .skills/preferences.yaml (per-repo).

609	 Options:

611	                              Prints empty string + exits 0 if absent.

613	                              (so 'true', '42', '2026-04-23', and bare strings
614	                              all work). Quote complex values.
