66	
67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
76	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
77	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
78	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
79	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
80	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
81	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
82	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
83	
84	Active series in this repo:
85	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
86	
87	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
88	
89	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
90	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
91	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
92	
93	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
94	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
95	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
96	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
97	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
98	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
99	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
100	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
101	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
102	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
103	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
104	
105	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
106	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
107	
108	## Marketplace Catalog
109	
110	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
111	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
112	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
113	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
114	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
115	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
116	for the full mechanism.
117	
118	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
119	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
120	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
121	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
122	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
123	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
124	
125	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
126	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
127	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
128	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
129	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
130	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
131	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
132	within-group caveat in
133	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
134	
135	## SKILL.md Format
136	
137	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
138	
139	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
140	
141	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
142	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
143	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
144	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
145	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
146	
147	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
148	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
149	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
150	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
151	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
152	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
153	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
154	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
155	
156	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
157	
158	```bash
159	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
160	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
161	
162	# …or remove them afterward
163	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
164	```
165	
166	## Project Memory Workflow
167	
168	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
169	
170	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
171	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
172	
173	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
174	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
175	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
176	
177	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
178	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
179	
180	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
181	
182	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
183	
184	   ```bash
185	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
186	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
187	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
188	   ```
189	
190	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
191	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
192	
193	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
194	
195	   ```bash
196	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
197	   ```
198	
199	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
200	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
201	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
202	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
203	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
204	
205	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
206	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
207	   afterwards to catch drift.
208	
209	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
210	
211	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
212	
213	```bash
214	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
215	```
216	
217	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
218	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
219	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
220	
221	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
222	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
223	
224	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
225	
226	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
227	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
228	own conventions). It has four subareas:
229	
230	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
231	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
232	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
233	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
234	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
235	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
236	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
237	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
238	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
239	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
240	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
241	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
242	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
243	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
244	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
245	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
246	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
247	  status / license / last_verified`).
248	
249	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
250	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
251	
252	| Status | Meaning |
253	|---|---|
254	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
255	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
256	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
257	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
258	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
259	
260	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
261	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
262	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
263	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
264	
265	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
266	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
267	
268	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
269	
270	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
271	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
272	
273	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
274	2. The root cause
275	3. The workaround
276	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
277	
278	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
279	the explanation they do not know yet.
280
```
</details></tool-use>

 ## Workflow
 
 ### 1. Read preferences first
 
 Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded

 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
 | `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
 
 ### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)

   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \

 Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read

   explicit, alphabetical nav;

 Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.

 `pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the

 ```bash

 This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)

 - `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them

 - `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when

 - `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`

 - `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
 - `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language

 - `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
   `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
   builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
 
 ## Gotchas
 
 - **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
   to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
   no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
   dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
   it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
   it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
   `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
   cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
   `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
 - **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
   `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
   `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
   error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
   (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
   `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
   same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
   the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
   there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
   Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.

 # Handling existing `docs/` content
 
 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
 
 ## Decision tree
 
 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
 
 ```
 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
 │         on the existing site.
 └── NO  → continue
     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
 ```
 
 ## Three options to present
 
 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
 for an honest consent gate.
 
 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
 
 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
   `docs/` untouched**.
 - The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
   from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
   pages.)
 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
 
 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
 
-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
-  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
-  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
-  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
+  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
+  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
+  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
+  include fragments are not navigation pages.
 - Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
   deterministic alphabetical order.
 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
   content is already there.
 
 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
 
 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
   has been asked once.
 
 ## What "non-hidden files" means
 
 For the purposes of this check:
 
 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
   "no existing content".
 
 Implementation hint:
 
 ```bash
 find docs -type f \
   -not -path '*/\.*' \
   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
   | head -50
 ```
 
 ## Things this skill must NOT do
 
+- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
+  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
+  repository.
+- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
+  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
+  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
   absolute" without an explicit ask.
 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
   breaks rendering.
 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
 
 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
 
 ## After bootstrap
 
 Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
 for option a) and report:
 
 - Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
 - Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
 - Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
   are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
 
 ## Recording the decision
 
 ```bash
 bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
 ```

9	 ## Workflow
10	 
11	 ### 1. Read preferences first
12	 
13	 Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
14	 decision:
15

19	 ```
20

22	 
23	 | State | Meaning | What to do |
24	 |---|---|---|
25	 | File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
26	 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
27	 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
28	 | `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
29	 
30	 ### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
31	 
32	 Ask the user explicitly:
33	 
34	 1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
35	    (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
36	 2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
37	    (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
38	 
39	 Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
40	 
41	 ```bash
42	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
43	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
44	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
45	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
46	 ```
47	 
48	 If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
49	 future invocations.
50	 
51	 ### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
52	 
53	 Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
54	 `references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
55	 the short version:
56	 
57	 - If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
58	   exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
59	 - If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
60	   (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
61	   with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
62	   (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
63	   explicit, alphabetical nav;
64	   (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
65	 - If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
66	 
67	 Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
68	 
69	 ### 4. Scaffold
70	 
71	 Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
72	 `pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
73	 `docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
74	 copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
75	 `.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
76	 `--social` is on.
77	 
78	 ```bash
79	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
80	   --site-name "My Project" \
81	   --repo-slug owner/repo \
82	   --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
83	 ```
84	 
85	 Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
86	-files unless `--force` is passed.
87	+files unless `--force` is passed, and refuses symlinks anywhere in an existing
88	+`docs/` tree rather than risking writes outside the repository. In `skip` and
89	+`wrap` modes it omits `copy-to-llm`, whose build hook writes generated assets
90	+under `docs/`; users can opt into that plugin separately after choosing where
91	+those generated files belong.
92	 
93	 Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
94	 are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
95	 the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
96	 
97	 After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
98	 
99	 ```bash
100	 uv sync --extra docs
101	 uv run mkdocs build --strict
102	 ```
103	 
104	 ### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
105	 
106	 This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
107	 and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
108	 say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
109	 Only proceed on explicit yes.
110	 
111	 ```bash
112	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
113	   --repo owner/repo
114	 ```
115	 
116	 Flags:
117	 - `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
118	 - `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
119	 
120	 After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
121	 in preferences.
122	 
123	 ### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
124	 
125	 For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
126	 `mkdocs.yml`:
127	 
128	 ```bash
129	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
130	   --section workflows \
131	   --title "My new workflow" \
132	   --slug my-new-workflow
133	 ```
134	 
135	 It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
136	 nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
137	 — re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
138	 
139	 If the project has additional languages configured in
140	 `.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
141	 also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
142	 terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
143	 translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
144	 
145	 ### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
146	 
147	 The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
148	 `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
149	 This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
150	 
151	 Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
152	 "add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
153	 
154	 Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
155	 preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
156	 invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
157	 
158	 Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
159	 keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
160	 warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
161	 `Makefile` for you):
162	 
163	 ```bash
164	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
165	   --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
166	 ```
167	 
168	 This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
169	 siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
170	 pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
171	 `--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
172	 `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
173	 is a no-op.
174	 
175	 If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
176	 instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
177	 
178	 After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
179	 
180	 ```bash
181	 uv sync --extra docs
182	 uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
183	 ```
184	 
185	 #### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
186	 
187	 `add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
188	 `*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
189	 pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
190	 translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
191	 rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
192	 canonical).
193	 
194	 Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
195	 — do not assume. A reasonable script:
196	 
197	 > "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
198	 > 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
199	 > follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
200	 > invent translations)."
201	 
202	 Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
203	 — they're already valid pages and the build passes.
204	 
205	 When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
206	 for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
207	 §nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
208	 user may want one without the other.
209	 
210	 ## Available scripts
211	 
212	 - **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
213	   `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
214	   - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
215	     `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
216	 - **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
217	   - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,

219	   - Always appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to `.gitignore`,
220	     idempotently.
221	   - `--social` opts into OG/Twitter cards: expands the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers in
222	     the templates with the blocks in `assets/social/`, and adds `/.cache/` to
223	     `.gitignore`. Off by default (keeps the scaffold Cairo/Pango-free).
224	 - **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via

229	-  `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.

253	   user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
254	   step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
255	 - `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
256	   pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
257	   exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
258	 - `references/i18n-guide.md` — Bilingual / multi-language docs setup using
259	   `mkdocs-static-i18n`. Read this **before** running `add-language.sh`. Includes
260	   the verbatim "preserve English originals" terminology rule for zh-TW pages.
261	 - `references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md` — Why the stack pins `mkdocs<2` and
262	   `mkdocs-material<10`. Captures the MkDocs 2.0 plugin-removal situation,
263	   Material team's Zensical replacement, and the criteria for lifting the
264	   caps. Read whenever a user asks about upgrading MkDocs or why the docs
265	   build is on 1.x.
266	 
267	 ## Bundled assets
268	 
269	 Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
270	 
271	 - `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
272	   plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
273	   `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`. Carries `__SOCIAL_*__` marker lines that
274	   `init-docs-site.sh` expands (with `--social`) or deletes.
275	 - `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
276	   optional-deps group. Has a `__SOCIAL_IMAGING__` marker.
277	 - `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
278	   paths filter, uv setup, strict build, Pages deploy. Has a `__SOCIAL_CI__`
279	   marker for the Cairo/Pango + card-cache steps.
280	 - `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when
281	   `init-docs-site.sh --social` is passed: `mkdocs-plugin.yml` (the `social`
282	   plugin block), `pyproject-dep.txt` (`mkdocs-material[imaging]`), and
283	   `ci-steps.yml` (the Cairo/Pango install + `.cache/plugin/social` cache).
284	   Pre-indented for their insertion points — keep the indentation.
285	 - `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
286	   examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
287	 - `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
288	 - `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
289	   pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
290	   terminology-rule admonition.
291	 - `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
292	   `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
293	   builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
294	 
295	 ## Gotchas
296	 
297	 - **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
298	   to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
299	   no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
300	   dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
301	   it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
302	   it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
303	   `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
304	   cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
305	   `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
306	 - **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
307	   `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
308	   `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
309	   error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
310	   (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
311	   `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
312	   same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
313	   the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
314	   there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
315	   Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.

420	 # Handling existing `docs/` content
421	 
422	 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
423	 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
424	 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
425	 
426	 ## Decision tree
427	 
428	 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
429	 
430	 ```
431	 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
432	 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
433	 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
434	 │         on the existing site.
435	 └── NO  → continue
436	     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
437	     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
438	     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
439	     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
440	         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
441	         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
442	 ```
443	 
444	 ## Three options to present
445	 
446	 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
447	 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
448	 for an honest consent gate.
449	 
450	 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
451	 
452	 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
453	   `docs/` untouched**.
454	 - The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
455	   from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
456	   pages.)
457	 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
458	 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
459	   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
460	   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
461	 
462	 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
463	 
464	-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
465	-  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
466	-  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
467	-  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
468	+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
469	+  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
470	+  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
471	+  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
472	+  include fragments are not navigation pages.
473	 - Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
474	   deterministic alphabetical order.
475	 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
476	   content is already there.
477	 
478	 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
479	 
480	 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
481	 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
482	 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
483	   has been asked once.
484	 
485	 ## What "non-hidden files" means
486	 
487	 For the purposes of this check:
488	 
489	 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
490	 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
491	 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
492	   "no existing content".
493	 
494	 Implementation hint:
495	 
496	 ```bash
497	 find docs -type f \
498	   -not -path '*/\.*' \
499	   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
500	   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
501	   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
502	   | head -50
503	 ```
504	 
505	 ## Things this skill must NOT do
506	 
507	+- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
508	+  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
509	+  repository.
510	+- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
511	+  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
512	+  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
513	 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
514	   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
515	 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
516	   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
517	 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
518	   absolute" without an explicit ask.
519	 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
520	   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
521	   breaks rendering.
522	 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
523	   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
524	   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
525	 
526	 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
527	 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
528	 
529	 ## After bootstrap
530	 
531	 Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
532	 for option a) and report:
533	 
534	 - Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
535	 - Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
536	 - Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
537	   are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
538	 
539	 ## Recording the decision
540	 
541	 ```bash
542	 bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
543	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
544	 ```
545	 
546	 Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
547	 `wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).

840	 # --- helper: copy template, refusing to overwrite unless --force ---
841	 copy_template() {
842	   local src="$1" dst="$2"
843	   [ -f "$src" ] || die "template missing: $src" 4
844	   if [ -e "$dst" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
845	     die "exists, refusing to overwrite: $dst (use --force)" 3
846	   fi
847	   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
848	     log "[dry-run] cp $src → $dst"
849	     return 0
850	   fi
851	   mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"
852	   cp "$src" "$dst"
853	 }

855	 # --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
856	 # With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
857	 # (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
858	 # marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
859	 expand_marker() {
860	   local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
861	   [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
862	   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
863	     log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"
864	     return 0
865	   fi
866	   if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
867	     [ -f "$snippet" ] || die "social snippet missing: $snippet" 4
868	     awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
869	       index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
870	       { print }
871	     ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
872	   else
873	     awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
874	   fi
875	 }

147	 The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the

183	 ```

186	 
187	 `add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each

295	 ## Gotchas
296	 
297	 - **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
298	   to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
299	   no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
300	   dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
301	   it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
302	   it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
303	   `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
304	   cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
305	   `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
306	 - **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
307	   `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
308	   `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
309	   error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
310	   (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
311	   `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
312	   same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
313	   the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
314	   there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
315	   Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.

420	 # Handling existing `docs/` content
421	 
422	 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
423	 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
424	 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
425	 
426	 ## Decision tree
427	 
428	 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
429	 
430	 ```
431	 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
432	 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
433	 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
434	 │         on the existing site.
435	 └── NO  → continue
436	     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
437	     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
438	     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
439	     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
440	         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
441	         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
442	 ```
443	 
444	 ## Three options to present
445	 
446	 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
447	 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
448	 for an honest consent gate.
449	 
450	 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
451	 
452	 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
453	   `docs/` untouched**.
454	 - The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
455	   from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
456	   pages.)
457	 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
458	 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
459	   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
460	   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
461	 
462	 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
463	 
464	-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
465	-  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
466	-  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
467	-  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
468	+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
469	+  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
470	+  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
471	+  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
472	+  include fragments are not navigation pages.
473	 - Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
474	   deterministic alphabetical order.
475	 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
476	   content is already there.
477	 
478	 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
479	 
480	 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
481	 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
482	 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
483	   has been asked once.
484	 
485	 ## What "non-hidden files" means
486	 
487	 For the purposes of this check:
488	 
489	 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
490	 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
491	 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
492	   "no existing content".
493	 
494	 Implementation hint:
495	 
496	 ```bash
497	 find docs -type f \
498	   -not -path '*/\.*' \
499	   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
500	   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
501	   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
502	   | head -50
503	 ```
504	 
505	 ## Things this skill must NOT do
506	 
507	+- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
508	+  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
509	+  repository.
510	+- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
511	+  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
512	+  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
513	 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
514	   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
515	 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
516	   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
517	 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
518	   absolute" without an explicit ask.
519	 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
520	   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
521	   breaks rendering.
522	 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
523	   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
524	   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
525	 
526	 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
527	 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
528	 
529	 ## After bootstrap
530	 
531	 Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
532	 for option a) and report:
533	 
534	 - Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
535	 - Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
536	 - Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
537	   are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
538	 
539	 ## Recording the decision
540	 
541	 ```bash
542	 bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
543	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
544	 ```
545	 
546	 Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
547	 `wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).

855	 # --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
856	 # With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
857	 # (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
858	 # marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
859	 expand_marker() {
860	   local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
861	   [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
862	   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
863	     log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"

866	   if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
867	     [ -f "$snippet" ] || die "social snippet missing: $snippet" 4
868	     awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
869	       index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
870	       { print }
871	     ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
872	   else
873	     awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"

875	 }

263	   Material team's Zensical replacement, and the criteria for lifting the
264	   caps. Read whenever a user asks about upgrading MkDocs or why the docs
265	   build is on 1.x.
266	 
267	 ## Bundled assets
268	 
269	 Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
270	 
271	 - `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
272	   plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
273	   `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`. Carries `__SOCIAL_*__` marker lines that
274	   `init-docs-site.sh` expands (with `--social`) or deletes.
275	 - `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
276	   optional-deps group. Has a `__SOCIAL_IMAGING__` marker.
277	 - `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
278	   paths filter, uv setup, strict build, Pages deploy. Has a `__SOCIAL_CI__`
279	   marker for the Cairo/Pango + card-cache steps.
280	 - `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when
281	   `init-docs-site.sh --social` is passed: `mkdocs-plugin.yml` (the `social`
282	   plugin block), `pyproject-dep.txt` (`mkdocs-material[imaging]`), and
283	   `ci-steps.yml` (the Cairo/Pango install + `.cache/plugin/social` cache).
284	   Pre-indented for their insertion points — keep the indentation.
285	 - `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
286	   examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
287	 - `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
288	 - `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
289	   pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
290	   terminology-rule admonition.
291	 - `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
292	   `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
293	   builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
294	 
295	 ## Gotchas
296	 
297	 - **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
298	   to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
299	   no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
300	   dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
301	   it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
302	   it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
303	   `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
304	   cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
305	   `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
306	 - **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
307	   `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
308	   `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
309	   error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
310	   (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
311	   `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
312	   same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
313	   the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
314	   there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
315	   Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.

420	 # Handling existing `docs/` content
421	 
422	 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
423	 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
424	 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
425	 
426	 ## Decision tree
427	 
428	 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
429	 
430	 ```
431	 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
432	 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
433	 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
434	 │         on the existing site.
435	 └── NO  → continue
436	     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
437	     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
438	     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
439	     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
440	         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
441	         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
442	 ```
443	 
444	 ## Three options to present
445	 
446	 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
447	 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
448	 for an honest consent gate.
449	 
450	 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
451	 
452	 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
453	   `docs/` untouched**.
454	 - The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
455	   from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
456	   pages.)
457	 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
458	 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
459	   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
460	   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
461	 
462	 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
463	 
464	-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
465	-  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
466	-  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
467	-  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
468	+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
469	+  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
470	+  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
471	+  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
472	+  include fragments are not navigation pages.
473	 - Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
474	   deterministic alphabetical order.
475	 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
476	   content is already there.
477	 
478	 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
479	 
480	 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
481	 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
482	 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
483	   has been asked once.
484	 
485	 ## What "non-hidden files" means
486	 
487	 For the purposes of this check:
488	 
489	 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
490	 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
491	 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
492	   "no existing content".
493	 
494	 Implementation hint:
495	 
496	 ```bash
497	 find docs -type f \
498	   -not -path '*/\.*' \
499	   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
500	   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
501	   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
502	   | head -50
503	 ```
504	 
505	 ## Things this skill must NOT do
506	 
507	+- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
508	+  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
509	+  repository.
510	+- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
511	+  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
512	+  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
513	 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
514	   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
515	 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
516	   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
517	 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
518	   absolute" without an explicit ask.
519	 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
520	   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
521	   breaks rendering.
522	 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
523	   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
524	   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
525	 
526	 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
527	 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
528	 
529	 ## After bootstrap
530	 
531	 Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
532	 for option a) and report:
533	 
534	 - Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
535	 - Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
536	 - Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
537	   are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
538	 
539	 ## Recording the decision
540	 
541	 ```bash
542	 bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
543	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
544	 ```
545	 
546	 Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
547	 `wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).

296	 
297	 - **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
298	   to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
299	   no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
300	   dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
301	   it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
302	   it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
303	   `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
304	   cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
305	   `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
306	 - **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
307	   `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
308	   `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
309	   error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
310	   (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
311	   `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
312	   same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
313	   the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
314	   there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
315	   Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.

420	 # Handling existing `docs/` content
421	 
422	 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
423	 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
424	 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
425	 
426	 ## Decision tree
427	 
428	 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
429	 
430	 ```
431	 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
432	 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
433	 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
434	 │         on the existing site.
435	 └── NO  → continue
436	     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
437	     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
438	     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
439	     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
440	         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
441	         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
442	 ```
443	 
444	 ## Three options to present
445	 
446	 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
447	 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
448	 for an honest consent gate.
449	 
450	 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
451	 
452	 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
453	   `docs/` untouched**.
454	 - The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
455	   from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
456	   pages.)
457	 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
458	 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
459	   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
460	   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
461	 
462	 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
463	 
464	-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
465	-  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
466	-  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
467	-  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
468	+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
469	+  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
470	+  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
471	+  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
472	+  include fragments are not navigation pages.
473	 - Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
474	   deterministic alphabetical order.
475	 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
476	   content is already there.
477	 
478	 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
479	 
480	 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
481	 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
482	 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
483	   has been asked once.
484	 
485	 ## What "non-hidden files" means
486	 
487	 For the purposes of this check:
488	 
489	 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
490	 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
491	 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
492	   "no existing content".
493	 
494	 Implementation hint:
495	 
496	 ```bash
497	 find docs -type f \
498	   -not -path '*/\.*' \
499	   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
500	   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
501	   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
502	   | head -50
503	 ```
504	 
505	 ## Things this skill must NOT do
506	 
507	+- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
508	+  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
509	+  repository.
510	+- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
511	+  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
512	+  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
513	 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
514	   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
515	 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
516	   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
517	 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
518	   absolute" without an explicit ask.
519	 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
520	   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
521	   breaks rendering.
522	 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
523	   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
524	   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
525	 
526	 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
527	 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
528	 
529	 ## After bootstrap
530	 
531	 Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
532	 for option a) and report:
533	 
534	 - Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
535	 - Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
536	 - Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
537	   are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
538	 
539	 ## Recording the decision
540	 
541	 ```bash
542	 bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
543	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
544	 ```
545	 
546	 Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
547	 `wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).

855	 # --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
856	 # With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
857	 # (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
858	 # marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
859	 expand_marker() {
860	   local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
861	   [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
862	   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
863	     log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"
864	     return 0
865	   fi
866	   if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
867	     [ -f "$snippet" ] || die "social snippet missing: $snippet" 4
868	     awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
869	       index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
870	       { print }
871	     ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
872	   else
873	     awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
874	   fi
875	 }

43	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
44	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
45	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true

50	 
51	 ### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
52	 
53	 Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
54	 `references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
55	 the short version:
56	 
57	 - If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
58	   exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
59	 - If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
60	   (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
61	   with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
62	   (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
63	   explicit, alphabetical nav;
64	   (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
65	 - If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
66	 
67	 Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
68	 
69	 ### 4. Scaffold
70	 
71	 Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
72	 `pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
73	 `docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
74	 copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
75	 `.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
76	 `--social` is on.
77	 
78	 ```bash
79	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
80	   --site-name "My Project" \
81	   --repo-slug owner/repo \
82	   --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
83	 ```

86	-files unless `--force` is passed.
87	+files unless `--force` is passed, and refuses symlinks anywhere in an existing

104	 ### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
105

123	 ### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
124	 
125	 For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
126	 `mkdocs.yml`:

135	 It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
136	 nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
137	 — re-running with the same slug is a no-op.

142	 terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
143	 translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
144	 
145	 ### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
146	 
147	 The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
148	 `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
149	 This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
150	 
151	 Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
152	 "add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
153	 
154	 Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
155	 preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
156	 invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
157	 
158	 Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
159	 keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"

161	 `Makefile` for you):

165	   --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
166	 ```
167	 
168	 This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub

170	 pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
171	 `--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in

183	 ```

186	 
187	 `add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
188	 `*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
189	 pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM

191	 rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
192	 canonical).

199	 > follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
200	 > invent translations)."

206	 for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
207	 §nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
208	 user may want one without the other.

229	-  `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.
230	+- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page, update explicit nav when
231	+  present, and keep `llmstxt.sections` synchronized. With auto-navigation
232	+  (`nav` omitted), `_root` pages remain filesystem-discovered instead of
233	+  creating a partial explicit nav. A named `--section` must already exist and
234	+  is validated before any page is written. If multiple languages are
235	+  configured, also writes `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.
236	   - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--lang LANG`
237	     (single-language stub only), `--dry-run`, `--force`.
238	 - **`scripts/add-language.sh`** — Retrofit a non-default language into an
239	   existing site. Inserts `plugins.i18n`, creates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs with
240	   the terminology admonition, updates preferences, uncomments the static-i18n
241	   dep. Keeps `mkdocs-llmstxt` by default; auto-patches CI to drop `--strict`
242	   with `--drop-strict`. Idempotent.
243	   - Flags: `--lang LANG` (required), `--name NAME`, `--default-lang LANG`,
244	     `--target-dir DIR`, `--no-stubs`, `--remove-llmstxt`, `--drop-strict`,
245	     `--dry-run`, `--force`.
246	 
247	 ## Reference files
248	 
249	 - `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
250	   `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
251	   whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
252	 - `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
253	   user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
254	   step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
255	 - `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
256	   pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
257	   exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
258	 - `references/i18n-guide.md` — Bilingual / multi-language docs setup using
259	   `mkdocs-static-i18n`. Read this **before** running `add-language.sh`. Includes
260	   the verbatim "preserve English originals" terminology rule for zh-TW pages.
261	 - `references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md` — Why the stack pins `mkdocs<2` and
262	   `mkdocs-material<10`. Captures the MkDocs 2.0 plugin-removal situation,
263	   Material team's Zensical replacement, and the criteria for lifting the
264	   caps. Read whenever a user asks about upgrading MkDocs or why the docs
265	   build is on 1.x.
266	 
267	 ## Bundled assets
268	 
269	 Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
270	 
271	 - `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
272	   plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
273	   `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`. Carries `__SOCIAL_*__` marker lines that
274	   `init-docs-site.sh` expands (with `--social`) or deletes.
275	 - `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
276	   optional-deps group. Has a `__SOCIAL_IMAGING__` marker.
277	 - `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with

279	   marker for the Cairo/Pango + card-cache steps.
280	 - `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when
281	   `init-docs-site.sh --social` is passed: `mkdocs-plugin.yml` (the `social`
282	   plugin block), `pyproject-dep.txt` (`mkdocs-material[imaging]`), and
283	   `ci-steps.yml` (the Cairo/Pango install + `.cache/plugin/social` cache).
284	   Pre-indented for their insertion points — keep the indentation.
285	 - `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
286	   examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
287	 - `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
288	 - `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
289	   pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
290	   terminology-rule admonition.
291	 - `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
292	   `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
293	   builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
294	 
295	 ## Gotchas
296	 
297	 - **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
298	   to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
299	   no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
300	   dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
301	   it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
302	   it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
303	   `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
304	   cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
305	   `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
306	 - **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
307	   `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
308	   `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
309	   error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
310	   (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
311	   `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
312	   same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
313	   the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
314	   there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
315	   Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
