214	render_starter_blocks() {
215	  local file="$1" mode="$2" nav="$3" llmstxt="$4" copy_to_llm="$5" tmp rc
216	  tmp="${file}.tmp.$$"
217	  if awk -v mode="$mode" -v nav="$nav" -v llmstxt="$llmstxt" -v copy_to_llm="$copy_to_llm" '
218	    function emit(path, line) {
219	      while ((getline line < path) > 0) print line
220	      close(path)
221	    }
222	    BEGIN {
223	      block = ""
224	      nav_begin = nav_end = 0
225	      llmstxt_begin = llmstxt_end = 0
226	      copy_begin = copy_end = 0
227	      invalid = 0
228	    }
229	    /__STARTER_NAV_BEGIN__/ {
230	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
231	      nav_begin++
232	      block = "nav"
233	      if (mode == "replace") emit(nav)
234	      next
235	    }
236	    /__STARTER_NAV_END__/ {
237	      if (block != "nav") invalid = 1
238	      nav_end++
239	      block = ""
240	      next
241	    }
242	    /__STARTER_LLMSTXT_BEGIN__/ {
243	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
244	      llmstxt_begin++
245	      block = "llmstxt"
246	      if (mode == "replace") emit(llmstxt)
247	      next
248	    }
249	    /__STARTER_LLMSTXT_END__/ {
250	      if (block != "llmstxt") invalid = 1
251	      llmstxt_end++
252	      block = ""
253	      next
254	    }
255	    /__STARTER_COPY_TO_LLM_BEGIN__/ {
256	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
257	      copy_begin++
258	      block = "copy"
259	      if (mode == "replace") emit(copy_to_llm)
260	      next
261	    }
262	    /__STARTER_COPY_TO_LLM_END__/ {
263	      if (block != "copy") invalid = 1
264	      copy_end++
265	      block = ""
266	      next
267	    }
268	    block == "" || mode == "keep" { print }
269	    END {
270	      if (invalid || block != "" ||
271	          nav_begin != 1 || nav_end != 1 ||
272	          llmstxt_begin != 1 || llmstxt_end != 1 ||
273	          copy_begin != 1 || copy_end != 1) exit 2
274	    }
275	  ' "$file" > "$tmp"; then
276	    mv "$tmp" "$file"
277	  else
278	    rc=$?
279	    rm -f "$tmp"
280	    return "$rc"
281	  fi
282	}

145	# --- helper: copy template, refusing to overwrite unless --force ---
146	copy_template() {
147	  local src="$1" dst="$2"
148	  [ -f "$src" ] || die "template missing: $src" 4
149	  if [ -e "$dst" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
150	    die "exists, refusing to overwrite: $dst (use --force)" 3
151	  fi
152	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
153	    log "[dry-run] cp $src → $dst"
154	    return 0
155	  fi
156	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"
157	  cp "$src" "$dst"
158	}
159	
160	# --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
161	# With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
162	# (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
163	# marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
164	expand_marker() {
165	  local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
166	  [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
167	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
168	    log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"
169	    return 0
170	  fi
171	  if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
172	    [ -f "$snippet" ] || die "social snippet missing: $snippet" 4
173	    awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
174	      index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
175	      { print }
176	    ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
177	  else
178	    awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
179	  fi
180	}

188	      \( -type f -not -name '.DS_Store' -not -name '.gitkeep' -print \) |
189	      sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort

214	render_starter_blocks() {
215	  local file="$1" mode="$2" nav="$3" llmstxt="$4" copy_to_llm="$5" tmp rc
216	  tmp="${file}.tmp.$$"
217	  if awk -v mode="$mode" -v nav="$nav" -v llmstxt="$llmstxt" -v copy_to_llm="$copy_to_llm" '
218	    function emit(path, line) {
219	      while ((getline line < path) > 0) print line
220	      close(path)
221	    }
222	    BEGIN {
223	      block = ""
224	      nav_begin = nav_end = 0
225	      llmstxt_begin = llmstxt_end = 0
226	      copy_begin = copy_end = 0
227	      invalid = 0
228	    }
229	    /__STARTER_NAV_BEGIN__/ {
230	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
231	      nav_begin++
232	      block = "nav"
233	      if (mode == "replace") emit(nav)
234	      next
235	    }
236	    /__STARTER_NAV_END__/ {
237	      if (block != "nav") invalid = 1
238	      nav_end++
239	      block = ""
240	      next
241	    }
242	    /__STARTER_LLMSTXT_BEGIN__/ {
243	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
244	      llmstxt_begin++
245	      block = "llmstxt"
246	      if (mode == "replace") emit(llmstxt)
247	      next
248	    }
249	    /__STARTER_LLMSTXT_END__/ {
250	      if (block != "llmstxt") invalid = 1
251	      llmstxt_end++
252	      block = ""
253	      next
254	    }
255	    /__STARTER_COPY_TO_LLM_BEGIN__/ {
256	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
257	      copy_begin++
258	      block = "copy"
259	      if (mode == "replace") emit(copy_to_llm)
260	      next
261	    }
262	    /__STARTER_COPY_TO_LLM_END__/ {
263	      if (block != "copy") invalid = 1
264	      copy_end++
265	      block = ""
266	      next
267	    }
268	    block == "" || mode == "keep" { print }
269	    END {
270	      if (invalid || block != "" ||
271	          nav_begin != 1 || nav_end != 1 ||
272	          llmstxt_begin != 1 || llmstxt_end != 1 ||
273	          copy_begin != 1 || copy_end != 1) exit 2
274	    }
275	  ' "$file" > "$tmp"; then
276	    mv "$tmp" "$file"
277	  else
278	    rc=$?
279	    rm -f "$tmp"
280	    return "$rc"
281	  fi
282	}

322	    rm -f "$paths" "$nav" "$llmstxt" "$copy_to_llm"

```text
1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
36	  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
37	  pages.)
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
46	  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
47	  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
48	  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
49	  include fragments are not navigation pages.
50	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
51	  deterministic alphabetical order.
52	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
53	  content is already there.
54	
55	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
56	
57	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
58	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
59	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
60	  has been asked once.
61	
62	## What "non-hidden files" means
63	
64	For the purposes of this check:
65	
66	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
67	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
68	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
69	  "no existing content".
70	
71	Implementation hint:
72	
73	```bash
74	find docs -type f \
75	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
76	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
77	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
78	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
79	  | head -50
80	```
81	
82	## Things this skill must NOT do
83	
84	- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
85	  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
86	  repository.
87	- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
88	  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
89	  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
90	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
91	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
92	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
93	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
94	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
95	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
96	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
97	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
98	  breaks rendering.
99	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
100	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
101	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
102	
103	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
104	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
105	
106	## After bootstrap
107	
108	Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
109	for option a) and report:
110	
111	- Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
112	- Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
113	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
114	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
115	
116	## Recording the decision
117	
118	```bash
119	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
120	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
121	```
122	
123	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
124	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).
125
```
</details></tool-use>

2	name: mkdocs-site-bootstrap

Consent-gated; records repo preferences and never auto-migrates existing docs.

5	
6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
10	
11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
22	- User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
23	  applied to a new project
24	- User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
25	- User asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual",
26	  "add Traditional Chinese", "add zh-TW", "translate the docs", or to add
27	  any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7
28	
29	## When NOT to trigger
30	
31	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
32	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
33	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
34	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
35	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
36	
37	## Workflow
38	
39	### 1. Read preferences first
40	
41	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
42	decision:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
46	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
47	```
48	
49	Possible states:
50	
51	| State | Meaning | What to do |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
54	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
55	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
56	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
57	
58	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
59	
60	Ask the user explicitly:
61	
62	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
63	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
64	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
65	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
66	
67	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
68	
69	```bash
70	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
71	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
72	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
73	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
74	```
75	
76	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
77	future invocations.
78	
79	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
80	
81	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
82	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
83	the short version:
84	
85	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
86	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
87	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
88	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
89	  with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
90	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
91	  explicit, alphabetical nav;
92	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
93	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
94	
95	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
96	
97	### 4. Scaffold
98	
99	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
100	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
101	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
102	copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
103	`.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
104	`--social` is on.
105	
106	```bash
107	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
108	  --site-name "My Project" \
109	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
110	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
111	```
112	
113	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
114	files unless `--force` is passed, and refuses symlinks anywhere in an existing
115	`docs/` tree rather than risking writes outside the repository. In `skip` and
116	`wrap` modes it omits `copy-to-llm`, whose build hook writes generated assets
117	under `docs/`; users can opt into that plugin separately after choosing where

122	the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
123	
124	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
125	
126	```bash
127	uv sync --extra docs
128	uv run mkdocs build --strict
129	```
130	
131	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
132	
133	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
134	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
135	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
136	Only proceed on explicit yes.
137	
138	```bash
139	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
140	  --repo owner/repo
141	```
142	
143	Flags:
144	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
145	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
146	
147	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
148	in preferences.
149	
150	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
151	
152	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
153	`mkdocs.yml`:
154	
155	```bash
156	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
157	  --section workflows \
158	  --title "My new workflow" \
159	  --slug my-new-workflow
160	```
161	
162	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
163	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
164	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
165	
166	If the project has additional languages configured in
167	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
168	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
169	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
170	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
171	
172	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
173	
174	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
175	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
176	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
177	
178	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
179	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
180	
181	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
182	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
183	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
184	
185	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
186	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
187	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
188	`Makefile` for you):
189	
190	```bash
191	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
192	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
193	```
194	
195	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
196	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
197	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
198	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
199	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
200	is a no-op.
201	
202	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
203	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
204	
205	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
206	
207	```bash
208	uv sync --extra docs
209	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
210	```
211	
212	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
213	
214	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
215	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
216	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
217	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
218	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
219	canonical).
220	
221	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
222	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
223	
224	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
225	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
226	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
227	> invent translations)."
228	
229	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
230	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
231	
232	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
233	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
234	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
235	user may want one without the other.

319	## Gotchas
320	
321	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
322	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
323	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
324	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
325	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
326	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
327	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
328	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
329	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
330	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
331	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
332	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
333	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
334	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
335	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
336	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
337	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
338	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
339	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
340	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
341	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
342	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
343	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
344	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
345	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
346	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
347	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
348	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
349	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
350	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
351	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
352	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
353	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
354	  `select()` form.
355	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
356	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
357	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
358	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
359	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
360	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
361	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
362	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
363	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
364	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
365	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
366	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
367	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
368	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
369	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
370	  Counter-intuitive name.
371	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
372	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
373	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
374	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
375	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
376	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
377	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
378	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
379	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
380	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
381	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
382	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
383	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
384	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
385	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
386	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
387	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
388	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
389	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
390	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
391	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
392	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
393	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
394	  is just acting on it.
395	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
396	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
397	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
398	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
399	
400	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
401	
402	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
403	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
404	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
405	have customizations the templates don't know about.
406

   145	# --- helper: copy template, refusing to overwrite unless --force ---
   146	copy_template() {

   149	  if [ -e "$dst" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then

   151	  fi

   154	    return 0
   155	  fi
   156	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"
   157	  cp "$src" "$dst"

   160	# --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
   161	# With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
   162	# (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
   163	# marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
   164	expand_marker() {
   165	  local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
   166	  [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
   167	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
   168	    log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"
   169	    return 0
   170	  fi

   172	    [ -f "$snippet" ] || die "social snippet missing: $snippet" 4
   173	    awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
   174	      index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
   175	      { print }
   176	    ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
   177	  else
   178	    awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
   179	  fi
   180	}

   203	list_markdown_paths() {

   214	render_starter_blocks() {
   215	  local file="$1" mode="$2" nav="$3" llmstxt="$4" copy_to_llm="$5" tmp rc
   216	  tmp="${file}.tmp.$$"
   217	  if awk -v mode="$mode" -v nav="$nav" -v llmstxt="$llmstxt" -v copy_to_llm="$copy_to_llm" '
   218	    function emit(path, line) {
   219	      while ((getline line < path) > 0) print line
   220	      close(path)
   221	    }
   222	    BEGIN {
   223	      block = ""
   224	      nav_begin = nav_end = 0
   225	      llmstxt_begin = llmstxt_end = 0
   226	      copy_begin = copy_end = 0
   227	      invalid = 0
   228	    }
   229	    /__STARTER_NAV_BEGIN__/ {
   230	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
   231	      nav_begin++
   232	      block = "nav"
   233	      if (mode == "replace") emit(nav)
   234	      next
   235	    }
   236	    /__STARTER_NAV_END__/ {
   237	      if (block != "nav") invalid = 1
   238	      nav_end++
   239	      block = ""
   240	      next
   241	    }
   242	    /__STARTER_LLMSTXT_BEGIN__/ {
   243	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
   244	      llmstxt_begin++
   245	      block = "llmstxt"
   246	      if (mode == "replace") emit(llmstxt)
   247	      next
   248	    }
   249	    /__STARTER_LLMSTXT_END__/ {
   250	      if (block != "llmstxt") invalid = 1
   251	      llmstxt_end++
   252	      block = ""
   253	      next
   254	    }
   255	    /__STARTER_COPY_TO_LLM_BEGIN__/ {
   256	      if (block != "") invalid = 1
   257	      copy_begin++
   258	      block = "copy"
   259	      if (mode == "replace") emit(copy_to_llm)
   260	      next
   261	    }
   262	    /__STARTER_COPY_TO_LLM_END__/ {
   263	      if (block != "copy") invalid = 1
   264	      copy_end++
   265	      block = ""
   266	      next
   267	    }
   268	    block == "" || mode == "keep" { print }
   269	    END {
   270	      if (invalid || block != "" ||
   271	          nav_begin != 1 || nav_end != 1 ||
   272	          llmstxt_begin != 1 || llmstxt_end != 1 ||
   273	          copy_begin != 1 || copy_end != 1) exit 2
   274	    }
   275	  ' "$file" > "$tmp"; then
   276	    mv "$tmp" "$file"
   277	  else
   278	    rc=$?
   279	    rm -f "$tmp"
   280	    return "$rc"
   281	  fi
   282	}

17	mkdocs.yml under the matching section heading.
18	
19	Options:
20	  --section NAME      Section name (must match an existing top-level nav section
21	                      heading in mkdocs.yml, e.g. "Workflows", "Reference").
22	                      Use "_root" to add at top level (no section).
23	  --title TITLE       Display title (e.g., "My new workflow"). Required.
24	  --slug SLUG         Filename slug without .md (default: derived from --title).

30	                      If omitted, creates the default-language page plus

20	Options:
21	  --site-name NAME         Display name for the site (required).
22	  --site-description DESC  One-paragraph site description (default: derived from --site-name).
23	  --site-url URL           Public URL (e.g., https://owner.github.io/repo/) (required).

33	  --social                 Enable the Material social plugin (OG/Twitter preview
34	                           cards). Off by default: it needs system Cairo/Pango
35	                           (and mkdocs-material[imaging]), so a plain scaffold

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# add-docs-page.sh — Create a new docs/ page and insert it into mkdocs.yml nav.
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible. Requires `yq` (mikefarah/yq v4+) for nav editing.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
ASSETS="$SKILL_DIR/assets"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: add-docs-page.sh [OPTIONS]

Create docs/<section>/<slug>.md from a template and insert a nav entry into
mkdocs.yml under the matching section heading.

Options:
  --section NAME      Section name (must match an existing top-level nav section
                      heading in mkdocs.yml, e.g. "Workflows", "Reference").
                      Use "_root" to add at top level (no section).
  --title TITLE       Display title (e.g., "My new workflow"). Required.
  --slug SLUG         Filename slug without .md (default: derived from --title).
  --template PATH     Page template (default: skill's assets/page.md.template).
  --target-dir DIR    Repo root (default: walk up from CWD looking for mkdocs.yml).
  --lang LANG         Create the page only for LANG (e.g. zh-TW). Skips the
                      default-language file and the nav-insertion step
                      (mkdocs-static-i18n auto-discovers language siblings).
                      If omitted, creates the default-language page plus
                      *.<LANG>.md stubs for every non-default language listed
                      in .skills/preferences.yaml.
  --dry-run           Print actions without writing.
  --force             Overwrite existing page file.
  --help, -h          Show this help and exit.

Examples:
  add-docs-page.sh --section Workflows --title "My new workflow"
  add-docs-page.sh --section Reference --title "API schema" --slug api-schema
  add-docs-page.sh --section _root --title "About" --slug about
  add-docs-page.sh --section _root --title "About" --slug about --lang zh-TW

Exit codes:
  0  success (idempotent: re-running with same slug is a no-op)
  1  invalid arguments
  2  mkdocs.yml not found
  3  refusing to overwrite (use --force)
  4  yq error or section not found in nav
EOF
}

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

SECTION=""
TITLE=""
SLUG=""
TEMPLATE=""
TARGET=""
LANG_ONLY=""
DRY_RUN=0
FORCE=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --section)     SECTION="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --title)       TITLE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --slug)        SLUG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --template)    TEMPLATE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --target-dir)  TARGET="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --lang)        LANG_ONLY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run)     DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --force)       FORCE=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h)     usage; exit 0 ;;
    -*)            die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    *)             die "unexpected positional argument: $1" 1 ;;
  esac
done

[ -n "$SECTION" ] || die "--section is required (use _root for top-level)" 1
[ -n "$TITLE" ]   || die "--title is required" 1

command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "yq not found in PATH (install: brew install yq)" 4

# Resolve target.
if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
  cur="$(pwd)"
  while [ "$cur" != "/" ]; do
    if [ -f "$cur/mkdocs.yml" ]; then TARGET="$cur"; break; fi
    cur="$(dirname "$cur")"
  done
  [ -n "$TARGET" ] || die "could not find mkdocs.yml walking up from $(pwd)" 2
fi
[ -f "$TARGET/mkdocs.yml" ] || die "no mkdocs.yml in $TARGET" 2

# Derive slug from title if not given.
if [ -z "$SLUG" ]; then
  SLUG=$(printf '%s' "$TITLE" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -cs '[:alnum:]' '-' | sed 's/^-//; s/-$//')
fi

# Compute paths.
if [ "$SECTION" = "_root" ]; then
  REL_PATH="${SLUG}.md"
else
  # Section dir = lowercased section name (matches our convention).
  SECTION_DIR=$(printf '%s' "$SECTION" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr ' ' '-')
  REL_PATH="${SECTION_DIR}/${SLUG}.md"
fi
ABS_PATH="$TARGET/docs/$REL_PATH"

[ -n "$TEMPLATE" ] || TEMPLATE="$ASSETS/page.md.template"
[ -f "$TEMPLATE" ] || die "template not found: $TEMPLATE" 4

STUB_TEMPLATE="$ASSETS/translation-stub.md.template"
MKDOCS="$TARGET/mkdocs.yml"

# Helper: write a stub for a non-default language at <base>.<LANG>.md.
write_lang_stub() {
  local base_path="$1" lang="$2"
  local stub_path="${base_path%.md}.${lang}.md"
  if [ -e "$stub_path" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
    log "Stub already exists: $stub_path (use --force to overwrite)"
    return 0
  fi
  [ -f "$STUB_TEMPLATE" ] || die "stub template missing: $STUB_TEMPLATE" 4
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] write stub $stub_path"
    return 0
  fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$stub_path")"
  sed -e "s|{{PAGE_TITLE}}|${TITLE}|g" \
      -e "s|{{LANG}}|${lang}|g" \
      "$STUB_TEMPLATE" > "$stub_path"
  log "Created stub: $stub_path"
}

# --- --lang shortcut: only create the language stub, skip default + nav ---
if [ -n "$LANG_ONLY" ]; then
  write_lang_stub "$ABS_PATH" "$LANG_ONLY"
  printf '{"page":"%s","lang":"%s","status":"stub_created"}\n' \
    "${REL_PATH%.md}.${LANG_ONLY}.md" "$LANG_ONLY"
  exit 0
fi

# --- 1. Create the default-language page ---
if [ -e "$ABS_PATH" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
  log "Page already exists: $ABS_PATH (use --force to overwrite)"
  log "Skipping page creation; will still ensure nav entry."
else
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $(dirname "$ABS_PATH"); cp $TEMPLATE → $ABS_PATH"
  else
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ABS_PATH")"
    cp "$TEMPLATE" "$ABS_PATH"
    sed -i.bak \
      -e "s|{{PAGE_TITLE}}|${TITLE}|g" \
      "$ABS_PATH"
    rm -f "${ABS_PATH}.bak"
    log "Created: $ABS_PATH"
  fi
fi

# --- 2. Insert into mkdocs.yml nav ---

# Idempotency check: does the nav already mention this path?
if grep -qF "$REL_PATH" "$MKDOCS"; then
  log "Nav already references $REL_PATH — checking language stubs only."
  NAV_STATUS="already_exists"
else
  if [ "$SECTION" = "_root" ]; then
    EXPR=".nav += [{\"$TITLE\": \"$REL_PATH\"}]"
  else
    # Find the index of the section in nav (top-level dict whose only key is $SECTION).
    IDX=$(SEC="$SECTION" yq 'env(SEC) as $s | [.nav[] | keys | .[0]] | to_entries | map(select(.value == $s)) | .[0].key' \
      "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "null")
    if [ "$IDX" = "null" ] || [ -z "$IDX" ]; then
      EXISTING_SECTIONS=$(yq '[.nav[] | keys | .[0]] | join(",")' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
      die "section '$SECTION' not found at top of nav: in $MKDOCS (existing: $EXISTING_SECTIONS)" 4
    fi
    EXPR=".nav[$IDX].\"$SECTION\" += [{\"$TITLE\": \"$REL_PATH\"}]"
  fi
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] yq -i '$EXPR' $MKDOCS"
  else
    TMP="${MKDOCS}.tmp.$$"
    yq "$EXPR" "$MKDOCS" > "$TMP" || { rm -f "$TMP"; die "yq failed: $EXPR" 4; }
    mv "$TMP" "$MKDOCS"
    log "Updated nav in: $MKDOCS"
  fi
  NAV_STATUS="created"
fi

# --- 3. Create *.<LANG>.md stubs for every non-default language ---
# Read the languages list directly from preferences.yaml (check-preferences.sh
# --get returns nested YAML for list values, which is awkward to parse in shell).
PREFS_FILE="$TARGET/.skills/preferences.yaml"
STUBS_CREATED=0
LANGUAGES_LIST=""
if [ -f "$PREFS_FILE" ]; then
  LANGUAGES_LIST=$(yq -r '.mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages[]?' "$PREFS_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)
fi

if [ -n "$LANGUAGES_LIST" ]; then
  DEFAULT_LANG=""
  for loc in $LANGUAGES_LIST; do
    [ -z "$loc" ] && continue
    if [ -z "$DEFAULT_LANG" ]; then DEFAULT_LANG="$loc"; continue; fi
    write_lang_stub "$ABS_PATH" "$loc"
    STUBS_CREATED=$((STUBS_CREATED + 1))
  done
fi

printf '{"page":"%s","section":"%s","status":"%s","lang_stubs":%d}\n' \
  "$REL_PATH" "$SECTION" "$NAV_STATUS" "$STUBS_CREATED"

--- INIT BASE ---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# init-docs-site.sh — Scaffold a MkDocs Material docs site in the current repo.
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible. See SKILL.md for the full workflow including consent
# gates and existing-docs handling (which the agent does, not this script).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
ASSETS="$SKILL_DIR/assets"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: init-docs-site.sh [OPTIONS]

Scaffold mkdocs.yml, pyproject.toml (docs extras), .github/workflows/docs.yml,
and a starter docs/ tree in the current repo (or --target-dir).

Options:
  --site-name NAME         Display name for the site (required).
  --site-description DESC  One-paragraph site description (default: derived from --site-name).
  --site-url URL           Public URL (e.g., https://owner.github.io/repo/) (required).
  --repo-slug owner/repo   GitHub slug (required).
  --repo-name NAME         Python package-ish name for pyproject.toml (default: repo basename).
  --target-dir DIR         Repo root (default: current Git worktree root, or CWD
                           when outside Git).
  --existing skip|wrap     How to handle existing docs/ (default: skip — leave as-is,
                           omit nav for MkDocs auto-navigation).
                           wrap: add Markdown paths to nav alphabetically.
  --no-workflow            Don't create .github/workflows/docs.yml.
  --no-skeleton            Don't create the docs/ skeleton (use existing docs/ as-is).
  --social                 Enable the Material social plugin (OG/Twitter preview
                           cards). Off by default: it needs system Cairo/Pango
                           (and mkdocs-material[imaging]), so a plain scaffold
                           stays dependency-free. See SKILL.md § Social cards.
  --dry-run                Print actions without writing.
  --force                  Overwrite existing files (mkdocs.yml, pyproject.toml).
  --help, -h               Show this help and exit.

Examples:
  init-docs-site.sh \
    --site-name "My Project" \
    --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/ \
    --repo-slug owner/repo

  init-docs-site.sh --dry-run --site-name X --site-url https://x.io/ --repo-slug a/b

Exit codes:
  0  success
  1  invalid arguments
  2  target dir not found
  3  refusing to overwrite (use --force)
  4  template missing
EOF
}

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

# ensure_gitignore <pattern> <comment> — idempotently append to $TARGET/.gitignore
ensure_gitignore() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] would ensure $1 is in $TARGET/.gitignore"
  elif ! grep -qxF "$1" "$TARGET/.gitignore" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '\n# %s\n%s\n' "$2" "$1" >> "$TARGET/.gitignore"
    log "Added $1 to .gitignore ($2)."
  fi
}

SITE_NAME=""
SITE_DESC=""
SITE_URL=""
REPO_SLUG=""
REPO_NAME=""
TARGET=""
EXISTING="skip"
NO_WORKFLOW=0
NO_SKELETON=0
SOCIAL=0
DRY_RUN=0
FORCE=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --site-name)        SITE_NAME="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --site-description) SITE_DESC="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --site-url)         SITE_URL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --repo-slug)        REPO_SLUG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --repo-name)        REPO_NAME="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --target-dir)       TARGET="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --existing)         EXISTING="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --no-workflow)      NO_WORKFLOW=1; shift ;;
    --no-skeleton)      NO_SKELETON=1; shift ;;
    --social)           SOCIAL=1; shift ;;
    --dry-run)          DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --force)            FORCE=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h)          usage; exit 0 ;;
    -*)                 die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    *)                  die "unexpected positional argument: $1" 1 ;;
  esac
done

[ -n "$SITE_NAME" ] || die "--site-name is required (try --help)" 1
[ -n "$SITE_URL" ]  || die "--site-url is required" 1
[ -n "$REPO_SLUG" ] || die "--repo-slug is required (e.g. owner/repo)" 1
case "$EXISTING" in skip|wrap) ;; *) die "--existing must be 'skip' or 'wrap'" 1 ;; esac

[ -n "$SITE_DESC" ] || SITE_DESC="Documentation for $SITE_NAME"

# Resolve target dir.
if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
  if TARGET="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; then
    :
  else
    TARGET="$(pwd)"
  fi
fi
[ -d "$TARGET" ] || die "target dir not found: $TARGET" 2

[ -n "$REPO_NAME" ] || REPO_NAME="$(basename "$TARGET")"

log "Target: $TARGET"
log "Site:   $SITE_NAME @ $SITE_URL"
log "Repo:   $REPO_SLUG"
log "Social: $([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "on (OG cards; needs Cairo/Pango)" || echo "off (pass --social to enable)")"

# --- helper: substitute {{VAR}} placeholders ---
substitute() {
  local file="$1"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] would substitute placeholders in $file"
    return 0
  fi
  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|{{SITE_NAME}}|${SITE_NAME}|g" \
    -e "s|{{SITE_DESCRIPTION}}|${SITE_DESC}|g" \
    -e "s|{{SITE_URL}}|${SITE_URL}|g" \
    -e "s|{{REPO_SLUG}}|${REPO_SLUG}|g" \
    -e "s|{{REPO_NAME}}|${REPO_NAME}|g" \
    "$file"
  rm -f "${file}.bak"
}

# --- helper: copy template, refusing to overwrite unless --force ---
copy_template() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2"
  [ -f "$src" ] || die "template missing: $src" 4
  if [ -e "$dst" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
    die "exists, refusing to overwrite: $dst (use --force)" 3
  fi
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] cp $src → $dst"
    return 0
  fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"
  cp "$src" "$dst"
}

# --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
# With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
# (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
# marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
expand_marker() {
  local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
  [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
    [ -f "$snippet" ] || die "social snippet missing: $snippet" 4
    awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
      index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
      { print }
    ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
  else
    awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
  fi
}

has_existing_docs() {
  local first
  [ -d "$TARGET/docs" ] || return 1
  first="$(find "$TARGET/docs" -type f \
    -not -path '*/.*' \
    -not -name '.DS_Store' \
    -not -name '.gitkeep' \
    -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
    -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
    -print -quit)"
  [ -n "$first" ]
}

list_markdown_paths() {
  [ -d "$TARGET/docs" ] || return 0
  (
    cd "$TARGET/docs"
    find . -type f -name '*.md' \
      -not -path '*/.*' \
      -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
      -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
      -print | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort
  )
}

replace_marked_block() {
  local file="$1" begin="$2" end="$3" replacement="$4" tmp rc
  tmp="${file}.tmp.$$"
  if awk -v begin="$begin" -v end="$end" -v replacement="$replacement" '
    BEGIN { inside = 0; begin_count = 0; end_count = 0 }
    index($0, begin) {
      begin_count++
      inside = 1
      while ((getline line < replacement) > 0) print line
      close(replacement)
      next
    }
    index($0, end) { end_count++; inside = 0; next }
    !inside { print }
    END {
      if (inside || begin_count != 1 || end_count != 1) exit 2
    }
  ' "$file" > "$tmp"; then
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
  else
    rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmp"
    return "$rc"
  fi
}

strip_starter_markers() {
  local file="$1" tmp="${1}.tmp.$$" rc
  if awk '!/__STARTER_(NAV|LLMSTXT)_(BEGIN|END)__/' "$file" > "$tmp"; then
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
  else
    rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmp"
    return "$rc"
  fi
}

configure_existing_docs() {
  local file="$1" mode="$2" paths nav llmstxt path escaped rc
  paths="$(mktemp "$TARGET/.mkdocs-paths.XXXXXX")"
  nav="$(mktemp "$TARGET/.mkdocs-nav.XXXXXX")"
  llmstxt="$(mktemp "$TARGET/.mkdocs-llmstxt.XXXXXX")"

  if list_markdown_paths > "$paths"; then
    :
  else
    rc=$?
    rm -f "$paths" "$nav" "$llmstxt"
    return "$rc"
  fi

  : > "$nav"
  if [ "$mode" = "wrap" ]; then
    if [ -s "$paths" ]; then
      printf 'nav:\n' >> "$nav"
      while IFS= read -r path; do
        escaped="$(printf '%s' "$path" | sed "s/'/''/g")"
        printf "  - '%s'\n" "$escaped" >> "$nav"
      done < "$paths"
    else
      printf 'nav: []\n' >> "$nav"
    fi
  fi

  : > "$llmstxt"
  if [ -s "$paths" ]; then
    printf '      sections:\n        Guides:\n' >> "$llmstxt"
    while IFS= read -r path; do
      escaped="$(printf '%s' "$path" | sed "s/'/''/g")"
      printf "          - '%s'\n" "$escaped" >> "$llmstxt"
    done < "$paths"
  fi

  if replace_marked_block "$file" '__STARTER_NAV_BEGIN__' '__STARTER_NAV_END__' "$nav" &&
     replace_marked_block "$file" '__STARTER_LLMSTXT_BEGIN__' '__STARTER_LLMSTXT_END__' "$llmstxt"; then
    rm -f "$paths" "$nav" "$llmstxt"
  else
    rc=$?
    rm -f "$paths" "$nav" "$llmstxt"
    return "$rc"
  fi
}

HAS_EXISTING_DOCS=0
if has_existing_docs; then HAS_EXISTING_DOCS=1; fi

# --- 1. mkdocs.yml ---
copy_template "$ASSETS/mkdocs.yml.template" "$TARGET/mkdocs.yml"
substitute "$TARGET/mkdocs.yml"
expand_marker "$TARGET/mkdocs.yml" "__SOCIAL_PLUGIN__" "$ASSETS/social/mkdocs-plugin.yml"
if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
  if [ "$HAS_EXISTING_DOCS" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] would configure existing docs with --existing=$EXISTING"
  elif [ "$NO_SKELETON" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] would remove starter page references because --no-skeleton is set"
  else
    log "[dry-run] would keep starter nav and llmstxt page references"
  fi
elif [ "$HAS_EXISTING_DOCS" = "1" ]; then
  configure_existing_docs "$TARGET/mkdocs.yml" "$EXISTING" || \
    die "failed to configure existing docs in $TARGET/mkdocs.yml" 4
elif [ "$NO_SKELETON" = "1" ]; then
  configure_existing_docs "$TARGET/mkdocs.yml" skip || \
    die "failed to remove starter page references from $TARGET/mkdocs.yml" 4
else
  strip_starter_markers "$TARGET/mkdocs.yml" || \
    die "failed to finalize starter configuration in $TARGET/mkdocs.yml" 4
fi

# --- 2. pyproject.toml ---
if [ -e "$TARGET/pyproject.toml" ]; then
  log "Note: $TARGET/pyproject.toml already exists; not modifying it."
  log "      Add this to your [project.optional-dependencies]:"
  log "        docs = [\"mkdocs>=1.6\", \"mkdocs-material>=9.5\","
  if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
    log "                \"mkdocs-material[imaging]>=9.5\",  # social/OG cards"
  fi
  log "                \"mkdocs-llmstxt>=0.2\", \"mkdocs-copy-to-llm>=0.1\","
  log "                \"pymdown-extensions>=10.7\"]"
  if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
    log "      The social plugin also needs system Cairo/Pango — see the"
    log "      'social cards' step in docs-workflow.yml.template."
  fi
else
  copy_template "$ASSETS/pyproject.toml.template" "$TARGET/pyproject.toml"
  substitute "$TARGET/pyproject.toml"
  expand_marker "$TARGET/pyproject.toml" "__SOCIAL_IMAGING__" "$ASSETS/social/pyproject-dep.txt"
fi

# --- 3. .github/workflows/docs.yml ---
if [ "$NO_WORKFLOW" = "0" ]; then
  copy_template "$ASSETS/docs-workflow.yml.template" "$TARGET/.github/workflows/docs.yml"
  expand_marker "$TARGET/.github/workflows/docs.yml" "__SOCIAL_CI__" "$ASSETS/social/ci-steps.yml"
fi

# --- 3b. .gitignore: build output (always) + social plugin cache (--social) ---
# `mkdocs build` writes the rendered site to ./site/ (default site_dir) every
# run — a generated artifact that must never be committed.
ensure_gitignore '/site/' 'mkdocs build output (regenerated every build)'
if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
  ensure_gitignore '/.cache/' 'mkdocs social plugin card+font cache (regenerated every build)'
fi

# --- 4. docs/ skeleton ---
if [ "$HAS_EXISTING_DOCS" = "1" ]; then
  log "Note: docs/ already has content. Honoring --existing=$EXISTING:"
  case "$EXISTING" in
    skip)
      log "  Skipping skeleton creation (existing files left alone)."
      log "  mkdocs.yml omits nav so MkDocs auto-generates it from the filesystem."
      ;;
    wrap)
      log "  Skipping skeleton creation (existing files left alone)."
      log "  mkdocs.yml lists existing Markdown paths alphabetically."
      ;;
  esac
elif [ "$NO_SKELETON" = "1" ]; then
  log "Skipping docs skeleton and starter page references (--no-skeleton)."
elif [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
  log "[dry-run] would copy docs-skeleton/* → $TARGET/docs/"
else
  mkdir -p "$TARGET/docs/_snippets" "$TARGET/docs/assets/copy-to-llm"
  copy_template "$ASSETS/docs-skeleton/index.md" "$TARGET/docs/index.md"
  substitute "$TARGET/docs/index.md"
  copy_template "$ASSETS/docs-skeleton/getting-started.md" "$TARGET/docs/getting-started.md"
  substitute "$TARGET/docs/getting-started.md"
  copy_template "$ASSETS/docs-skeleton/_snippets/README.md" "$TARGET/docs/_snippets/README.md"
  cp "$ASSETS/docs-skeleton/assets/copy-to-llm/"* "$TARGET/docs/assets/copy-to-llm/"
fi

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
  log "Dry run complete."
  exit 0
fi

# Structured success output.
printf '{"target":"%s","site_name":"%s","site_url":"%s","social":%s,"next_steps":[' \
  "$TARGET" "$SITE_NAME" "$SITE_URL" "$([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo true || echo false)"
printf '"uv sync --extra docs",'
printf '"uv run mkdocs build --strict",'
printf '"git add and commit the new files",'
printf '"Run enable-pages.sh to deploy to GitHub Pages"]}\n'
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
8	
9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash
14	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
15	make sync
16	
17	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
18	make sync-check
19	
20	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
21	make kanban
22	
23	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
24	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
25	make marketplace
26	
27	# Exercise native Claude Code + Codex marketplace add/list/install in isolated state.
28	make native-marketplace-smoke
29	
30	# YAML-parse every skills/**/SKILL.md frontmatter. A file that fails to parse
31	# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
32	make lint-frontmatter
33	
34	# All portable publish gates at once (frontmatter + marketplace + TODO format).
35	# CI additionally runs `make native-marketplace-smoke` with pinned CLIs.
36	make validate
37	
38	# Install scripts/git-hooks/pre-push so `git push` runs `make validate` first.
39	make install-hooks
40	
41	# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
42	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
43	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
44	# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
45	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
46	
47	# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
48	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
49	  --title "Title" --description "Description"
50	
51	# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
52	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
53	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines
54	
55	# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
56	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
57	
58	# Create a new local skill
59	cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
60	
61	# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
62	uv sync --extra docs
63	make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
64	make docs-build     # produces ./site/
65	```
66	
67	## Vendor System
68	
69	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
70	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
71	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
72	
73	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
74	
75	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
76	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
77	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
78	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
79	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
80	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
81	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
82	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
83	
84	Active series in this repo:
85	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
86	
87	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
88	
89	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
90	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
91	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
92	
93	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
94	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
95	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
96	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
97	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
98	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
99	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
100	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
101	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
102	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
103	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
104	
105	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
106	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
107	
108	## Marketplace Catalog
109	
110	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
111	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
112	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
113	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
114	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
115	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
116	for the full mechanism.
117	
118	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
119	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
120	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
121	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
122	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
123	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
124	
125	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
126	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
127	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
128	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
129	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
130	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
131	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
132	within-group caveat in
133	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
134	
135	## SKILL.md Format
136	
137	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
138	
139	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
140	
141	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
142	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
143	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
144	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
145	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
146	
147	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
148	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
149	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
150	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
151	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
152	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
153	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
154	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
155	
156	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
157	
158	```bash
159	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
160	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
161	
162	# …or remove them afterward
163	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
164	```
165	
166	## Project Memory Workflow
167	
168	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
169	
170	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
171	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
172	
173	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
174	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
175	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
176	
177	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
178	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
179	
180	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
181	
182	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
183	
184	   ```bash
185	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
186	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
187	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
188	   ```
189	
190	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
191	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
192	
193	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
194	
195	   ```bash
196	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
197	   ```
198	
199	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
200	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
201	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
202	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
203	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
204	
205	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
206	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
207	   afterwards to catch drift.
208	
209	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
210	
211	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
212	
213	```bash
214	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
215	```
216	
217	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
218	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
219	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
220	
221	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
222	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
223	
224	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
225	
226	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
227	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
228	own conventions). It has four subareas:
229	
230	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
231	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
232	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
233	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
234	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
235	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
236	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
237	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
238	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
239	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
240	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
241	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
242	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
243	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
244	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
245	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
246	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
247	  status / license / last_verified`).
248	
249	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
250	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
251	
252	| Status | Meaning |
253	|---|---|
254	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
255	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
256	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
257	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
258	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
259	
260	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
261	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
262	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
263	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
264	
265	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
266	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
267	
268	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
269	
270	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
271	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
272	
273	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
274	2. The root cause
275	3. The workaround
276	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
277	
278	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
279	the explanation they do not know yet.
280
```

91	  explicit, alphabetical nav;
92	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
93	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
94	
95	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
96	
97	### 4. Scaffold
98	
99	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
100	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
101	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
102	copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
103	`.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
104	`--social` is on.
105	
106	```bash
107	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
108	  --site-name "My Project" \
109	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
110	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
111	```
112	
113	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
114	files unless `--force` is passed, and refuses symlinks anywhere in an existing
115	`docs/` tree rather than risking writes outside the repository. In `skip` and
116	`wrap` modes it omits `copy-to-llm`, whose build hook writes generated assets
117	under `docs/`; users can opt into that plugin separately after choosing where
118	those generated files belong.
119	
120	Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
121	are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
122	the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
123	
124	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
125	
126	```bash
127	uv sync --extra docs
128	uv run mkdocs build --strict
129	```
130	
131	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
132	
133	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
134	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
135	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
136	Only proceed on explicit yes.
137	
138	```bash
139	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
140	  --repo owner/repo
141	```
142	
143	Flags:
144	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
145	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
146	
147	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
148	in preferences.
149	
150	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
151	
152	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
153	`mkdocs.yml`:
154	
155	```bash
156	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
157	  --section workflows \
158	  --title "My new workflow" \
159	  --slug my-new-workflow
160	```
161	
162	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
163	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
164	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
165	
166	If the project has additional languages configured in
167	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
168	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
169	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
170	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
171

174	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the

176	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
177
