179	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
180	
181	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
182	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
183	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
184	
185	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
186	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
187	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
188	`Makefile` for you):
189	
190	```bash
191	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
192	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
193	```
194	
195	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
196	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
197	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
198	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
199	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
200	is a no-op.
201	
202	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
203	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
204	
205	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
206	
207	```bash
208	uv sync --extra docs
209	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
210	```
211	
212	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
213	
214	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
215	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
216	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
217	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
218	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
219	canonical).
220	
221	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
222	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
223	
224	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
225	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
226	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
227	> invent translations)."
228	
229	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
230	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
231	
232	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
233	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
234	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
235	user may want one without the other.
236	
237	## Available scripts
238	
239	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
240	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
241	  - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
242	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
243	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
244	  - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,
245	    `--no-workflow`, `--no-skeleton`, `--social`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
246	  - Always appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to `.gitignore`,
247	    idempotently.
248	  - `--social` opts into OG/Twitter cards: expands the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers in
249	    the templates with the blocks in `assets/social/`, and adds `/.cache/` to
250	    `.gitignore`. Off by default (keeps the scaffold Cairo/Pango-free).
251	- **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via
252	  `gh api`. Requires `gh auth status` to pass first.
253	  - Flags: `--repo OWNER/REPO`, `--no-trigger`, `--dry-run`.
254	- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page, update explicit nav when
255	  present, and keep `llmstxt.sections` synchronized. With auto-navigation
256	  (`nav` omitted), `_root` pages remain filesystem-discovered instead of
257	  creating a partial explicit nav. A named `--section` must already exist and
258	  is validated before any page is written. If multiple languages are
259	  configured, also writes `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.
260	  - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--lang LANG`
261	    (single-language stub only), `--dry-run`, `--force`.
262	- **`scripts/add-language.sh`** — Retrofit a non-default language into an
263	  existing site. Inserts `plugins.i18n`, creates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs with
264	  the terminology admonition, updates preferences, uncomments the static-i18n
265	  dep. Keeps `mkdocs-llmstxt` by default; auto-patches CI to drop `--strict`
266	  with `--drop-strict`. Idempotent.
267	  - Flags: `--lang LANG` (required), `--name NAME`, `--default-lang LANG`,
268	    `--target-dir DIR`, `--no-stubs`, `--remove-llmstxt`, `--drop-strict`,
269	    `--dry-run`, `--force`.
270	
271	## Reference files
272	
273	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
274	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
275	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
276	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
277	  user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
278	  step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
279	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
280	  pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
281	  exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
282	- `references/i18n-guide.md` — Bilingual / multi-language docs setup using
283	  `mkdocs-static-i18n`. Read this **before** running `add-language.sh`. Includes
284	  the verbatim "preserve English originals" terminology rule for zh-TW pages.
285	- `references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md` — Why the stack pins `mkdocs<2` and
286	  `mkdocs-material<10`. Captures the MkDocs 2.0 plugin-removal situation,
287	  Material team's Zensical replacement, and the criteria for lifting the
288	  caps. Read whenever a user asks about upgrading MkDocs or why the docs
289	  build is on 1.x.
290	
291	## Bundled assets
292	
293	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
294	
295	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
296	  plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
297	  `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`. Carries `__SOCIAL_*__` marker lines that
298	  `init-docs-site.sh` expands (with `--social`) or deletes.
299	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
300	  optional-deps group. Has a `__SOCIAL_IMAGING__` marker.
301	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
302	  paths filter, uv setup, strict build, Pages deploy. Has a `__SOCIAL_CI__`
303	  marker for the Cairo/Pango + card-cache steps.
304	- `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when
305	  `init-docs-site.sh --social` is passed: `mkdocs-plugin.yml` (the `social`
306	  plugin block), `pyproject-dep.txt` (`mkdocs-material[imaging]`), and
307	  `ci-steps.yml` (the Cairo/Pango install + `.cache/plugin/social` cache).
308	  Pre-indented for their insertion points — keep the indentation.
309	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
310	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
311	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
312	- `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
313	  pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
314	  terminology-rule admonition.
315	- `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
316	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
317	  builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
318	
319	## Gotchas
320	
321	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
322	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
323	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
324	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
325	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
326	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
327	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
328	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
329	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
330	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
331	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
332	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
333	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
334	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
335	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
336	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
337	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
338	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
339	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
340	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
341	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
342	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
343	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
344	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
345	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
346	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
347	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
348	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
349	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
350	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
351	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
352	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
353	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
354	  `select()` form.
355	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
356	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
357	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
358	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
359	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
360	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
361	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
362	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
363	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
364	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
365	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
366	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
367	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
368	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
369	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
370	  Counter-intuitive name.
371	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
372	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
373	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
374	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
375	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
376	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
377	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
378	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
379	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
380	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
381	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
382	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
383	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
384	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
385	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
386	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
387	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
388	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
389	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
390	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
391	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
392	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
393	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
394	  is just acting on it.
395	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
396	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
397	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
398	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
399	
400	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
401	
402	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
403	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
404	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
405	have customizations the templates don't know about.
406
```

177	## Interaction with `llmstxt` and `copy-to-llm`
178	
179	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
180	  `--strict`.** The llmstxt plugin resolves source URIs against the page
181	  index, but `reconfigure_material: true` in static-i18n remaps that index,
182	  so every entry in `llmstxt.sections` triggers `Page URI 'X' not found`
183	  warnings — which abort `--strict` builds. `sections:` is a required field
184	  on the llmstxt plugin, so you can't just empty it out.
185	
186	  **`add-language.sh` keeps `mkdocs-llmstxt` by default** because most users
187	  opted into this skill specifically to get `/llms.txt`. To make CI happy,
188	  pair the run with `--drop-strict`, which patches
189	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` to remove `--strict` from any
190	  `mkdocs build --strict` invocation:
191	
192	  ```bash
193	  bash scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
194	  ```
195	
196	  If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than lose `--strict`, flip the trade-off
197	  with `--remove-llmstxt` (the dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way, so
198	  re-adding later is one yaml edit):
199	
200	  ```bash
201	  bash scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW --remove-llmstxt
202	  ```
203	
204	- **`mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button text is English-only.** The "Copy to LLM" /
205	  "Open in ChatGPT" / "Open in Claude" labels stay in English on
206	  non-English pages. Customising them requires forking the plugin's CSS/JS —
207	  out of scope for this skill. Cosmetic only; doesn't break the build.
208	
209	- **The translation-stub admonition is zh-TW-specific.** The terminology
210	  rule it injects is written for Traditional Chinese and uses the
211	  「中文 (English original)」 format. If you add `--lang ja` or another
212	  language, the admonition still says "Terminology rule (ja pages)" but the
213	  body is in Chinese. Either edit
214	  `assets/translation-stub.md.template` to be language-neutral first, or
215	  hand-edit the stubs after creation.
216	
217	## Removing a language
218	
219	To remove `zh-TW` later:
220	
221	1. Delete the `zh-TW` entry from `plugins[].i18n.languages` in `mkdocs.yml`.
222	2. (Optional) Delete every `*.zh-TW.md` file under `docs/`.
223	3. Update `.skills/preferences.yaml`:
224	   ```bash
225	   bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
226	     --set 'mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=["en"]'
227	   ```
228	4. If you only had two languages and want to fully remove the plugin, also
229	   delete the `i18n:` block and re-comment `mkdocs-static-i18n` in
230	   `pyproject.toml`.
231	
232	## Reset path
233	
234	If you want to fully back out of all the i18n decisions and start over:
235	
236	```bash
237	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
238	# Then manually revert mkdocs.yml / pyproject.toml as above, and
239	# re-run init-docs-site.sh or add-language.sh from scratch.
240	```
241	
242	The `--reset` clears the recorded decision; the agent will re-interview on
243	the next invocation.

9	 ## Workflow

11	 ### 1. Read preferences first

26	 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
27	 | `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
28	 | `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |

30	 ### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
31	 
32	 Ask the user explicitly:
33	 
34	 1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
35	    (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
36	 2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
37	    (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
38	 
39	 Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
40	 
41	 ```bash
42	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
43	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
44	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
45	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
46	 ```
47	 
48	 If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
49	 future invocations.
50	 
51	 ### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
52	 
53	 Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
54	 `references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
55	 the short version:
56	 
57	 - If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
58	   exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
59	 - If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
60	   (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
61	   with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
62	   (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
63	   explicit, alphabetical nav;
64	   (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
65	 - If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
66	 
67	 Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
68	 
69	 ### 4. Scaffold
70	 
71	 Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
72	 `pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
73	 `docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
74	 copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
75	 `.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
76	 `--social` is on.
77	 
78	 ```bash
79	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
80	   --site-name "My Project" \
81	   --repo-slug owner/repo \
82	   --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
83	 ```
84	 
85	 Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
86	-files unless `--force` is passed.
87	+files unless `--force` is passed, and refuses symlinks anywhere in an existing
88	+`docs/` tree rather than risking writes outside the repository. In `skip` and
89	+`wrap` modes it omits `copy-to-llm`, whose build hook writes generated assets
90	+under `docs/`; users can opt into that plugin separately after choosing where
91	+those generated files belong.
92	 
93	 Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
94	 are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
95	 the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
96	 
97	 After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
98	 
99	 ```bash
100	 uv sync --extra docs
101	 uv run mkdocs build --strict
102	 ```
103	 
104	 ### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
105	 
106	 This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
107	 and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
108	 say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
109	 Only proceed on explicit yes.

111	 ```bash

113	   --repo owner/repo
114	 ```

116	 Flags:
117	 - `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
118	 - `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
119	 
120	 After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
121	 in preferences.
122	 
123	 ### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
124	 
125	 For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
126	 `mkdocs.yml`:
127	 
128	 ```bash
129	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
130	   --section workflows \
131	   --title "My new workflow" \
132	   --slug my-new-workflow
133	 ```
134	 
135	 It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
136	 nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
137	 — re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
138	 
139	 If the project has additional languages configured in
140	 `.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
141	 also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
142	 terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
143	 translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
144	 
145	 ### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
146	 
147	 The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
148	 `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
149	 This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
150	 
151	 Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
152	 "add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
153	 
154	 Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
155	 preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
156	 invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
157	 
158	 Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
159	 keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
160	 warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
161	 `Makefile` for you):
162	 
163	 ```bash
164	 bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
165	   --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
166	 ```
167	 
168	 This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
169	 siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
170	 pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
171	 `--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
172	 `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
173	 is a no-op.
174	 
175	 If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
176	 instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
177	 
178	 After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
179	 
180	 ```bash
181	 uv sync --extra docs
182	 uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
183	 ```
184	 
185	 #### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
186	 
187	 `add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
188	 `*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
189	 pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
190	 translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
191	 rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
192	 canonical).
193	 
194	 Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
195	 — do not assume. A reasonable script:
196	 
197	 > "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
198	 > 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
199	 > follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
200	 > invent translations)."
201	 
202	 Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
203	 — they're already valid pages and the build passes.
204	 
205	 When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
206	 for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
207	 §nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
208	 user may want one without the other.

290	   terminology-rule admonition.
291	 - `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
292	   `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
293	   builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
294	 
295	 ## Gotchas
296	 
297	 - **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
298	   to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
299	   no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
300	   dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
301	   it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
302	   it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
303	   `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
304	   cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
305	   `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
306	 - **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
307	   `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
308	   `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
309	   error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
310	   (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
311	   `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
312	   same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
313	   the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
314	   there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
315	   Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.

416	index 0231acb..09c4c98 100644

420	 # Handling existing `docs/` content
421	 
422	 The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
423	 content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
424	 hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
425	 
426	 ## Decision tree
427	 
428	 Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
429	 
430	 ```
431	 Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
432	 ├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
433	 │         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
434	 │         on the existing site.
435	 └── NO  → continue
436	     Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
437	     ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
438	     │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
439	     └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
440	         ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
441	         └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
442	 ```
443	 
444	 ## Three options to present
445	 
446	 When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
447	 present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
448	 for an honest consent gate.
449	 
450	 ### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
451	 
452	 - Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
453	   `docs/` untouched**.
454	 - The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
455	   from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
456	   pages.)
457	 - Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
458	 - Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
459	   rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
460	   `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
461	 
462	 ### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
463	 
464	-- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing Markdown paths into an explicit
465	-  path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them later. Paths are
466	-  relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted alphabetically under the
467	-  C locale; non-Markdown files are not navigation pages.
468	+- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
469	+  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
470	+  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
471	+  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
472	+  include fragments are not navigation pages.
473	 - Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
474	   deterministic alphabetical order.
475	 - Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
476	   content is already there.
477	 
478	 ### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
479	 
480	 - Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
481	 - Tell the user to re-run when ready.
482	 - Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
483	   has been asked once.
484	 
485	 ## What "non-hidden files" means
486	 
487	 For the purposes of this check:
488	 
489	 - Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
490	 - Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
491	 - An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
492	   "no existing content".
493	 
494	 Implementation hint:
495	 
496	 ```bash
497	 find docs -type f \
498	   -not -path '*/\.*' \
499	   -not -name '.gitkeep' \
500	   -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
501	   -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
502	   | head -50
503	 ```
504	 
505	 ## Things this skill must NOT do
506	 
507	+- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
508	+  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
509	+  repository.
510	+- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
511	+  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
512	+  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
513	 - **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
514	   `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
515	 - **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
516	   flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
517	 - **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
518	   absolute" without an explicit ask.
519	 - **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
520	   `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
521	   breaks rendering.
522	 - **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
523	   decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
524	   as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
525	 
526	 If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
527	 a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
528	 
529	 ## After bootstrap
530	 
531	 Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
532	 for option a) and report:
533	 
534	 - Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
535	 - Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
536	 - Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
537	   are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
538	 
539	 ## Recording the decision
540	 
541	 ```bash
542	 bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
543	   --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
544	 ```
545	 
546	 Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
547	 `wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).

855	 # --- helper: expand a __SOCIAL_*__ marker line ---
856	 # With --social, replace the marker line with the snippet file's contents
857	 # (snippets are pre-indented for their target). Without --social, delete the
858	 # marker line. Keeps every other line — and its comments — untouched.
859	 expand_marker() {
860	   local file="$1" marker="$2" snippet="$3"
861	   [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
862	   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
863	     log "[dry-run] expand $marker in $file ($([ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ] && echo "insert $snippet" || echo "delete marker"))"
864	     return 0
865	   fi
866	   if [ "$SOCIAL" = "1" ]; then
867	     [ -f "$snippet" ] || die "social snippet missing: $snippet" 4
868	     awk -v marker="$marker" -v repl="$snippet" '
869	       index($0, marker) { while ((getline line < repl) > 0) print line; close(repl); next }
870	       { print }
871	     ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
872	   else
873	     awk -v marker="$marker" '!index($0, marker)' "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
874	   fi
875	 }

```text
1	# yq invalid expression / wrong query result
2	
3	## Symptom
4	
5	```
6	Error: bad expression, please check expression syntax
7	error: yq failed applying: ... 3
8	```
9	
10	Or yq query silently returns `null` even though the data clearly contains the
11	match (no error, just wrong answer).
12	
13	Two common triggers:
14	
15	1. **Unquoted ISO date in `--set` value** —
16	   `bash check-preferences.sh --set foo.decided_at=2026-04-23` produces a
17	   yq expression like `.foo.decided_at = 2026-04-23`, and yq treats
18	   `2026-04-23` as the arithmetic expression `2026 - 04 - 23`, which it
19	   then chokes on. (Bare integers and `true`/`false`/`null` are fine; ISO
20	   dates and most other "looks like a literal" strings need quoting.)
21	
22	2. **`strenv(VAR)` inside a chained pipeline that yq can't bind** —
23	   `yq '.nav | to_entries | map(select(.value | type == "!!map" and (keys | .[0] == strenv(SEC))))' file`
24	   returns `null` even though `[.nav[] | keys | .[0]]` clearly contains
25	   the value of `$SEC`. `strenv(...)` reads at parse time from a yq env
26	   binding that is not always plumbed through deeply nested `select(...)`.
27	
28	## Root cause
29	
30	mikefarah/yq's expression language has two ways to read environment
31	variables:
32	
33	- `strenv(VAR)` — early-bound string lookup, sometimes does not survive
34	  through certain pipeline shapes.
35	- `env(VAR)` + `as $var` — late-bound, works inside `select(...)` and
36	  nested expressions reliably.
37	
38	For values, yq follows YAML scalar parsing rules: an unquoted token that
39	looks like a YAML scalar of any type is parsed as that type.
40	`2026-04-23` is not a YAML date in yq's expression grammar — it's a
41	subtraction. The fix is to emit it as a quoted string (`"2026-04-23"`).
42	
43	## Workaround
44	
45	**For env-var-in-query**: prefer the `env(VAR) as $var` form:
46	
47	```bash
48	SEC=Reference yq 'env(SEC) as $s |
49	  [.nav[] | keys | .[0]] | to_entries |
50	  map(select(.value == $s)) | .[0].key' mkdocs.yml
51	```
52	
53	**For unquoted-date in `--set`**: quote anything that is not a
54	bool/`null`/pure-integer:
55	
56	```bash
57	case "$v" in
58	  true|false|null) yv="$v" ;;
59	  ''|*[!0-9]*)     yv="\"${v//\"/\\\"}\"" ;;  # any non-digit → quote
60	  *)               yv="$v" ;;                  # all-digits → leave as int
61	esac
62	yq -i ".$ns.$key = $yv" "$file"
63	```
64	
65	## Prevention
66	
67	- When writing yq queries that need shell variables, default to
68	  `env(VAR) as $name` over `strenv(VAR)`. The latter is fine for
69	  top-level string substitution but failure-prone in nested selects.
70	- When writing values into yq via `--set`, never trust that the raw
71	  string will be interpreted as a YAML string. Quote everything that
72	  is not provably a number/bool/null. Test with at least one ISO date
73	  and one URL.
74	- Both `add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` in
75	  `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/` ship with the workarounds
76	  above; copy from there when writing new yq-using scripts.
77	
78	## Where this was hit
79	
80	Building `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/{add-docs-page,check-preferences}.sh`
81	during the initial scaffold (commit `a0886a5`). Both bugs were silent: the
82	add-docs-page one returned `null` and bailed with a "section not found"
83	error pointing at the wrong cause; the preferences one printed `bad
84	expression` but the date wasn't visually obviously the trigger.
85
```
</details></tool-use>

79	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
80	
81	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
82	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
83	the short version:
84	
85	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
86	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
87	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
88	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them
89	  with `nav` omitted for filesystem auto-navigation;
90	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my Markdown paths included as-is in an
91	  explicit, alphabetical nav;
92	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
93	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
94	
95	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
96	
97	### 4. Scaffold
98	
99	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
100	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
101	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
102	copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
103	`.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
104	`--social` is on.
105	
106	```bash
107	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
108	  --site-name "My Project" \
109	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
110	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
111	```
112	
113	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
114	files unless `--force` is passed, and refuses symlinks anywhere in an existing
115	`docs/` tree rather than risking writes outside the repository. In `skip` and
116	`wrap` modes it omits `copy-to-llm`, whose build hook writes generated assets
117	under `docs/`; users can opt into that plugin separately after choosing where
118	those generated files belong.
119	
120	Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
121	are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
122	the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
123	
124	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
125	
126	```bash
127	uv sync --extra docs
128	uv run mkdocs build --strict
129	```
130	
131	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
132	
133	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
134	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
135	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
136	Only proceed on explicit yes.
137	
138	```bash
139	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
140	  --repo owner/repo
141	```
142	
143	Flags:
144	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
145	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
146	
147	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
148	in preferences.
149	
150	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
151	
152	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
153	`mkdocs.yml`:
154	
155	```bash
156	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
157	  --section workflows \
158	  --title "My new workflow" \
159	  --slug my-new-workflow
160	```
161	
162	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
163	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
164	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
165	
166	If the project has additional languages configured in
167	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
168	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
169	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
170	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
171	
172	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
173	
174	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
175	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
176	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
177	
178	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
179	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
180	
181	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
182	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
183	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
184	
185	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
186	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
187	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
188	`Makefile` for you):
189	
190	```bash
191	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
192	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
193	```
194	
195	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
196	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
197	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
198	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
199	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
200	is a no-op.
201	
202	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
203	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
204	
205	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
206	
207	```bash
208	uv sync --extra docs
209	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
210	```
211	
212	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
213	
214	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
215	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
216	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
217	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
218	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
219	canonical).
220	
221	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
222	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
223	
224	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
225	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
226	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
227	> invent translations)."
228	
229	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
230	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
231	
232	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
233	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
234	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
235	user may want one without the other.
236	
237	## Available scripts
238	
239	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
240	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
241	  - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
242	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
243	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
244	  - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,
245	    `--no-workflow`, `--no-skeleton`, `--social`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
246	  - Always appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to `.gitignore`,
247	    idempotently.
248	  - `--social` opts into OG/Twitter cards: expands the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers in
249	    the templates with the blocks in `assets/social/`, and adds `/.cache/` to

251	- **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via
252	  `gh api`. Requires `gh auth status` to pass first.
253	  - Flags: `--repo OWNER/REPO`, `--no-trigger`, `--dry-run`.
254	- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page, update explicit nav when
255	  present, and keep `llmstxt.sections` synchronized. With auto-navigation
256	  (`nav` omitted), `_root` pages remain filesystem-discovered instead of
257	  creating a partial explicit nav. A named `--section` must already exist and
258	  is validated before any page is written. If multiple languages are
259	  configured, also writes `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.
260	  - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--lang LANG`
261	    (single-language stub only), `--dry-run`, `--force`.
262	- **`scripts/add-language.sh`** — Retrofit a non-default language into an
263	  existing site. Inserts `plugins.i18n`, creates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs with
264	  the terminology admonition, updates preferences, uncomments the static-i18n
265	  dep. Keeps `mkdocs-llmstxt` by default; auto-patches CI to drop `--strict`
266	  with `--drop-strict`. Idempotent.
267	  - Flags: `--lang LANG` (required), `--name NAME`, `--default-lang LANG`,
268	    `--target-dir DIR`, `--no-stubs`, `--remove-llmstxt`, `--drop-strict`,
269	    `--dry-run`, `--force`.
270	
271	## Reference files
272	
273	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
274	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
275	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
276	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling

279	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,

290	
291	## Bundled assets
292	
293	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
294	
295	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm

313	  pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim

315	- `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the

318	
319	## Gotchas
320	
321	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
322	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
323	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
324	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
325	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
326	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
327	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
328	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
329	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
330	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
331	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
332	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
333	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
334	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
335	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
336	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
337	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
338	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
339	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
340	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
341	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
342	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
343	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
344	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
345	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
346	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
347	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
348	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
349	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
350	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
351	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
352	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
353	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
354	  `select()` form.
355	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
356	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
357	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
358	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
359	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
360	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
361	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
362	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
363	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
364	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
365	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
366	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
367	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
368	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
369	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
370	  Counter-intuitive name.
371	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
372	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
373	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
374	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
375	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
376	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
377	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
378	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
379	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
380	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
381	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
382	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
383	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
384	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
385	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
386	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
387	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
388	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
389	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
390	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
391	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
392	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
393	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
394	  is just acting on it.
395	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
396	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
397	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
398	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
399	
400	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
401	
402	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
403	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
404	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
405	have customizations the templates don't know about.
406
```

```text
1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
36	  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
37	  pages.)
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
46	  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
47	  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
48	  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
49	  include fragments are not navigation pages.
50	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
51	  deterministic alphabetical order.
52	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
53	  content is already there.
54	
55	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
56	
57	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
58	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
59	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
60	  has been asked once.
61	
62	## What "non-hidden files" means
63	
64	For the purposes of this check:
65	
66	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
67	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
68	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
69	  "no existing content".
70	
71	Implementation hint:
72	
73	```bash
74	find docs -type f \
75	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
76	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
77	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
78	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
79	  | head -50
80	```
81	
82	## Things this skill must NOT do
83	
84	- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
85	  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
86	  repository.
87	- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
88	  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
89	  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
90	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
91	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
92	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
93	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
94	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
95	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
96	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
97	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
98	  breaks rendering.
99	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
100	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
101	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
102	
103	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
104	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
105	
106	## After bootstrap
107	
108	Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
109	for option a) and report:
110	
111	- Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
112	- Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
113	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
114	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
115	
116	## Recording the decision
117	
118	```bash
119	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
120	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
121	```
122	
123	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
124	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).
125

411	CLAUDE.md:7:A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
412	CLAUDE.md:9:The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).

```text
1	---
2	name: skill-author
3	description: Author a new agent skill or refactor an existing one to follow agentskills.io best practices — gotchas sections, output templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity (fragility-based), and agentic script design (--help, --dry-run, structured stdout, stderr diagnostics, PEP 723 inline deps, pinned uvx/npx versions). Use whenever the user wants to create a new skill from scratch, scaffold a SKILL.md, write a reference file, design a script meant to be invoked by an agent, lint a draft skill for quality, or convert an ad-hoc workflow into a reusable skill. For evaluating skill output quality with test cases, benchmarking, or optimizing the description trigger rate, defer to the `skill-creator` skill instead — this skill focuses on authoring, not evaluation.
4	---
5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
43	auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
44	symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.
45	
46	```bash
47	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
48	```
49	
50	Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):
51	
52	| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
55	| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
56	| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |
57	
58	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
59	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
60	
61	> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
62	> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
63	> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
64	> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
65	> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
66	> out without further prompting.
67	
68	After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
69	`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
70	follow-up actions deterministically.
71	
72	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
73	
74	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
75	that matter most:
76	
77	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
78	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
79	  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
80	  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
81	  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
82	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
83	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
84	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
85	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
86	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
87	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
88	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
89	  escape hatches.
90	
91	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
92	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
93	happens"), not just that it exists.
94	
95	### 4. Design any scripts
96	
97	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
98	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
99	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
100	requirements:
101	
102	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
103	- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
104	- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
105	- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
106	- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
107	- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
108	
109	For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
110	`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
111	have to set up an environment first.
112	
113	### 5. Lint
114	
115	Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
116	
117	```bash
118	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
119	```
120	
121	It checks three things:
122	
123	1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
124	   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
125	   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
126	2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
127	   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
128	   script).
129	3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
130	   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
131	
132	Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.
133	
134	### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator
135	
136	Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
137	quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
138	`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
139	right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
140	skill runs test cases and benchmarks."
141	
142	## Available scripts
143	
144	- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
145	  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
146	  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
147	  table in step 2.
148	  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
149	    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
150	    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
151	  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
152	    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
153	    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
154	    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
155	    symlinks).
156	- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
157	  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
158	  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
159	- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
160	  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
161	  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
162	  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
163	  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
164	  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
165	  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
166	  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
167	    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.
168	
169	## Bundled assets
170	
171	Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:
172	
173	- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
174	- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
175	- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
176	  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
177	  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
178	- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
179	  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.
180	
181	## Reference files
182	
183	- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
184	  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
185	  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
186	- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
187	  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
188	  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
189	- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
190	  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
191	  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.
192	
193	## Gotchas
194	
195	- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
196	  symlink with a real file.
197	- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
198	  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
199	  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
200	- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
201	  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
202	  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
203	- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
204	  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
205	  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
206	  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
207	- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
208	  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
209	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
210	  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
211	  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
212	  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
213	  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
214	  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
215	- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
216	  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
217	  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
218	  investing in authoring.
219	- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
220	  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
221	  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
222	  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
223	  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
224	  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
225	  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
226	- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
227	  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
228	  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
229	  if you ever hand-create one, see
230	  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).
231	
232	## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)
233	
234	Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
235	identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
236	weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
237	check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
238	quantitative validation.
239
```

```text
1	# Conventions
2	
3	These are the rules every local skill in this repo follows. They exist so
4	the package shipped via `npx skills` stays predictable and so adding a new
5	skill is mechanical, not a design exercise.
6	
7	## Local skill layout
8	
9	Each `skills/local/<skill>/` directory should contain:
10	
11	- **`SKILL.md`** — required, with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`)
12	  and a body that follows the
13	  [agentskills.io best practices](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices)
14	  (lean SKILL.md under ~500 lines, defaults over menus, procedures over
15	  declarations).
16	- **`assets/`** — templates the skill copies into a target project
17	  (e.g. `TODO.md.template`, `pitfall-doc.md.template`).
18	- **`scripts/`** — executable helpers the agent should invoke instead of
19	  re-implementing logic in chat. Bash 3.2 compatible (so they run on stock
20	  macOS without homebrew bash).
21	- **`references/`** — long-form material the agent loads on demand
22	  (decision tables, schema cheatsheets, anti-pattern lists). Push detail
23	  here rather than swelling `SKILL.md`.
24	
25	## Mirror scripts to top-level `scripts/`
26	
27	Where a skill ships scripts that this repo also wants to run directly
28	(currently only [`project-knowledge-harness`](skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)),
29	copy them into the top-level [`scripts/`](reference/scripts.md) directory
30	so `make` targets and CI can invoke them. Keep the canonical copy inside
31	the skill so the package shipped via `npx skills` stays self-contained.
32	
33	The pair must stay byte-identical. The repo doesn't (yet) enforce this in
34	CI; if you edit one, edit the other in the same commit.
35	
36	## Vendor skill layout
37	
38	`skills/vendor/<skill>/` mirrors the upstream layout exactly. Don't edit
39	vendored skills in place — modifications get overwritten by `make sync`.
40	If you need to customize a vendored skill, fork it into `skills/local/`
41	and update [`vendor.yaml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/vendor.yaml)
42	to drop the upstream entry.
43	
44	## Documentation
45	
46	Every local skill should also have a page under `docs/skills/<skill>.md`.
47	The skill's `SKILL.md` is for the agent (concise, machine-aimed); the
48	`docs/skills/<skill>.md` page is for humans deciding whether to use it.
49	Both surfaces are valuable — don't try to merge them.
50	
51	Long-form references that the agent loads on demand
52	(`skills/local/<skill>/references/*.md`) can be mirrored or summarized
53	under `docs/reference/` when the audience extends to humans browsing the
54	site, but the canonical copy still lives next to `SKILL.md`.
55	
56	## Personal scratch areas
57	
58	`Collections.md` and `notes/` at the repo root are personal scratch space
59	for the maintainer and are intentionally not part of the published docs
60	site or the agent-facing surface. Don't link into them from `SKILL.md` or
61	from any docs page.
62

1	# Script design for agent skills
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/using-scripts>. Read this
4	before adding anything to `scripts/` in a skill.
5	
6	The headline difference from "regular" CLI design: **the caller is an LLM that
7	reads your stderr to decide what to do next.** Optimize for that.
8	
9	## Table of contents
10	
11	1. [One-off commands vs bundled scripts](#one-off-commands-vs-bundled-scripts)
12	2. [Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx`](#pin-versions)
13	3. [Self-contained scripts (PEP 723 etc.)](#self-contained-scripts)
